item.title: Peak Climbing in Nepal: Tips for Beginners and Experts
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Nepal, home to 8 of the 14 highest peaks in the world, is a dream destination for mountaineers and adventure seekers. From beginner-friendly trekking peaks to challenging high-altitude climbs, the Himalayas offer experiences that test both physical endurance and mental strength. Whether it’s your first summit attempt or you are an experienced climber, careful planning, preparation, and guidance are key to a safe and memorable expedition.

Why Climb Peaks in Nepal?

Peak climbing in Nepal is more than just reaching the top—it’s about the journey through pristine landscapes, glaciers, and remote villages, and the satisfaction of achieving something extraordinary. Every climb provides panoramic views of snow-capped mountains, deep valleys, and unique Himalayan ecosystems. Beyond adventure, climbing peaks also offers an opportunity to connect with local communities and their traditions, making your journey culturally enriching as well.

Tips for Beginners

For those attempting their first peak climb, preparation is crucial:

  • Choose the Right Peak: Start with trekking peaks like Island Peak (Imja Tse), Mera Peak, or Lobuche East, which are suitable for beginners.

  • Physical Fitness: Focus on cardio, hiking, and strength training to improve stamina and endurance.

  • Acclimatization: Take rest days to adjust to altitude and reduce the risk of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS).

  • Hire Experienced Guides: Professional guides provide safety, training, and valuable local insights.

  • Gear and Equipment: Ensure you have quality climbing boots, crampons, harnesses, ropes, and warm clothing.

Tips for Experienced Climbers

Even seasoned climbers need careful planning:

  • Plan Your Route and Permits: Peaks in Nepal require government permits, which must be arranged in advance.

  • Monitor Weather and Conditions: Himalayan weather changes rapidly; check forecasts and adjust plans accordingly.

  • High-Altitude Safety: Know your limits, monitor oxygen levels, and practice safe climbing techniques.

  • Sustainable Practices: Respect the environment, minimize waste, and follow local regulations.

Responsible Peak Climbing

At Ever Peak Adventure, we emphasize responsible and ethical climbing. We encourage climbers to protect fragile ecosystems, respect local communities, and support sustainable tourism. Using trained Sherpa guides, eco-friendly equipment, and proper waste management ensures that these mountains remain pristine for future adventurers.

Conclusion

Climbing peaks in Nepal is a life-changing adventure, offering unparalleled views, personal growth, and unforgettable experiences. Whether you are a beginner taking your first steps toward the summit or an expert challenging higher peaks, Ever Peak Adventure provides professional guidance, personalized itineraries, and unwavering support to make your climb safe, responsible, and truly rewarding.

item.title: Top 5 Treks in Nepal You Must Experience
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Nepal is a trekker’s paradise, offering breathtaking landscapes, rich cultural experiences, and world-class adventure opportunities. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced trekker, these five treks showcase the very best of the Himalayas and provide memories that last a lifetime.

1. Everest Base Camp Trek

The Everest Base Camp Trek is one of the most iconic trekking routes in the world. Walk in the footsteps of legendary mountaineers, pass traditional Sherpa villages, and enjoy stunning views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, and Nuptse. The trail combines adventure, culture, and natural beauty, making it a must for any trekking enthusiast.

Highlights: Kala Patthar sunrise views, Tengboche Monastery, and Sherpa culture experiences.
Duration: 12–16 days
Difficulty: Moderate to challenging

2. Annapurna Circuit Trek

The Annapurna Circuit offers a diverse trekking experience, ranging from subtropical forests and terraced fields to alpine landscapes and snow-capped peaks. This trek is famous for its changing scenery, cultural richness, and the thrilling Thorong La Pass.

Highlights: Tilicho Lake, Manang villages, Thorong La Pass, and panoramic views of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
Duration: 14–21 days
Difficulty: Moderate to challenging

3. Langtang Valley Trek

Langtang Valley is known for its remote beauty and serenity. This trek takes you through lush forests, glacial rivers, and traditional Tamang villages. It’s less crowded than Everest or Annapurna, offering a peaceful trekking experience.

Highlights: Langtang National Park, Kyanjin Gompa, and close encounters with wildlife like red pandas and Himalayan monals.
Duration: 7–10 days
Difficulty: Moderate

4. Manaslu Circuit Trek

The Manaslu Circuit is perfect for adventure seekers looking for an off-the-beaten-path experience. This trek combines stunning landscapes with rich Tibetan culture, remote villages, and the dramatic Manaslu mountain views.

Highlights: Larkya La Pass, Samagaon village, and traditional Tibetan monasteries.
Duration: 14–21 days
Difficulty: Challenging

5. Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek

Ideal for those with limited time or seeking a shorter trek, the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek offers spectacular sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. This trek is perfect for beginners and those looking for a memorable experience without a long journey.

Highlights: Poon Hill sunrise, rhododendron forests, and Gurung village culture.
Duration: 4–6 days
Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Conclusion

Nepal’s trekking routes offer something for everyone, from iconic trails like Everest Base Camp to hidden gems like Langtang Valley. With its diverse landscapes, rich culture, and welcoming communities, trekking in Nepal is more than an adventure—it’s a life-changing experience.

At Ever Peak Adventure, we provide customized itineraries, experienced guides, and full support, ensuring your trek is safe, enjoyable, and unforgettable. Explore the Himalayas with us and create memories that last a lifetime.

item.title: Responsible Travel in Nepal: How to Make a Positive Impact
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Nepal is a land of breathtaking landscapes, rich culture, and warm communities. As tourism grows, it’s essential for travelers to practice responsible travel, ensuring that their adventures leave a positive impact on the environment, local communities, and cultural heritage. At Ever Peak Adventure, we are committed to promoting sustainable tourism that preserves Nepal’s natural beauty and traditions for future generations.

What is Responsible Travel?

Responsible travel means making choices that respect the environment, benefit local communities, and honor cultural practices. It goes beyond simply visiting a destination—it is about leaving a positive mark on the places you explore. By adopting sustainable practices, travelers can help maintain Nepal’s fragile ecosystems, support local livelihoods, and encourage ethical tourism.

How You Can Make a Difference

Here are some practical ways to practice responsible travel in Nepal:

  • Support Local Businesses: Choose locally-owned guesthouses, restaurants, and guides to directly benefit the community.

  • Minimize Environmental Impact: Reduce single-use plastics, carry reusable water bottles, and follow “Leave No Trace” principles while trekking.

  • Respect Cultural Traditions: Dress modestly, seek permission before photographing locals, and learn about local customs.

  • Responsible Trekking Practices: Stick to marked trails, avoid disturbing wildlife, and properly dispose of waste.

  • Volunteer or Give Back: Consider supporting community-based projects, schools, or conservation programs along your route.

Responsible Tourism in Action

At Ever Peak Adventure, every trip is designed with sustainability in mind. We use eco-friendly accommodations, trained local guides, and ethical trekking practices to minimize environmental impact. Our team educates travelers about local culture, wildlife, and conservation, ensuring that your journey is both enriching and responsible.

Why Responsible Travel Matters

Nepal’s natural and cultural heritage is fragile. By practicing responsible travel, you help preserve the Himalayas’ stunning landscapes, the traditions of local communities, and the biodiversity of this unique region. Small actions, like carrying out your trash or supporting a local family business, can create a meaningful difference.

Conclusion

Traveling responsibly transforms your adventure into a positive force for the environment and communities you visit. When you choose Ever Peak Adventure, you are not only exploring Nepal’s mountains and valleys—you are contributing to sustainable tourism that ensures these treasures remain for generations to come.

item.title: Bhaktapur Day Tour– 4 hours
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Bhaktapur Bhadgaon, also known as Bhaktapur, stood the capital of Nepal Valley once during the olden days. And today it is a treasure home of medieval arts and architectures. According to a legend this city was founded in 889 A.D. by late King Anand Deb who belonged to the famous Lichhabi dynasty. The whole city takes the relevant shape of a 'Khat-Kon' or David's Star. Bhaktapur signifies the "City of Devotees", with the sole majority of Hindus. The urban sector covers an area of 4 square miles. Pottery plus weaving form its traditional industries. They make the best yogurt of the kingdom; so it is known as 'juju dhou' or 'king curd.' Nowadays numerous cottage factories produce masks and wooden handicrafts as well. Bhaktapur is 13 kilometers direct east of Kathmandu and is accessible by public taxi vehicles including the bus, mini-bus, trolley-bus, cab and auto-rickshaw. Tour starts at - 9 am Tour Ends at - 3 pm Trip Duration - 6 hours

What to see in Bhaktapur

Bhaktapur Durbar Square

Bhaktapur, literally the city of Devotees', is renowned for its elegant art, fabulous culture, colorful festivals, traditional dances and the typical Newar life style. Tourists visiting Nepal feel their visit incomplete unless they get a mesmerizing glimpse of this ancient city of culture. Old dances and festival are still observed by the locals with the same fervor and enthusiasm as their ancestors did in the past. King Yarsh Mall (15th century) heavily fortified this city. The Hindus and the Buddhists have coexisted in harmony and drawn inspirations from each other through the ages. Bhaktapur is predominantly comprised of the peasantry, painting, carving, masonry, bronze casting, jewelry; pottery, etc are other traditional enterprises still existing. Monuments and artistic carvings on wood, stone and metals are strewn all over the historical core of the city. Alleys and narrow and zigzagged lanes lead you to see the Environment of Newar medieval settlements.

Datta - Traya Square

Further to the north-east of Toumadhi Square is another interesting locality called Datta-Traya Square. In fact this is the second important urban spot of Bhadgaon. The Datta-Traya Temple also built by late King Vupatindra Malla in the 17th century is a famous pagoda carrying an amusing history. This is a wooden temple facing west; it is believed that the timber used for its relevant construction was sawed out of a single tree. So you can imagine how big the tree must have been. The square has been nomenclatures from the name of the Deity itself. The three-storied temple is dedicated to the three-headed Deity of the orthodox Hindus. It symbolizes the divine triad, a mere combination of Brahma (the Creator), Bishnu (the Preserver) and Maheshwor (the Destroyer). The square as a whole can be regarded as a marvelous gallery of intricate wood carvings. One can smell environments of medieval period around the square. In the periphery of the temple, you can also see monasteries, Vimsen Temple and a platform. There are a couple of handicraft quarters around where watching the skills of the carvers is a sheer joy. The Pujari-Math Temple has the renowned Peacock Window in the lane side facing the cardinal direction of east. It is a pure wooden structure, a master-piece indeed. Apart from these, there exist two special museums-the Metal Craft Museum and the Wood Craft Museum.

Changu Narayan

It is Listed in the world cultural heritage, it is also a scenic spot situated at the altitude of about 1700, 4 km to the north of Bhaktapur. The temple is believed to be the oldest of all the temples of Nepal. It is said to have built by king Hari Datta Verma in 323 A.D. And most Authentic inscription locates in the precinct of changu Narayan is dated 464 AD. And it is accredited to the King Lichavi King Mandeva.

item.title: Chandra Giri Cable Car - 3 hours
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Trip Duration – One day (4 hours) Tour Starts at – 9 am Tour Ends at – 1 am Highlight – Soaring peaks and breath taking views of whole Kathmandu Valley and Himalayan range Chandragiri Hill, 7 km from Thankot, lies on the South-West of Kathmandu Valley and is 2551 meters from sea level. Soaring peaks and breath taking views of whole Kathmandu Valley covered with lush green blanket of flora makes Chandragiri truly a great bountiful and pristine landscape. The panoramic views of Kathmandu Valley & Himalayan ranges from Annapurna to Everest makes any one feel like seeing whole Nepal from this hill.

The Cost – 90 US$ per person

item.title: Helicopter Sightseeing
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Sightseeing by Helicopter around the Himalayas is one of the most pleasurable space journey for every visitors to get a closest, almost touching distance to the high Himalayan ranges. Helicopter tour over the Nepal Himalayas is truly awesome adventure for a lifetime filled with breathtaking scenery and glistering snow peak. Ever Peak Adventure customize Helicopter day tour as per the preferences of individual, family or friends. We have been running the Heli tour over the Himalayas covering the visit of all 8000 meter peaks.
Our most popular Heli Package in the Himalayas Everest Helicopter Tour
Tour Duration : 3 hours 30 minutes including ground time in Everest View Hotel and Lukla Minimum Group Size : 1 (Five-seated helicopter) Best time : September – December and January and June
Everest helicopter Sightseeing tour is one of the most popular Helicopter tour in the Nepal Himalayas. Our flight takes off at 7 am from Kathmandu airport. The helicopter take you over the Himalayas giving you a wonderful feeling of being close to the mountains. You will be stopping at Lukla to refuel on the way up and continue your space journey enjoying the views of the highest mountain on earth. You will land in Pheriche to get Oxygen cylinder before flying to Kalapather and Everest Base Camp. While flying you will be able to see the Mt. Everest in a closest point , spectacular mountains like Pumari, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Thamaserku, Kongde, Gaurishanker, Number and many others places like Gokyo Lake, Chukung valley… On the way back you will be stopping at Everest View Hotel (highest located star hotel) for a cup of tea or breakfast/ lunch. The total flight hour will be about three hours. You will be given extra time for breakfast, photography, viewing mountain etc.
Itinerary:
7:15 am - Fly from Pokhara airport to Annapurna Base Camp 8:10 am - Land at Lukla for fuel 8:30 am - Continue to over Himalayas 9:00 am - Land in Pheriche for oxygen cylinder 9:15 am - Continue toward EBC, Kalapathar 10:00 am - Land in Everest view Hotel for cup of tea/ breakfast 10:40 am - Fly to Kathmandu 11:40 am - Land in Kathmandu
Cost:
US$ 5000 in group of 04 pax per helicopter
Cost inclusion: Helicopter tour Airport transfer by car Airport Tax Price Excludes: National park fee US$ 32 per person Breakfast/coffee at Syangboche Annapurna Base Camp Helicopter Tour
Tour Duration : 1 hour including ground time in Annapurna Base Camp Minimum Group Size : 1 (Four-seated helicopter) Best time : September – December and January and June
Ever Peak Adventure one hour Heli tour from Pokhara to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) commences from a great scenic flight towards South of Sarangkot via Fewa Lake or North of Sarangkot and Deurali towards stunning views of world’s top Himalayan ranges such as Machhapuchhre at 6,993 meters which dominates the beautiful valley. Also you can enjoy the beauty of Annapurna South, Patal Hiunchuli, Bharha Chuli, Annapurna I, II, III & IV, Khangsar Kang, Tare Kang and Gangapurna and finally landing on the vast field at Annapurna base camp at 4,095 meters high. From there you can overlook striking views of Annapurna I, A III, A South and Huinchuli, Gangapurna, including the great North West Face of Mt. Machhapuchhre after an enjoyable stop with refreshment heading back to Pokhara. Himalayana Nomad Trek has been operating Heli tour regularly from Pokhara – Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) – Pokhara. (Normally we off the flight in monsoon time from May to September)
ABC Flight accommodates maximum 5 – 6 persons depending on the weight. The total bearable weight for the ABC flight from Pokhara is max. 470/480 kgs.
We also provide the flight on individual (per person) basis. The two way flight timing for ABC from Pokhara is max. 30-35 minutes and the ground time at ABC is max. 30 minutes.
Itinerary:
8:30 am - Fly from Pokhara airport to Annapurna Base Camp
9:00 am - Land at Annapurna Base Camp
9:30 am - Fly to Pokhara
9:15 am - Pokhara Land
Cost:
US$ 2400 in group of 4/5 pax per helicopter
Cost inclusion: Helicopter tour Airport transfer by car Airport Tax Price Exclusion: National park fee US$ 32 per person Breakfast/coffee at Syangboche Langtang Valley Helicopter Tour
Tour Duration : 1 hour including ground time in Kyangjing Gompa Minimum Group Size : 1 (Four-seated helicopter) Best time : September – December and January and June
In a few minutes of Heli tour toward the northern part of Kathmandu takes you into the high alpine country. Langtang valley is inhabited by the Shepra and Tamang ethnic group. It is completely recovered from the massive avalanche due to earthquake in April 2015. Ever Peak Adventure organize Heli tour for individuals, couples, families and groups. You will be flying above the Gosaikunda Lake and to Kyanging Gompa and surrounding Langtang Himalayan ranges. You will be rewarded by breathtaking beautiful display of Himalayas
Itinerary:
8:30 am - Fly from Kathmandu airport to Langtang Valley
9:00 am - Land at Kyangjing Gompa
10:15 am - Fly to Kathmandu
10:45 am - Land in Kathmandu
Cost:
US$ 2000 in group of 4/5 pax per helicopter
Cost inclusion: Helicopter tour Airport transfer by car Airport Tax Price Exclusion: National park fee US$ 32 per person Breakfast/coffee at Kyangjing Gompa Rara Lake Helicopter Tour (Far Western Nepal)
Tour Duration : 4 hour including ground time in Rara Lake Minimum Group Size : 1 (Four-seated helicopter) Best time : September – December and January and June
A flight to Rara Lake is one of the most incredible and fascinating flight in all the Himalayan range lie northwest of Kathmandu in the remote area of Karnali. If you are looking of wilderness and solitude journey, this flight is an ideal choice. Rara Lake is the largest lake of Nepal located in high altitude. The untouched beauty of the Rara Lake is considered as the virgin blue lake. It is so clear which mirrors the snow capped Himalayas is ringed with blue pine, black juniper forest and Himalayan cypress Lake Rara is a popular serenity pilgrimage for Nepalese.
The national Park is one of the best places in Nepal to see wildlife: musk deer, leopards, ghorals, tahr, Himalayan black beer, and the rare red panda are all native. The park is also a bird watcher's delight, especially during November and April when many species of birds visit during their seasonal migration.
Itinerary:
8:30 am - Fly from Kathmandu airport to Rara Lake
10 am - Land Rara Lake
10 to 12 pm - Spend time around Rara
2:00 pm - Land in Kathmandu
Cost:
US$ 7500 in group of 4/5 pax per helicopter
Cost inclusion: Helicopter tour Airport transfer by car Airport Tax Price Exclusion: Rara Naional park fee US$ 32 per person Breakfast/coffee at Rara Lake
In the meanwhile, should you require further information, please revert to us at your convenience. We look forward to provide you best service in the safety and comfort of our helicopter

item.title: Bardia National Park Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
A Kathmandu and Bardia Tour is a perfect combination of Nepal’s rich cultural heritage and unspoiled wilderness adventure. This unique travel experience connects the ancient temples and UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Kathmandu with the pristine jungle landscapes of Bardiya National Park, offering travelers an authentic and diverse Nepal holiday. Ideal for culture lovers, wildlife enthusiasts, photographers, and nature seekers, the Kathmandu and Bardia tour provides a balanced itinerary that showcases the spiritual heart of Nepal alongside one of the country’s best wildlife safari destinations.

The journey typically begins in Kathmandu Valley, where visitors explore centuries-old temples, royal palaces, and sacred pilgrimage sites. Highlights include the holy Pashupatinath Temple, one of the most important Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, and the magnificent Boudhanath Stupa, a spiritual center for Tibetan Buddhism. Travelers also visit the hilltop shrine of Swayambhunath, which offers panoramic views of the Kathmandu Valley, and the historic Kathmandu Durbar Square, known for its ancient palaces and intricate wood carvings. These cultural landmarks provide deep insight into Nepal’s Hindu and Buddhist traditions, vibrant festivals, and architectural brilliance.

After exploring Kathmandu’s cultural treasures, the tour continues to Bardiya National Park in western Nepal. Less crowded and more remote than other wildlife reserves, Bardiya offers a truly wild and authentic jungle safari experience. Spanning vast areas of subtropical forest, grasslands, and river systems, Bardiya National Park is home to rare and endangered species, including the Bengal tiger, one-horned rhinoceros, wild elephants, swamp deer, and Gangetic dolphins. Jeep safaris, guided jungle walks, canoe rides along the Karnali River, and bird-watching tours allow visitors to experience Nepal’s incredible biodiversity up close. Because Bardiya is less commercialized, wildlife sightings are often more intimate and rewarding, making it a top choice for serious wildlife enthusiasts and photographers.

In addition to wildlife activities, the Kathmandu and Bardiya Tour also offers cultural encounters with the indigenous Tharu community. Visitors can explore traditional Tharu villages, learn about their unique customs and lifestyle, and enjoy local cultural dance performances. This cultural interaction adds depth and authenticity to the overall travel experience.

The best time to enjoy the Kathmandu and Bardiya Tour is during autumn (September to November) and spring (March to May), when the weather is clear and ideal for sightseeing and jungle activities. Winter months also provide good wildlife viewing opportunities, especially for bird watchers.

Overall, the Kathmandu and Bardiya Tour is a perfect Nepal travel package that combines ancient heritage, spiritual exploration, and thrilling wildlife adventure. From the sacred temples of Kathmandu to the untamed jungles of Bardiya, this tour offers an unforgettable journey into the heart of Nepal’s culture and natural beauty.

item.title: Chitwan Safari Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Nepal's Southern lowland known as the Terai is covered with dense tropical jungles teeming with diverse wildlife, exotic birds and reptiles. Here you will find some of the most exciting safari destination in the world. You will be going into deep evergreen jungle on Elephant back safari to view wild animals in their natural habitat. Other thrills are canoe rides on the Jungle Rivers, nature walks, bird watching excursions village tours etc.
Chitwan National Park is Nepal's first National Park, it is located in the mid Terrai area of Nepal. Chitwan National Park is popular for jungle safari and its unique culture of Tharu community.This park is biggest attraction for many visitors after the trek and tour in Kathmandu.
Covering an area of 932 sq. km the park includes hilly areas covered by deciduous forest. This ecologically diverse area is the last remaining home in Nepal for more than 300 of the endangered Asian one-horned rhinoceros and harbors one of the largest population of the elusive and rare Royal Bengal Tiger. Beside the Rhino and Tiger, Chitwan also supports a great variety of flora and fauna. There are four species of deer, including the spotted Chital, Leopard, Sloth bear, Wild boar, rhesus monkey, Grey Langur monkey, wild dog, small wild cats, the white gaur (the world's largest wild cattle) and many other smaller animals.
The following activities can be done in Chitwan National Park:
Elephant Ride / Safari Bish Hajar Taal Trip Jungle Walk / Safari Elephant's Breeding Center Tharu Village Tour Jeep Drive / Safari Pilgrimage Trip of Chitwan Bird Watching

item.title: Astam – Dhampus Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded: The tour from Astam to Dhampus is one of the most scenic and short hike around Pokhara that provides visitors the authentic rural lifestyle of mid western Nepal near Pokhara as well as the panoramic views of the Annapurna Himalayas. Dhampus besides being very close to Pokhara still retains much of its traditional culture and appearances. Stone paved trails with the thatched roofed stone house along its both sides provide magnificent view of the typical village setup.

item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Zipline in Nepal experience by Ever Peak Adventure is available at several exciting locations in and around Kathmandu Valley, making it one of the most flexible and accessible tour packages in Nepal. Travelers can choose from multiple scenic zipline spots based on distance, views, and adventure level.

Nagarkot is one of the most popular zipline destinations near Kathmandu. Known for its sunrise views and hilltop landscapes, ziplining in Nagarkot offers breathtaking aerial scenery of forests, valleys, and nearby villages.

Ghyampe Danda is another exciting zipline location, perfect for adventure lovers who enjoy open hills and wide valley views. This area is less crowded and offers a calm yet thrilling zipline experience close to Kathmandu.

The Chandragiri Hills area provides a unique zipline experience with sweeping views of Kathmandu Valley. Located southwest of the city, Chandragiri is easily accessible and ideal for travelers looking for a short adventure combined with sightseeing.

Dhulikhel is known for its peaceful environment and scenic beauty. Zipline rides in Dhulikhel allow riders to glide over terraced fields, hills, and valleys, making it a great choice for nature lovers and photographers.

The Shivapuri foothills, near Budhanilkantha, offer a forest-based zipline experience. This location is perfect for those who want to enjoy greenery, fresh air, and a nature-focused adventure without traveling far from the city.

Pharping is another nearby destination that combines adventure with cultural surroundings. Ziplining in Pharping gives a unique experience of flying over rural landscapes and open hills in a quiet environment.

The Kakani area, located north of Kathmandu, is popular for its cool climate and panoramic views. Zipline activities in Kakani are ideal for travelers seeking a refreshing outdoor adventure in a relaxed setting.

Choose the Best Zipline Near Kathmandu

With zipline locations in Nagarkot, Ghyampe Danda, Chandragiri, Dhulikhel, Shivapuri, Pharping, and Kakani, Ever Peak Adventure offers one of the best tour packages in Kathmandu. These multiple options allow travelers to select the most suitable location based on time, budget, and scenic preference.

Whether you want a quick thrill or a scenic adventure, this tour package in Nepal delivers excitement, safety, and unforgettable memories near Kathmandu.

Tour Highlights

  • One of the best Zipline experiences in Nepal

  • Stunning views of hills, forests, and local settlements

  • Locations close to Kathmandu Valley

  • Suitable for beginners and adventure lovers

  • Managed by professional and certified staff

Safety Measures & Equipment

Safety is a top priority at Ever Peak Adventure. All zipline activities are conducted under strict safety guidelines to ensure a secure and enjoyable ride.

Safety equipment included:

  • Certified full-body safety harness

  • Protective helmet

  • Safety gloves

  • High-grade steel cable system

  • Advanced pulley and braking system

  • Backup safety lines

Safety procedures:

  • Mandatory safety briefing before the ride

  • Equipment inspection before each participant rides

  • Weight and age verification

  • Trained operators stationed at launch and landing points

  • On-site emergency support and first-aid facilities

Participants are required to strictly follow the instructions provided by the guides for their own safety.

Participant Requirements

  • Minimum age requirement as per location policy

  • Weight limits apply for safety reasons

  • Comfortable clothing and closed shoes recommended

  • No serious heart conditions or major medical issues

item.title: Chisapani / Nagarkot Hike
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Overview

The Chisapani Nagarkot Hike is one of the most popular short trekking adventures near Kathmandu. It offers an excellent combination of Himalayan scenery, peaceful forests, traditional villages, and rich cultural experiences. Therefore, it is an ideal choice for travelers who want to enjoy Nepal's natural beauty without trekking to extreme altitudes. Moreover, the trail is suitable for beginners, families, and anyone looking for a relaxing outdoor adventure.

Highlights of the Chisapani Nagarkot Hike

The Chisapani Nagarkot Hike begins with a scenic drive to Sundarijal before entering the beautiful Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park. Along the way, you walk through dense forests, cross small streams, and pass charming villages surrounded by green hills and terraced farmland. In addition, the peaceful environment allows you to enjoy nature away from the busy city.

After reaching Chisapani, the trail follows scenic ridges toward Nagarkot, one of Nepal's most famous hill stations. Furthermore, Nagarkot is well known for its spectacular sunrise and panoramic Himalayan views. On clear days, you can admire Langtang, Ganesh Himal, Gaurishankar, Dorje Lakpa, and even Mount Everest in the distance.

Why Choose the Chisapani Nagarkot Hike?

The Chisapani Nagarkot Hike offers more than beautiful landscapes. During the journey, you experience authentic village life, meet friendly local people, and enjoy traditional Nepali hospitality. Afterwards, many travelers continue to the historic city of Bhaktapur, where they can explore ancient temples, courtyards, and impressive Newari architecture. As a result, the trip combines trekking, culture, and sightseeing in one rewarding itinerary.

Because the trail is easy to moderate, it is suitable for most fitness levels. Additionally, comfortable local lodges provide cozy accommodation and traditional meals along the route. Spring and autumn are the best seasons because the weather is pleasant and the mountain views are exceptionally clear.

Overall, the Chisapani Nagarkot Hike is the perfect short escape from Kathmandu. Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or looking for a peaceful nature walk, this memorable hike offers stunning Himalayan panoramas, cultural discovery, and unforgettable experiences close to the capital.

item.title: Dhampus Hike
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Overview

The Dhampus Hike is one of the best short hiking experiences near Pokhara. It is perfect for travelers who want to enjoy Himalayan scenery, traditional villages, and Gurung culture in a short time. Moreover, the hike is easy to moderate, making it suitable for beginners, families, and nature lovers.

Scenic Beauty and Local Culture

The trail begins with a short drive from Pokhara before reaching the beautiful village of Dhampus. Along the way, you walk through forests, stone-paved paths, and peaceful farmland. In addition, you can experience the warm hospitality of the local Gurung community and explore their traditional stone houses and daily lifestyle.

Dhampus is famous for its outstanding mountain views. From the village, you can admire Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Dhaulagiri, Lamjung Himal, and several other Himalayan peaks. Furthermore, sunrise and sunset create unforgettable views over the snow-covered mountains.

Why Choose the Dhampus Hike?

The Dhampus Hike is an excellent choice if you have limited time in Nepal but still want a memorable Himalayan experience. Because the trail is well maintained, the walk is comfortable throughout the year. However, spring and autumn offer the clearest skies and the best mountain views.

During the hike, you can relax in comfortable local lodges and enjoy traditional Nepali meals. As a result, the journey combines natural beauty with authentic cultural experiences. Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or looking for a peaceful escape from the city, this hike is an ideal option.

Overall, the Dhampus Hike offers stunning mountain panoramas, rich village culture, and easy walking trails. Therefore, it remains one of the most popular short hikes in the Annapurna region.

item.title: Classic Everest Trek (Jiri -EBC)
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Classic Everest Trek from Jiri – The Pioneer Route
The Classic Everest Trek from Jiri is a historic journey to Everest Base Camp. This legendary route is the original trail followed by the first Everest pioneers before the airport in Lukla was built. Because it features uncommercialized pathways, deep valleys, and slow altitude gains, this multi-day walking expedition remains an absolute favorite for travelers looking for an authentic, deep immersion into the Solukhumbu region.
What to Expect on Your Historical Journey
Your mountain adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to the trailhead town of Jiri. From there, the footpaths wind gracefully through lush sub-tropical forests, green terraced fields, and over beautiful river suspension bridges. Along the way, staying in quiet local teahouses allows you to experience warm Nepalese hospitality firsthand while building excellent physical stamina for the higher altitude segments ahead.
Walk Through Authentic Villages to Everest Base Camp
One of the greatest highlights of the Classic Everest Trek from Jiri is walking through traditional ethnic settlements like Bhandar, Sete, and Junbesi that are completely bypassed by modern flights. You will cross the challenging Lamjura La Pass at 3,530 meters before entering the main Khumbu valley at Phakding. This gradual foot journey allows for proper acclimatization, drastically reducing the risks of altitude sickness while exposing you to ancient Buddhist monasteries.
Why Choose This Legendary Wilderness Holiday?
Opting for the Classic Everest Trek from Jiri offers the perfect mix of dramatic high-mountain landscapes, deep cultural discovery, and raw historical adventure. It serves as an ideal choice for hikers who want a classic Himalayan holiday away from the standard crowded modern routes. Ultimately, this unforgettable journey delivers incredible photography opportunities, profound peace, and memories that will last a lifetime.

Junbesi is one of the most beautiful villages on the classic Jiri route and offers a calm overnight stop.

Walk steadily, drink enough water, and take short breaks when needed.";}s:6:"item-5";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:54:"Day 6: Trek from Junbesi to Nunthala (2220m / 7283 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:422:"

Today you will continue through the classic Everest trail, passing forests, small villages, and scenic viewpoints. On a clear day, you may get your first distant view of Mt. Everest and other Himalayan peaks. The trail includes several descents and climbs before reaching Nunthala. The lower Solu region is rich in culture and natural beauty, giving you a different experience compared to the higher Khumbu region.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:" Junbesi (2,700 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Nunthala (2,220 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 17–19 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:" 6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:115:"Even though the altitude is not very high, the route has many ups and downs. Comfortable walking pace is important.";}s:6:"item-6";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:52:"Day 7: Trek from Nunthala to Bupsa (2360m / 7743 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:416:"

The trail descends towards the Dudh Koshi River and then climbs again through villages, fields, and forested paths. You will pass local settlements where you can see daily life in the lower Everest region. The route gradually becomes closer to the main Khumbu trail used by trekkers coming from Lukla. After a long day of walking with repeated climbs and descents, you will reach Bupsa for an overnight stay.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:19:" Nunthala (2,220 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:15:"Bupsa (2,360 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 16–18 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:148:"Today’s trail can feel longer because of the elevation changes. Keep your energy balanced and avoid walking too fast in the early part of the day.";}s:6:"item-7";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:52:"Day 8: Trek from Bupsa to Phakding (2610m / 8563 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:453:"

Today you will continue towards the main Everest trekking route. The trail passes through forests, ridges, small villages, and beautiful mountain landscapes. You will walk near Surke and Chheplung before joining the popular trail coming from Lukla. From there, the route continues through Sherpa villages, prayer wheels, mani walls, and suspension bridges towards Phakding. This day feels exciting as you enter the busier Everest trekking route.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:" Bupsa (2,360 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:" Phakding (2,610 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 18–20 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:" 6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:137:"The trail becomes more active after joining the Lukla route. Stay on the safe side of the trail when yaks, mules, or porters are passing.";}s:6:"item-8";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:61:"Day 9: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3440m / 11286 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:486:"

Today’s trek follows the Dudh Koshi River through pine forests, small villages, and several suspension bridges. You will pass Monjo and Jorsalle before entering Sagarmatha National Park. After crossing the famous high suspension bridge, the trail climbs steeply towards Namche Bazaar. On a clear day, you may get your first clear view of Mt. Everest during the climb. Namche Bazaar is the main trading town of the Everest region with lodges, shops, cafés, and mountain views.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Phakding (2,610 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 10–12 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:118:"This is an important altitude gain day. Walk slowly, drink enough water, and avoid rushing during the climb to Namche.";}s:6:"item-9";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:44:"Day 10: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:470:"

Today is an important rest and acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. You can take a short hike to the Everest View Hotel or nearby viewpoints for beautiful views of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other peaks. After the hike, you will return to Namche for rest. You can also explore the Sherpa culture museum, local market, bakeries, and shops. This day helps your body adjust before moving higher towards Tengboche, Dingboche, and Everest Base Camp.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:24:" Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:24:" Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:29:"Optional acclimatization hike";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:26:" 3–5 hours optional hike";s:14:"important_note";s:113:"Acclimatization means “climb high and sleep low.” A short hike is better than full-day rest inside the lodge.";}s:7:"item-10";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:63:"Day 11: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3860m / 12664 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:451:"

After breakfast, the trail follows a scenic route with excellent mountain views. You will enjoy beautiful views of Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Thamserku along the way. The trail descends to Phunki Tenga and then climbs through forested paths towards Tengboche. Tengboche is famous for its monastery, one of the most important spiritual centers in the Khumbu region. The village offers a peaceful environment and stunning mountain scenery.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:24:" Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Tengboche (3,860 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 10–12 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:110:"The final climb to Tengboche can be tiring. Take your time and visit the monastery respectfully if it is open.";}s:7:"item-11";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:59:"Day 12: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4410m / 14469 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:506:"

Today the trail descends through forests to Deboche and continues across the river before gradually climbing towards Pangboche. You will walk through beautiful Sherpa villages with views of Ama Dablam and surrounding peaks. As you move higher, the landscape becomes more open and alpine. The trail continues towards Dingboche, a beautiful high-altitude village surrounded by stone-walled fields and mountain views. Dingboche is an important stop before moving towards Lobuche and Everest Base Camp.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:20:" Tengboche (3,860 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Dingboche (4,410 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 11–12 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:138:"You will sleep above 4,000 meters today. Keep the pace slow, stay warm, and inform your guide if you notice any altitude-related symptoms.";}s:7:"item-12";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:40:"Day 13: Acclimatization Day in Dingboche";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:435:"

Today is another important acclimatization day before heading higher. You can take a short hike to Nangkartshang Hill for amazing views of Ama Dablam, Island Peak, Lhotse, Makalu, and surrounding Himalayan peaks. The hike helps your body adjust to the altitude while still returning to Dingboche for overnight rest. After returning, you can relax at the lodge, enjoy warm drinks, and prepare for the higher section of the trek.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:19:"Dingboche (4,410 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Dingboche (4,410 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:30:" Optional acclimatization hike";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:26:" 3–5 hours optional hike";s:14:"important_note";s:109:"Do not skip acclimatization at this altitude. Walk slowly during the hike and rest properly in the afternoon.";}s:7:"item-13";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:57:"Day 14: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4910m / 16109 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:445:"

After breakfast, the trail climbs gradually through open alpine landscapes towards Thukla. From Thukla, you will climb a steep section to the Everest memorial area, where monuments are built in memory of climbers who lost their lives in the mountains. After this emotional and scenic section, the trail continues towards Lobuche. The surrounding landscape becomes colder, drier, and more dramatic as you move closer to Everest Base Camp.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:19:"Dingboche (4,410 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:" Lobuche (4,910 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 10–11 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:146:"The altitude is now close to 5,000 meters. Keep your pace very slow, drink water regularly, and avoid unnecessary movement after reaching Lobuche.";}s:7:"item-14";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:79:"Day 15: Trek from Lobuche to Gorakshep and Everest Base Camp (5364m / 17598 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:439:"

Today is one of the most exciting days of the trek. You will trek from Lobuche to Gorakshep through rocky trails and glacial landscapes. After reaching Gorakshep, you will continue towards Everest Base Camp. The route follows the edge of the Khumbu Glacier with incredible mountain scenery. Reaching Everest Base Camp is a proud and memorable moment. After spending some time there, you will return to Gorakshep for overnight stay.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:" Lobuche (4,910 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Gorakshep (5,164 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:51:"Approx. 11–13 km trek including Everest Base Camp";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"7–8 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:168:"This is a long and high-altitude day. Carry warm clothes, water, snacks, sunglasses, and gloves. Walk slowly and follow your guide carefully on the rocky glacier trail.";}s:7:"item-15";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:68:"Day 16: Hike to Kala Patthar and Trek to Pheriche (4371m / 14340 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:438:"

Early in the morning, you will hike to Kala Patthar, one of the best viewpoints for close-up views of Mt. Everest, Nuptse, Pumori, and the surrounding peaks. The sunrise view from Kala Patthar is one of the highlights of the trek. After enjoying the view, you will descend back to Gorakshep for breakfast and then continue down towards Pheriche. As you descend, breathing becomes easier and the temperature feels more comfortable.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:20:" Gorakshep (5,164 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Pheriche (4,371 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 13–15 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:" 7–8 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:132:"The Kala Patthar hike is steep and very cold in the early morning. Wear warm layers and carry a headlamp if starting before sunrise.";}s:7:"item-16";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:62:"Day 17: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar (3440m / 11286 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:448:"

Today you will descend through beautiful villages, forests, and river valleys. The trail passes Pangboche and Tengboche before continuing towards Namche Bazaar. The return journey gives you another chance to enjoy the views of Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other peaks. As you return to lower altitude, the walk becomes more comfortable. After reaching Namche, you can enjoy a relaxed evening with better lodge facilities, bakeries, and shops.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Pheriche (4,371 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 18–20 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:102:"The day is mostly downhill but still long. Walk carefully, especially on stone steps and uneven paths.";}s:7:"item-17";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:58:"Day 18: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2860m / 9383 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:448:"

This is the final walking day of the Classic Everest Trek. The trail descends from Namche towards the Dudh Koshi River and continues through Monjo, Phakding, and several Sherpa villages. You will cross suspension bridges, pass prayer wheels, and enjoy the final views of the Khumbu region. After reaching Lukla, you can celebrate the successful completion of your long journey from Jiri to Everest Base Camp with your guide and porter team.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:" Lukla (2,860 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:24:" Approx. 18–20 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:" 6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:120:"Start early and walk carefully on downhill sections. Confirm the next morning’s Lukla flight schedule with your guide.";}s:7:"item-18";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:53:"Day 19: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu (1350m / 4412 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:513:"

Early in the morning, you will take a scenic flight from Lukla back to Kathmandu. The flight offers one final view of the Himalayan landscape before returning to the capital city. After arriving in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you to your hotel. The rest of the day is free for rest, hot shower, laundry, or a short walk around nearby markets. After completing the long Classic Everest Trek from Jiri to Everest Base Camp, this day gives you time to relax and enjoy the comfort of the city.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:" Lukla (2,860 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:57:"30–35 minutes flight and 30–45 minutes hotel transfer";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:26:" Flight and hotel transfer";s:14:"important_note";s:175:"Lukla flights can be delayed or cancelled due to weather. This return day should be kept flexible, and it is always better not to plan international departure on the same day.";}s:7:"item-19";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:29:"Day 20: Free Day in Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:520:"

Today is a free day in Kathmandu after returning from the trek. You can use this day for rest, shopping, souvenir buying, massage, or exploring the cultural heritage of the city. If you are interested, you can visit popular places such as Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, Swayambhunath, or Kathmandu Durbar Square. This day is also useful as a buffer day in case the Lukla flight is delayed due to weather. In the evening, you can enjoy a farewell dinner or spend your final night peacefully in Kathmandu.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:20:" Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:35:"Optional city tour / local transfer";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:31:"Free day / optional sightseeing";s:14:"important_note";s:164:"This free day is useful for both relaxation and flight safety. If the Lukla flight gets delayed, this extra day helps protect your international departure schedule.";}s:7:"item-20";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:38:"Day 21: Final Departure from Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:506:"

Your 21-day Classic Everest Trek from Jiri to Everest Base Camp comes to an end today. Depending on your international flight schedule, you may have some free time for packing, breakfast, or last-minute shopping. Our representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport for your final departure. You will leave Nepal with unforgettable memories of the classic Jiri route, Sherpa villages, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar, and the beautiful Himalayan landscapes of the Everest region.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:19:"Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:42:" Tribhuvan International Airport (1,350 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:21:"30–45 minutes drive";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:21:"Airport transfer only";s:14:"important_note";s:170:"Please keep your passport, flight ticket, and travel documents ready. For international flights, it is recommended to reach the airport at least 3 hours before departure.";}}

🎒 Backpack & Bags

  • Duffel bag (70–90L)
  • Daypack (30–40L)
  • Rain cover
  • Dry bags or waterproof liners

👕 Clothing

  • Trekking T-shirts (3–4)
  • Trekking pants (2–3 pairs)
  • Thermal base layers
  • Fleece jacket
  • Down jacket
  • Waterproof jacket & pants
  • Warm hat and sun hat
  • Gloves

👞 Footwear

  • Waterproof trekking boots
  • Camp shoes/sandals
  • Trekking socks (5–6 pairs)
  • Warm wool socks

🥾 Trekking Equipment

  • Sleeping bag (-15°C recommended)
  • Trekking poles
  • Headlamp
  • Water bottles or hydration bladder
  • Sunglasses
  • Power bank

🧴 Personal Items

  • Sunscreen
  • Lip balm
  • Personal medications
  • Basic first-aid kit
  • Toiletries
  • Wet wipes and hand sanitizer

❄️ Note: This 21-day trek involves longer walking days and a wider range of climates, from the lower hills of Jiri to the high-altitude Everest region. Warm layers, comfortable boots, and a quality sleeping bag are essential.
Experience the Classic Everest Trek from Jiri to Everest Base Camp with Sherpa villages, Kala Patthar, and stunning Himalayan views.
Classic Everest Trek from Jiri - Everpeak Adventure
Follow history on the Classic Everest Trek from Jiri. Explore the original pioneer route to Everest Base Camp through authentic villages and alpine forests.

item.title: Nepal Classic Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Experience the best of Nepal on this unforgettable 11-day Nepal Classic Tour, combining cultural heritage, natural beauty, wildlife adventures, and authentic local experiences. This journey takes you through Nepal’s most iconic destinations, offering a perfect introduction to the country’s rich traditions, breathtaking landscapes, and warm hospitality.

Begin in Kathmandu, the vibrant capital city, where you will explore ancient temples, sacred shrines, and UNESCO World Heritage Sites while witnessing centuries-old rituals and living cultural traditions. A full-day excursion to Bhaktapur Durbar Square reveals Nepal’s finest medieval architecture, traditional craftsmanship, and unique Newari culture.

Travel to Chitwan National Park for an exciting wildlife experience. Enjoy jungle activities, canoe rides, nature walks, and opportunities to spot rare wildlife including the one-horned rhinoceros and various bird species.

Continue to the beautiful lakeside city of Pokhara, surrounded by the majestic Himalayas. Explore serene Phewa Lake, stunning viewpoints, caves, waterfalls, and enjoy spectacular mountain scenery. From Pokhara, embark on a scenic 1 Night 2 Days Dhampus Hike, offering breathtaking views of the Annapurna range, charming Gurung villages, and authentic rural lifestyles.

Discover the picturesque hilltop town of Bandipur, renowned for its preserved cultural heritage, traditional architecture, and panoramic mountain views. Later, visit Nagarkot, one of Nepal’s most famous viewpoints, where you can witness unforgettable sunrise and sunset views over the Himalayan peaks.

Throughout the journey, you will immerse yourself in Nepal’s diverse cultures, ancient customs, religious ceremonies, local traditions, and daily village life, making this tour a truly enriching and memorable experience.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Explore Kathmandu’s UNESCO World Heritage Sites
  • Full-day cultural tour of Bhaktapur
  • Experience authentic Hindu and Buddhist rituals
  • Wildlife safari activities in Chitwan National Park
  • Discover the beauty of Pokhara and Phewa Lake
  • Scenic 1 Night 2 Days Dhampus Trek
  • Visit traditional Gurung villages and local communities
  • Explore the historic hill town of Bandipur
  • Enjoy Himalayan sunrise views from Nagarkot
  • Experience Nepal’s rich culture, heritage, and local lifestyle throughout the journey

a:11:{s:6:"item-0";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:28:"Day 1: Ariival at kathmandu ";s:11:"description";s:143:"Arrive in Kathmandu, receive a warm welcome, transfer to your hotel, and enjoy a relaxing introduction to Nepal's vibrant culture and heritage.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:1126:"

Welcome to Nepal. Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, our representative will warmly greet you and transfer you to your hotel. After check-in, take some time to rest and recover from your journey.

Depending on your arrival time, you may explore the lively streets of Kathmandu, visit nearby local markets, or enjoy a leisurely walk around the bustling Thamel area. This is a great opportunity to experience the unique blend of ancient traditions and modern city life that makes Kathmandu so fascinating.

In the evening, attend a short tour briefing where your guide will provide an overview of the Nepal Classic Tour, including important travel information, destinations, accommodations, and activities planned for the coming days. You will also have the opportunity to ask questions and make final preparations for your adventure.

Later, enjoy a traditional Nepali welcome dinner featuring authentic local cuisine and cultural hospitality.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:42:"Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:9:"Kathmandu";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:21:"Airport transfer only";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:50:"Approximately 30–45 minutes depending on traffic";s:14:"important_note";s:282:"Please ensure your passport, travel insurance, and other necessary travel documents are readily available. Airport transfers are included, and our representative will be waiting for you outside the arrival terminal with a name board. Early check-in is subject to hotel availability.";}s:6:"item-1";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:37:"Day 2: Kathmandu Heritage Sightseeing";s:11:"description";s:156:"Explore Kathmandu's most sacred temples, ancient palaces, and UNESCO World Heritage Sites while experiencing Nepal's rich cultural and religious traditions.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:581:"

After breakfast, begin a guided heritage tour of Kathmandu Valley. Visit the sacred Pashupatinath Temple, one of the most important Hindu pilgrimage sites in Nepal, and explore the magnificent Boudhanath Stupa, a major center of Tibetan Buddhism. Continue to Swayambhunath Stupa, popularly known as the Monkey Temple, offering panoramic views of Kathmandu Valley. Later, visit the historic Kathmandu Durbar Square, home to ancient temples, palaces, and living cultural traditions. After a full day of sightseeing and cultural exploration, return to your hotel in Kathmandu.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:9:"Kathmandu";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:9:"Kathmandu";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:44:"Approximately 25 km / 16 miles (sightseeing)";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:25:"Approximately 7–8 hours";s:14:"important_note";s:171:"Modest clothing is recommended when visiting religious sites. Comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen, and a camera are highly recommended for today's sightseeing activities.";}s:6:"item-2";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:37:"Day 3: Drive to Chitwan National Park";s:11:"description";s:166:"Journey from the hills of Kathmandu to the subtropical plains of Chitwan and experience the unique culture and natural beauty of Nepal's premier wildlife destination.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:571:"

After breakfast, leave Kathmandu and enjoy a scenic drive to Chitwan National Park, passing through picturesque landscapes, rivers, terraced farmlands, and traditional villages. Upon arrival, check in to your jungle resort and relax amidst the peaceful surroundings. In the late afternoon, take a guided walk through a traditional Tharu village to learn about the culture, lifestyle, and customs of the indigenous Tharu community. End the day with a beautiful sunset view along the Rapti River followed by a cultural dance performance showcasing local traditions.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:9:"Kathmandu";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:21:"Chitwan National Park";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:32:"Approximately 170 km / 106 miles";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:31:"Approximately 5–6 hours drive";s:14:"important_note";s:171:"Chitwan has a warmer and more humid climate than Kathmandu. Lightweight clothing, sunscreen, insect repellent, and comfortable walking shoes are recommended for your stay.";}s:6:"item-3";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:32:"Day 4: Chitwan Jungle Activities";s:11:"description";s:149:"Experience the rich wildlife and natural beauty of Chitwan National Park through exciting jungle activities and unforgettable encounters with nature.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:545:"

After breakfast, embark on a full day of jungle activities in and around Chitwan National Park. Begin with a peaceful canoe ride along the Rapti River, where you may spot crocodiles and various bird species. Continue with a guided nature walk and wildlife exploration before heading on an exciting jeep safari through the national park. Keep an eye out for rare wildlife, including the one-horned rhinoceros, deer, monkeys, and numerous bird species. In the evening, return to your resort and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere of the jungle.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:21:"Chitwan National Park";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:21:"Chitwan National Park";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:39:"Activities within Chitwan National Park";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:47:"Full Day Activities (Approximately 6–8 hours)";s:14:"important_note";s:222:"Wildlife sightings depend on weather conditions and animal movement. Wear comfortable clothing in natural colors, carry sunscreen and insect repellent, and follow your guide's instructions throughout all jungle activities.";}s:6:"item-4";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:23:"Day 5: Drive to Pokhara";s:11:"description";s:132:"Travel to the beautiful lakeside city of Pokhara, renowned for its tranquil atmosphere, stunning mountain views, and natural beauty.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:453:"

After breakfast, depart Chitwan and enjoy a scenic drive to Pokhara through rolling hills, rivers, and charming rural landscapes. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and take some time to relax. In the evening, enjoy a leisurely walk along the shores of Phewa Lake, the centerpiece of Pokhara. You may also explore the vibrant Lakeside area, known for its cafés, shops, and stunning views of the Annapurna mountain range reflected on the lake.

item.title: Bhutan Cultural & Scenic Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Experience the beauty, culture and peaceful Himalayan atmosphere of Bhutan on this carefully designed 7-day tour from Nepal. With six nights in Bhutan, this journey combines the country’s most important cultural landmarks with beautiful mountain scenery, traditional villages and the unforgettable Tiger’s Nest Monastery.

The adventure begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Paro, where Bhutan’s spectacular Himalayan landscape welcomes you. After meeting your local guide, drive through the beautiful Paro Valley toward Thimphu, Bhutan’s capital. The journey itself is part of the experience, with green hills, traditional houses, prayer flags and dramatic mountain scenery along the road.

Spend two nights in Thimphu exploring the capital and experiencing Bhutanese culture. Visit the impressive Buddha Dordenma Statue, National Memorial Chorten, Tashichho Dzong and local handicraft areas. You will also have time to walk around the town and experience the relaxed lifestyle of the Bhutanese people.

The journey then continues to Punakha through the spectacular Dochula Pass. On clear days, the pass provides beautiful views of the snow-covered Himalayan peaks. In Punakha, visit the magnificent Punakha Dzong, one of Bhutan’s most beautiful and historically important fortresses, dramatically situated between two rivers.

From Punakha, continue to the peaceful Gangtey Valley. Surrounded by forests and wide open landscapes, Gangtey provides a wonderful opportunity to experience Bhutan away from busy tourist areas. Visit Gangtey Monastery and enjoy a gentle walk through the valley and surrounding villages.

The final part of the journey takes you back to Paro, where you will spend two nights. The highlight is a hike to the world-famous Taktsang Monastery, better known as Tiger’s Nest. Built dramatically on a cliffside above Paro Valley, this sacred monastery is one of Bhutan’s most iconic destinations. The hike takes several hours and rewards you with beautiful mountain views and an unforgettable cultural experience.

Your final evening in Paro is relaxed, giving you time to explore the town, shop for traditional handicrafts or enjoy the peaceful surroundings before your flight back to Kathmandu the following day.

This 6-night, 7-day Bhutan tour is an excellent choice for travelers who want to experience Bhutan’s culture, Buddhist heritage, Himalayan scenery and traditional way of life in a comfortable and well-balanced itinerary.

item.title: Mount Kailash & Manasarovar Yatra – 13 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Mount Kailash & Manasarovar Yatra is one of the most sacred spiritual journeys in the world, located in the remote western region of Tibet. Revered by Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and Bon followers, Mount Kailash is believed to be the abode of Lord Shiva.

This pilgrimage includes a holy visit to Lake Manasarovar and a challenging yet rewarding circumambulation (Kora) of Mount Kailash. The journey offers a powerful combination of spiritual fulfillment, cultural exploration, and high-altitude adventure across the Tibetan Plateau.

item.title: Kathmandu Valley Cultural Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Kathmandu Valley Cultural Tour is a fascinating journey through the cultural, historical, and spiritual heritage of Nepal. This tour explores the three ancient cities of Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, and Patan—each known for its unique architecture, temples, and traditions.

You will visit UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including sacred temples, stupas, and royal palaces. The tour offers a perfect blend of history, art, culture, and local lifestyle, making it ideal for travelers who want to experience Nepal beyond trekking. With expert guides, comfortable transportation, and well-planned sightseeing, this tour delivers a memorable cultural experience.

item.title: Pokhara City & Nature Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Pokhara City & Nature Tour is a relaxing and scenic journey into Nepal’s most beautiful lakeside city, Pokhara. Surrounded by the Annapurna mountain range, Pokhara offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, adventure, and cultural experiences.

This tour includes visits to serene lakes, caves, waterfalls, and stunning viewpoints like Sarangkot. Travelers can enjoy breathtaking views of Machhapuchhre, Annapurna, and Dhaulagiri ranges. Ideal for all age groups, this tour is perfect for relaxation, photography, and short holiday escapes.

item.title: Nepal Heritage & Wildlife Safari Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded: Overview Embark on an unforgettable journey through Nepal's rich cultural heritage and remarkable wildlife habitats with this Heritage and Wildlife Safari Tour. Combining ancient cities, UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and two of Nepal's most celebrated national parks, this tour offers the perfect blend of culture, nature, and adventure. Begin your experience in Kathmandu, the historic capital of Nepal, where centuries-old temples, sacred shrines, and vibrant local traditions provide a fascinating introduction to the country's cultural heritage. Explore iconic landmarks and immerse yourself in the unique atmosphere of the Kathmandu Valley before heading into Nepal's southern lowlands. Continue to Chitwan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its diverse wildlife and subtropical jungle landscapes. Enjoy exciting jungle activities including jeep safaris, canoe rides, nature walks, and opportunities to spot the endangered one-horned rhinoceros, crocodiles, deer, and numerous bird species. The adventure then takes you to Bardiya National Park, Nepal's most pristine national park. Less crowded and more remote than Chitwan, Bardiya offers exceptional wildlife experiences and some of the best opportunities in Nepal to encounter Bengal tigers, wild elephants, rhinoceroses, and a wide variety of birds in their natural habitat. Explore dense forests, river ecosystems, and traditional Tharu communities while enjoying authentic wilderness experiences. Conclude your journey with a final night in Kathmandu, allowing time for relaxation, last-minute shopping, or further exploration before your departure. This carefully designed itinerary offers an enriching combination of Nepal's cultural treasures and extraordinary wildlife, making it ideal for travelers seeking both heritage discovery and safari adventure.

  • Visit UNESCO World Heritage Sites and ancient heritage monuments.
  • Enjoy thrilling jungle safaris in Chitwan National Park.

  • Experience authentic Tharu culture and traditions.
  • Discover the pristine wilderness of Bardiya National Park.
  • Search for the elusive Royal Bengal Tiger and other wildlife.
  • Enjoy guided nature walks, jeep safaris, and bird-watching activities.

item.title: Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan Golden Triangle Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan Golden Triangle Tour is Nepal’s most popular multi-destination travel package, offering a perfect blend of culture, nature, and wildlife. This journey covers the historical heritage of Kathmandu, the scenic beauty of Pokhara, and the rich biodiversity of Chitwan National Park.

This tour is ideal for first-time visitors who want to experience Nepal’s diversity in a short time—UNESCO heritage sites, Himalayan views, peaceful lakes, and thrilling jungle safaris. With comfortable accommodation, guided tours, and smooth transportation, it delivers a complete Nepal holiday experience.

item.title: Everest Mountain Flight Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Everest Mountain Flight Tour is a once-in-a-lifetime aerial experience that offers breathtaking views of the Himalayan range, including the world’s highest peak, Mount Everest. This short yet spectacular flight departs from Kathmandu and takes you close to the majestic peaks of the Everest region.

Ideal for travelers with limited time or those who prefer a comfortable alternative to trekking, this tour provides panoramic views of snow-capped mountains, glaciers, and valleys from the comfort of a window seat. It is one of the most popular luxury experiences in Nepal.

item.title: Annapurna Region Sightseeing Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Annapurna Region Sightseeing Tour is a perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural exploration, and Himalayan views without the need for long trekking. Centered around the beautiful city of Pokhara, this tour offers breathtaking panoramas of the Annapurna mountain range, peaceful lakes, traditional villages, and scenic viewpoints.

Travelers will explore iconic destinations such as Sarangkot for sunrise views, Phewa Lake for boating, and nearby cultural villages like Ghandruk. This tour is ideal for those seeking a relaxed Himalayan experience with light walking and comfortable accommodation.

item.title: Bhutan Spiritual & Meditation Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Bhutan Spiritual & Meditation Tour is a transformative journey designed for travelers seeking inner peace, mindfulness, and spiritual awakening in the serene Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan. Known as the last Buddhist kingdom, Bhutan offers a deeply spiritual environment filled with monasteries, temples, prayer flags, and meditation caves.

This tour takes you through sacred destinations like Paro, Thimphu, and Punakha, where you will meditate in ancient monasteries, interact with monks, and experience Bhutan’s rich Buddhist philosophy. Meditation sessions in peaceful natural settings and holy sites provide a unique opportunity for self-reflection and mental relaxation.

  • Visit iconic Tiger’s Nest Monastery
  • Spiritual teachings and interaction with Buddhist monks
  • Visit Dochula Pass with 108 stupas
  • Explore peaceful valleys like Phobjikha
  • Experience Bhutanese spiritual lifestyle and rituals
  • Yoga, mindfulness & self-reflection practices
  • Visit ancient temples and dzongs

item.title: Bhutan Honeymoon Tour

The Bhutan Honeymoon Tour is a romantic and peaceful getaway designed for couples seeking privacy, natural beauty, and cultural charm in the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan. Known for its serene landscapes, spiritual ambiance, and warm hospitality, Bhutan offers a perfect setting for unforgettable honeymoon memories.

item.title: Bhutan Adventure Tour
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Bhutan Adventure Tour is an exciting blend of hiking, nature exploration, and cultural discovery in the pristine Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan. This tour is perfect for travelers who want light adventure without extreme trekking, combining scenic hikes, mountain views, and visits to ancient monasteries.

You will explore the valleys of Paro, the capital Thimphu, and the peaceful Punakha region. The journey includes adventurous hikes to iconic sites like Tiger’s Nest Monastery, nature walks, and exploration of hidden trails, offering a perfect balance of adventure and culture.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
  • Scenic trekking trails and nature walks
  • Explore Thimphu and Punakha
  • Drive via Dochula Pass
  • River valley views and forest trails
  • Cultural visits to monasteries and dzongs
  • Bird watching and photography opportunities
  • Peaceful Himalayan adventure experience

item.title: Lhasa Cultural & Heritage Tour – 4/5 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Lhasa Cultural & Heritage Tour is a short yet deeply enriching journey into the spiritual and cultural heart of Tibet. Centered in the historic city of Lhasa, this tour introduces travelers to Tibetan Buddhism, ancient architecture, and traditional Himalayan lifestyle.

You will explore UNESCO-listed landmarks like the magnificent Potala Palace, sacred monasteries, and vibrant local markets. This tour is ideal for those seeking cultural immersion, spiritual insight, and a short yet meaningful Tibetan experience.

  • Explore Jokhang Temple
  • Walk around Barkhor Street (local pilgrimage circuit)
  • Witness monk debates at Sera Monastery
  • Experience Tibetan culture, religion & daily life
  • Visit traditional monasteries & heritage sites
  • Short and easy high-altitude cultural tour

item.title: Tibet Overland Tour (Lhasa to Kathmandu) – 7/8 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
The Tibet Overland Tour from Lhasa to Kathmandu is one of the most scenic cross-border journeys in the Himalayas. This adventure takes you from the spiritual city of Lhasa across the vast Tibetan Plateau, through high mountain passes, pristine lakes, and traditional villages, ending in Kathmandu.

Travel along the legendary Friendship Highway, visiting iconic sites such as Yamdrok Lake and the north face of Mount Everest near Rongbuk Monastery. This tour combines culture, adventure, and breathtaking landscapes, making it one of the most popular Tibet journeys.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Scenic overland drive from Lhasa to Kathmandu
  • Visit Potala Palace & Jokhang Temple
  • Stunning views of Yamdrok Lake
  • Explore Everest north face at Rongbuk
  • Drive through high Himalayan passes (5,000m+)
  • Unique Tibetan culture and landscapes
  • Cross Tibet–Nepal border at Gyirong
