item.title: Nepal Heritage, Wildlife & Himalayan Discovery Tour
item.dc:creator: Everpeak
item.content:encoded: Overview Experience the best of Nepal in 8 days, exploring the cultural treasures of Kathmandu, the wildlife of Chitwan National Park, the spiritual birthplace of Lord Buddha in Lumbini, the scenic beauty of Pokhara, and the breathtaking Himalayan sunrise from Nagarkot. This journey offers a perfect blend of heritage, nature, wildlife, spirituality, and mountain landscapes.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: B.B/ Full board in the park

• Explore Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
  • Witness stunning Himalayan sunrise views from Sarangkot and Nagarkot.
  • Enjoy a peaceful boat ride on Phewa Lake in Pokhara.
  • Visit Davis Falls, Gupteshwor Cave, and Bindabasini Temple.
  • Explore Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha.
  • Experience a Jeep Safari in Chitwan National Park.
  • Enjoy canoe rides, bird watching, and jungle activities.
  • Discover the unique culture of the Tharu community.
  • Scenic drives through Nepal's beautiful hills, villages, and countryside.
  • Perfect blend of culture, spirituality, wildlife, nature, and mountain views.

• Airport arrival and departure transfers.
  • 2 nights accommodation in Kathmandu.
  • 2 nights accommodation in Pokhara.
  • 1 night accommodation in Lumbini.
  • 1 night accommodation in Chitwan.
  • 2 nights accommodation in Nagarkot.
  • Daily breakfast at hotels.
  • Full-board meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) in Chitwan.
  • Private tourist vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing.
  • Kathmandu sightseeing tour with an experienced guide.
  • Pokhara sightseeing tour.
  • Lumbini sightseeing tour.
  • Chitwan National Park activities as per itinerary.
  • Jeep Safari in Chitwan National Park.
  • Canoe ride and jungle walk in Chitwan.
  • Tharu village visit and cultural dance program.
  • All government taxes and service charges

• International airfare.
  • Nepal entry visa fees.
  • Travel insurance.
  • Lunch and dinner except in Chitwan.
  • Personal expenses (laundry, telephone, drinks, etc.).
  • Optional activities and adventure sports.
  • Monument and entrance fees during sightseeing.
  • Tips and gratuities for guides, drivers, and hotel staff.
  • Any expenses arising from flight delays, natural disasters, strikes, or circumstances beyond our control.
  • Any services not specifically mentioned under "Package Includes".

🎒 Essential Items

  • Valid Passport & Travel Documents
  • Travel Insurance Documents
  • Cash and Credit/Debit Cards
  • Mobile Phone & Charger

👕 Clothing

  • Comfortable Walking Shoes
  • Lightweight & Comfortable Clothing
  • Warm Jacket/Fleece (for Nagarkot)
  • Rain Jacket or Umbrella (seasonal)
  • Hat or Cap
  • Sunglasses

🧴 Personal Care Items

  • Sunscreen
  • Lip Balm
  • Insect Repellent
  • Personal Toiletries
  • Reusable Water Bottle
  • Personal Medications

📷 Electronics & Accessories

  • Camera
  • Extra Batteries
  • Power Bank
  • Memory Cards
  • Universal Travel Adapter

🎯 Optional Items

  • Binoculars (for Chitwan wildlife viewing)
  • Small Daypack
  • Trekking Poles (optional)
  • Notebook & Pen
  • Light Snacks for Long Drives

ℹ️ Important Note

Pack light and comfortable clothing suitable for varying weather conditions, from the warm plains of Lumbini and Chitwan to the cooler hill station of Nagarkot. Comfortable walking shoes are highly recommended throughout the tour.

a:9:{s:6:"item-0";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:27:"Day 1: Arrival in Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:143:"Arrive in Kathmandu, receive a warm welcome, transfer to your hotel, and enjoy a relaxing introduction to Nepal's vibrant culture and heritage.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:1213:"

Welcome to Nepal! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, our representative will warmly greet you and transfer you to your hotel. After check-in, take some time to relax and recover from your journey while enjoying the comfort of your accommodation.

Depending on your arrival time, you may explore the lively streets of Kathmandu, visit nearby local markets, or enjoy a leisurely walk around the bustling Thamel area. This is a wonderful opportunity to experience the unique blend of ancient traditions and modern city life that makes Kathmandu one of South Asia's most fascinating capitals.

In the evening, attend a short tour briefing where your guide will provide an overview of your upcoming journey through Nepal, including important travel information, destinations, accommodations, and planned activities. You will also have the opportunity to ask questions and make any final preparations for the days ahead.

Later, enjoy a traditional Nepali welcome dinner featuring authentic local cuisine and warm cultural hospitality.

After breakfast, begin a full-day sightseeing tour of Kathmandu Valley's most renowned cultural and religious attractions. Your first stop is Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal’s most sacred Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated on the banks of the holy Bagmati River. Observe the temple's magnificent architecture and experience the spiritual atmosphere that attracts pilgrims from across the world.

Continue to Boudhanath Stupa, one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world and an important center of Tibetan Buddhism. Walk around the stupa, spin the colorful prayer wheels, and soak in the peaceful ambiance while observing monks and devotees performing their daily rituals.

Next, visit the hilltop shrine of Swayambhunath Stupa, popularly known as the Monkey Temple. This ancient Buddhist complex offers stunning panoramic views of Kathmandu Valley and features beautifully adorned shrines, prayer flags, and traditional architecture.

Later, explore Kathmandu Durbar Square, the historic heart of the old city. Discover centuries-old temples, palaces, courtyards, and intricate wood-carved monuments that reflect Nepal's rich artistic and architectural heritage. Learn about the history of the former royal palace and the cultural significance of this UNESCO-listed site.

After a fascinating day of cultural exploration, return to your hotel and enjoy the evening at leisure.

fter breakfast, depart from Kathmandu and travel to Pokhara through picturesque hills, river valleys, terraced farmlands, and charming rural settlements. The drive follows the Trishuli and Marsyangdi Rivers, offering beautiful scenery throughout the journey.

Upon arrival in Pokhara, check in to your hotel and relax before exploring the vibrant Lakeside area. Take a leisurely walk along the shores of Phewa Lake, enjoy the peaceful atmosphere, and admire reflections of the surrounding mountains in the tranquil waters.

The remainder of the day is free to relax or explore the local cafés, shops, and lakeside promenade at your own pace.

Start the day with an early morning drive to Sarangkot to witness a spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna Himalayan range. Enjoy breathtaking views of snow-capped peaks, including Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) and Annapurna.

After breakfast, visit some of Pokhara's most famous attractions, including Davis Falls, Gupteshwor Cave, and Bindabasini Temple. Later, enjoy a relaxing boat ride on Phewa Lake and visit the beautiful Tal Barahi Temple situated on a small island in the lake.

Spend the remainder of the day exploring the vibrant Lakeside area, known for its scenic beauty, cafés, and local shops, before returning to your hotel.

Photography opportunities are excellent throughout the day.";}s:6:"item-4";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:26:"Day 5: Pokhara – Lumbini";s:11:"description";s:159:"Travel from the scenic lakeside city of Pokhara to Lumbini, the sacred birthplace of Lord Buddha and one of the world's most important pilgrimage destinations.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:969:"

After breakfast, depart from Pokhara and begin a scenic drive towards Lumbini, located in the fertile plains of southern Nepal. The journey offers beautiful views of rolling hills, rivers, traditional villages, and agricultural landscapes, showcasing Nepal's diverse geography and rural lifestyle.

Upon arrival in Lumbini, check in to your hotel and begin exploring this renowned UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the sacred Maya Devi Temple, the exact birthplace of Lord Buddha, and explore the Sacred Garden, an important pilgrimage area filled with historical and spiritual significance.

Later, visit the International Monastic Zone, where beautifully designed monasteries built by various countries reflect different Buddhist traditions and architectural styles. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before returning to your hotel for an overnight stay.

After breakfast, depart from Lumbini and drive towards Chitwan, home to Nepal's first national park and one of the country's most renowned wildlife destinations. The scenic journey passes through picturesque villages, fertile farmlands, and beautiful landscapes of the Terai region.

Upon arrival in Chitwan, check in to your jungle resort and enjoy a welcome refreshment. After some time to relax, explore a traditional Tharu village and learn about the unique culture, customs, and lifestyle of the indigenous Tharu community.

Later, enjoy a peaceful walk along the banks of the Rapti River and admire the natural surroundings. In the evening, witness a lively Tharu Cultural Dance Program featuring traditional music and performances that showcase the rich heritage of the region.

After dinner, relax at the resort and prepare for the exciting jungle adventures awaiting you the following day.

After an early breakfast, begin your wildlife activities in Chitwan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its rich biodiversity. Enjoy a peaceful canoe ride along the Rapti River, where you may spot crocodiles, water birds, and other aquatic wildlife in their natural habitat.

Continue with a guided jungle walk and an exciting Jeep Safari through the park's forests and grasslands. Keep an eye out for one-horned rhinoceroses, deer, wild boars, monkeys, and various bird species while learning about the park's unique ecosystem from experienced naturalists.

Following the safari activities, depart from Chitwan and drive towards Nagarkot. The journey takes you through scenic countryside landscapes, traditional settlements, and rolling hills before reaching this popular hill station located on the eastern rim of Kathmandu Valley.

Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and enjoy the peaceful mountain atmosphere. If weather permits, witness a spectacular sunset over the Himalayas before settling in for the night.

Wake up to the tranquil atmosphere of Nagarkot and enjoy a leisurely breakfast while admiring panoramic views of the surrounding hills and Himalayan ranges. Known for its spectacular mountain vistas, Nagarkot offers a perfect retreat away from the hustle and bustle of city life.

The day is free for relaxation and exploration at your own pace. You may take a leisurely walk through the nearby villages and forest trails, interact with local communities, or simply unwind at your hotel while enjoying the stunning natural surroundings.

Throughout the day, enjoy magnificent views of the Himalayan peaks and the beautiful landscapes of the Kathmandu Valley. The peaceful environment makes Nagarkot an ideal destination for photography, nature walks, and relaxation.

In the evening, witness another unforgettable sunset over the mountains before spending a comfortable night at your hotel.

Rise early to experience one of the highlights of your journey—a breathtaking sunrise over the Himalayas from Nagarkot. On clear days, enjoy panoramic views of snow-capped peaks stretching across the horizon while the morning sunlight illuminates the majestic mountain range.

After breakfast at the hotel, take some time to enjoy the peaceful surroundings and fresh mountain air before beginning your drive back to Kathmandu. The scenic journey offers final glimpses of Nepal's beautiful countryside and traditional settlements.

Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to Tribhuvan International Airport for your onward flight. As your memorable journey through Nepal comes to an end, depart with wonderful memories of the country's rich culture, spiritual heritage, diverse wildlife, and stunning Himalayan landscapes.

item.title: Nagarkot-Dhulikhel-Namobuddha hike
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Overview

The Nagarkot Dhulikhel Namobuddha Hike is one of the best short hiking adventures near Kathmandu. It combines beautiful Himalayan views, peaceful hill trails, traditional villages, and important cultural sites. Therefore, it is an excellent choice for travelers who want to experience nature and local culture without trekking at high altitude.

Scenic Trail and Cultural Experience

The journey begins with a drive to Nagarkot, a famous hill station known for its spectacular sunrise over the Himalayas. From there, the trail follows forest paths and quiet ridges to Dhulikhel, offering panoramic views of the Langtang, Ganesh, Everest, and Gaurishankar ranges. Along the way, you pass charming villages, green farmland, and terraced hills. In addition, you can meet local people and experience authentic Newari culture.

Visit the Sacred Namobuddha

The highlight of the hike is Namobuddha, one of Nepal's most important Buddhist pilgrimage sites. Here, you can visit the peaceful monastery, observe monks during daily prayers, and enjoy the calm surroundings. Moreover, the spiritual atmosphere makes this destination truly memorable. Afterward, the trip continues to the historic city of Bhaktapur before returning to Kathmandu.

Why Choose This Hike?

The Nagarkot Dhulikhel Namobuddha Hike is suitable for beginners, families, and anyone looking for a relaxing outdoor adventure. Because the trails are easy to moderate, no previous trekking experience is required. Furthermore, the hike is enjoyable throughout the year, especially during spring and autumn when the weather is clear and the mountain views are outstanding.

Overall, the Nagarkot Dhulikhel Namobuddha Hike offers the perfect mix of mountain scenery, cultural heritage, and spiritual discovery. As a result, it remains one of the most rewarding short hikes in Nepal for travelers with limited time.

item.title: Dhaulagiri Trekking
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Dhaulagiri Trekking Overview

Dhaulagiri Trekking is one of Nepal's most challenging and rewarding trekking adventures. It takes you around Mount Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), the world's seventh-highest mountain. Unlike many popular trekking routes, this trail remains quiet and remote. Therefore, it is perfect for experienced trekkers looking for a true Himalayan adventure.

The journey begins through traditional villages, terraced fields, and beautiful forests. Soon, the trail enters rugged alpine landscapes filled with glaciers and rocky valleys. Moreover, every day brings spectacular views of Dhaulagiri, Tukuche Peak, Nilgiri, Annapurna I, and other snow-covered mountains. As a result, the scenery changes constantly and keeps the trek exciting.

Furthermore, the route follows peaceful trails with very few trekkers. Consequently, you can enjoy nature without large crowds. In addition, the remote campsites provide a genuine wilderness experience. Although the trek is demanding, every step rewards you with unforgettable mountain scenery.

Cross High Passes and Hidden Valleys

One of the biggest highlights of Dhaulagiri Trekking is crossing the famous French Pass (5,360 m). Afterwards, you continue through the beautiful Hidden Valley before reaching Dhampus Pass (5,240 m). From both passes, you enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Himalayas. Meanwhile, massive glaciers and dramatic ice fields surround the trail.

Moreover, the trek passes rivers, forests, alpine meadows, and rocky landscapes. Because the environment changes every day, the journey never feels repetitive. Likewise, wildlife lovers may spot blue sheep, Himalayan griffons, and other mountain animals.

Best Time for Dhaulagiri Trekking

Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the best seasons for Dhaulagiri Trekking. During these months, the weather is usually stable, and the skies stay clear. Therefore, mountain views are outstanding. However, the route reaches high elevations, so proper acclimatization is essential. In addition, good physical fitness and previous trekking experience are highly recommended.

Finally, Dhaulagiri Trekking offers an unforgettable journey through one of Nepal's wildest mountain regions. Overall, it combines remote trails, towering peaks, high mountain passes, and stunning glacier scenery. Whether you want adventure, solitude, or spectacular Himalayan landscapes, this trek delivers a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

item.title: Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek – North & South Base Camp (21 Days)
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek – Nepal's Ultimate Remote Adventure
The Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek is one of Nepal's most spectacular and least-explored trekking adventures. Located in eastern Nepal, this remarkable journey combines both the North and South Base Camps of Mount Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain at 8,586 meters. Unlike Nepal's busier trekking routes, this expedition offers peaceful trails, untouched wilderness, and authentic mountain culture. As a result, it is perfect for trekkers seeking a true Himalayan adventure.
Explore Remote Villages and Diverse Landscapes
The scenic route passes through lush forests, rhododendron hills, alpine meadows, glacier valleys, and high mountain passes. Along the way, you visit traditional Rai, Limbu, and Sherpa villages where local customs and warm hospitality remain unchanged. Furthermore, every day reveals breathtaking views of Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Jannu, and numerous snow-covered Himalayan peaks. In addition, the surrounding Conservation Area is home to rare wildlife, including the snow leopard, Himalayan black bear, red panda, blue sheep, and musk deer.
Visit Both North and South Base Camps
One of the greatest highlights of the itinerary is visiting both North Base Camp at Pangpema and South Base Camp near Oktang. Meanwhile, trekkers enjoy dramatic glaciers, towering ice walls, and unforgettable mountain panoramas. Afterward, crossing the scenic Sele La Pass connects the two valleys and adds even more adventure to the journey. Consequently, the trek becomes one of Nepal's most rewarding high-altitude expeditions.
Why Choose this Legendary Wilderness Route?
This epic path offers the perfect balance of challenging adventure, pristine nature, and deep cultural immersion. Not only does it offer incredible mountain scenery, but it also provides rich local culture, diverse landscapes, abundant wildlife, and peaceful trails. Ultimately, this unforgettable adventure delivers an authentic Himalayan experience that few trekkers ever have the opportunity to enjoy.

The Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek passes through lush forests, rhododendron hills, alpine meadows, glacier valleys, and high mountain passes. Along the way, you visit traditional Rai, Limbu, and Sherpa villages where local customs and warm hospitality remain unchanged. Furthermore, every day reveals breathtaking views of Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Jannu, and numerous snow-covered Himalayan peaks. In addition, the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area is home to rare wildlife, including the snow leopard, Himalayan black bear, red panda, blue sheep, and musk deer.

Visit Both North and South Base Camps

One of the greatest highlights of the Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek is visiting both North Base Camp at Pangpema and South Base Camp near Oktang. Meanwhile, trekkers enjoy dramatic glaciers, towering ice walls, and unforgettable mountain panoramas. Afterward, crossing the scenic Sele La Pass connects the two valleys and adds even more adventure to the journey. Consequently, the trek becomes one of Nepal's most rewarding high-altitude expeditions.

Why Choose the Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek?

The Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek is ideal for experienced trekkers who want to explore one of Nepal's last truly remote trekking regions. Not only does it offer incredible mountain scenery, but it also provides rich local culture, diverse landscapes, abundant wildlife, and peaceful trails. Ultimately, this unforgettable adventure delivers an authentic Himalayan experience that few trekkers ever have the opportunity to enjoy.

The Trail Conditions:

Straight, Uphill, Downhill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, somewhere flat man made stone steps, through the rhododendron, moss covered forests, suspensions metal bridges

Medication

  • Bandage for sprains
  • Plasters/Band-aids
  • Iodine or water filter (optional)
  • Moleskin/Second skin - for blisters
  • Antiseptic ointment for cuts
  • Anti-bacterial throat lozenges (with antiseptic)
  • Aspirin/paracetamol - general painkiller
  • Oral dehydration salts
  • Broad-spectrum antibiotic (norfloxacin or ciprofloxin)
  • Anti-diarrhea medication (antibiotic)
  • Diarrhea stopper (Imodium - optional)
  • Antibiotic for Giardia or similar microbe or bacteria
  • Diamox (altitude sickness - can be bought in Kathmandu)

 

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing / equipment for our trek to Kanchenjunga

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket
  • Set lightweight thermals
  • North Face down Jacket (Preferably)
  • Small thin towel (sports towel best)
  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
  • Hat
  • Cotton or silk bag liner – optional
  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves
  • Rucksack
  • Pack tissues
  • Pair sunglasses
  • Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.
  • Camera and films
  • Head torch and spare batteries
  • Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) deg C during our trek)

 

Above things are required for Kanchenjunga Trek. However if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.
Sightseeing / Cultural Day In Kathmandu Valley

✅ Package Includes

  • Airport pick-up and drop-off by private vehicle
  • Domestic flights: Kathmandu – Bhadrapur – Kathmandu
  • Private jeep transportation as per itinerary
  • Kanchenjunga Restricted Area Permit (RAP)
  • Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (KCAP)
  • All required government taxes and permit fees
  • Experienced English-speaking licensed trekking guide
  • Porter service (1 porter for every 2 trekkers)
  • Guide and porter salary, meals, accommodation, insurance, and equipment
  • Teahouse/lodge accommodation during the trek
  • Three meals a day during the trek (Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner)
  • Seasonal fresh fruits during the trek
  • Three nights hotel accommodation in Kathmandu with breakfast
  • Comprehensive first-aid medical kit carried by the guide
  • Sleeping bag and duffel bag (upon request)
  • Welcome and farewell dinner in Kathmandu
  • 24/7 emergency support from the company

• Nepal entry visa fees
  • International airfare to and from Nepal
  • Travel and rescue insurance
  • Personal trekking equipment and clothing
  • Lunch and dinner in Kathmandu
  • Hot showers, Wi-Fi, battery charging, and personal expenses during the trek
  • Alcoholic, soft, and bottled drinks
  • Snacks, desserts, and extra food outside the set menu
  • Tips for guide, porter, and driver (recommended)
  • Personal medical expenses
  • Extra hotel nights in Kathmandu due to early arrival, late departure, or itinerary changes
  • Costs arising from flight delays, natural disasters, strikes, weather conditions, or circumstances beyond our control
  • Any services not specifically mentioned in the "Package Includes" section

🎒 Backpack & Bags

  • Duffel bag (70–90L)
  • Daypack (30–40L)
  • Rain cover
  • Dry bags or waterproof liners

👕 Clothing

  • Trekking T-shirts (3–4)
  • Trekking pants (2–3 pairs)
  • Thermal base layers
  • Fleece jacket
  • Down jacket
  • Waterproof jacket & pants
  • Warm hat and sun hat
  • Gloves

👞 Footwear

  • Waterproof trekking boots
  • Camp shoes/sandals
  • Trekking socks (5–6 pairs)
  • Warm wool socks

🥾 Trekking Equipment

  • Sleeping bag (-15°C to -20°C recommended)
  • Trekking poles
  • Headlamp
  • Water bottles or hydration bladder
  • Sunglasses
  • Power bank

🧴 Personal Items

  • Sunscreen
  • Lip balm
  • Personal medications
  • Basic first-aid kit
  • Toiletries
  • Wet wipes and hand sanitizer

❄️ Note: Kanchenjunga is one of Nepal's most remote trekking regions. Expect long trekking days, limited facilities, and cold temperatures at higher elevations. Warm clothing, sturdy boots, and a high-quality sleeping bag are essential for a safe and comfortable journey.

item.title: Rara Lake Trekking
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Rara Lake Trekking – A Remote Himalayan Journey
The Rara Lake Trekking experience stands out as one of Nepal's most beautiful, remote, and peaceful wilderness adventures. Tucked away in the hidden Karnali region of western Nepal, this scenic pathway leads to the country's largest and deepest freshwater lake. Because it is far removed from the busier, highly commercialized routes, this serene high-altitude expedition remains an absolute favorite for travelers seeking deep tranquility and untouched natural landscapes.
What to Expect on Your Wilderness Trail
Your mountain journey begins with an exciting flight from Nepalgunj to the remote airstrip in Talcha. From there, the walking trails wind through pristine coniferous woods filled with blue pine, spruce, and rhododendron trees. As you ascend toward the water's edge, you explore traditional villages that reveal a unique local lifestyle and traditional culture unchanged by modern times. Along the way, staying in quiet teahouses allows you to experience authentic Nepalese hospitality.
Discover the Magnificent Blue Gem of Karnali
Arriving at your final destination provides an unparalleled view of the magnificent water body, which sits beautifully inside Rara National Park at an elevation of 2,990 meters. The lake is famous for its changing colors, shifting from deep blue to brilliant emerald throughout the day. Additionally, the surrounding protected conservation area serves as a safe sanctuary for rare wildlife, including the musk deer, Himalayan black bear, and numerous migratory bird species.
Why Choose This Remote Wilderness Holiday?
Opting for Rara Lake Trekking offers the perfect blend of dramatic alpine landscapes, rich cultural discovery, and peaceful trails. Not only do you walk through diverse ecological zones, but you also experience an off-the-beaten-path holiday that very few tourists ever witness. Ultimately, this unforgettable Himalayan journey delivers incredible photography opportunities, profound isolation, and a deep appreciation for the natural world.

Straight, Uphill, Downhill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, somewhere flat man made stone steps, through the rhododendron, moss covered forests, suspensions metal bridges

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing / equipment for our trek to Rara Lake

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket

  • Shampoo

  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves

  • Pack tissues

item.title: Nar Phu Valley & Thorong La Pass Expedition Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Nar Phu Valley Trek

The Nar Phu Valley Trek is one of Nepal's most remote and rewarding Himalayan adventures. This remarkable journey combines the untouched landscapes of Nar and Phu with the dramatic crossing of Thorong La Pass. Along the way, trekkers experience ancient villages, traditional Tibetan-influenced culture, historic monasteries, and spectacular mountain scenery. The route is ideal for experienced hikers who want to explore a quieter and less-traveled part of the Annapurna region.

Explore the Hidden Nar and Phu Valleys

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu before joining the Annapurna trail toward Koto. From there, the route enters the restricted Nar Phu region, where narrow valleys, dramatic cliffs, stone-built villages, and peaceful forests create an unforgettable Himalayan setting.

The trail passes through traditional settlements such as Meta, Phu, and Nar. Trekkers can observe local lifestyles, visit ancient monasteries, and enjoy impressive views of Annapurna II, Himlung Himal, Kang Guru, Pisang Peak, and Chulu East. The remote location and welcoming local communities give the journey an authentic cultural experience.

Experience Remote Himalayan Culture

One of the most rewarding aspects of the journey is the opportunity to experience the traditional way of life in the high Himalayas. The villages of Nar and Phu have preserved their distinctive customs, architecture, and Buddhist heritage. Exploring these communities provides a deeper understanding of mountain life while adding cultural richness to the adventure.

After leaving the Nar Phu region, the trail continues toward the Annapurna Circuit and prepares trekkers for the challenging high-altitude section.

Cross Thorong La Pass

A major highlight is the ascent to Thorong La Pass at 5,416 meters. Proper acclimatization is essential before attempting the pass. The demanding climb is rewarded with spectacular panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges. After crossing the pass, the trail descends toward Muktinath, an important pilgrimage destination known for its religious significance and dramatic mountain surroundings. From here, the journey continues through the beautiful Kali Gandaki region toward Pokhara.

Why Choose This Himalayan Adventure?

The Nar Phu Valley Trek is an excellent choice for experienced trekkers seeking remote landscapes, cultural discovery, and challenging Himalayan trails. The combination of restricted valleys, traditional villages, high mountain passes, and spectacular scenery makes this route different from more crowded trekking trails in Nepal.

For more information about related trekking routes, you can internally link to your [Annapurna Circuit Trek] page. You can also add a trustworthy external reference to the Nepal Tourism Board where appropriate.

This adventure is best suited to trekkers with good fitness and previous high-altitude experience. With proper preparation, gradual acclimatization, and an experienced guide, the journey offers an unforgettable exploration of Nepal's remote mountain landscapes.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• 🏔️ Explore the remote and restricted Nar Phu Valley, one of Nepal’s most untouched regions
  • 🏘️ Experience ancient Tibetan-influenced villages like Phu and Nar with preserved culture
  • 🥾 Scenic trekking through deep gorges, alpine valleys, and dramatic Himalayan landscapes
  • 🕉️ Visit sacred monasteries, chortens, and prayer-flag-filled spiritual trails
  • 🌿 Cross diverse terrain from lush river valleys to high-altitude barren landscapes
  • 🧭 Acclimatization experience in Manang with panoramic Himalayan views
  • 🏔️ Cross the legendary Thorong La Pass (5,416m) – one of the highest trekking passes in the world
  • 🙏 Visit the sacred pilgrimage site of Muktinath, important for both Hindus and Buddhists
  • 🚗 Scenic descent through Mustang region and Kali Gandaki valley to Pokhara
  • 🌏 A complete Himalayan expedition combining wilderness, culture, and adventure in one route
Sightseeing / Cultural Day In Kathmandu Valley

• 🚖 Airport pickup and drop (Kathmandu International Airport)
  • 🏨 2 nights hotel accommodation in Kathmandu (arrival & departure)
  • 🥾 Full guided trekking service with experienced licensed guide
  • 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Required number of porters (2 trekkers : 1 porter basis)
  • 🎟️ Restricted Area Permit (Nar Phu Valley Permit)
  • 🏔️ Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
  • 🚗 Kathmandu → Koto private/public transportation
  • 🚙 Muktinath → Pokhara transportation
  • 🚌 Pokhara → Kathmandu tourist bus transfer
  • 🏡 Basic tea house/lodge accommodation during trek
  • 🍽️ Three meals per day during trekking (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)
  • 🩺 First aid kit and basic medical support carried by guide
  • 🗺️ Trekking map and route briefing
  • 🧑‍🏫 All government taxes and service charges

• ✈️ International airfare to/from Nepal
  • 🛂 Nepal entry visa fee
  • 🍛 Meals in Kathmandu, Pokhara (except breakfast if stated)
  • 🛍️ Personal expenses (snacks, drinks, hot showers, charging, etc.)
  • 🏨 Extra hotel nights due to early arrival/late departure or delays
  • 🧗 Travel insurance (mandatory but not included)
  • 💰 Tips for guide and porter (recommended)
  • 🚁 Emergency evacuation or helicopter rescue costs (if needed)
  • 📸 Personal trekking equipment and gear
  • 🎫 Entry fees for monuments during city tours

👕 Clothing (Layer System)

  • 🧥 Down jacket (high altitude essential)
  • 🧥 Waterproof/windproof jacket
  • 👕 Quick-dry trekking t-shirts (2–4 pcs)
  • 👖 Trekking pants (2 pairs)
  • 🧦 Woolen socks + quick-dry socks (5–6 pairs)
  • 🧣 Buff / neck gaiter for dust & cold
  • 🧤 Warm gloves (inner + outer if possible)
  • 🧢 Sun hat + woolen cap (for cold mornings)
  • 🩳 Light clothes for lower altitude areas

👟 Footwear

  • 🥾 Strong waterproof trekking boots (well broken-in)
  • 🩴 Lightweight sandals/slippers (for lodges)

🎒 Backpack & Storage

  • 🎒 30–50L trekking backpack (day use)
  • 🎒 Duffel bag (carried by porter, if included)
  • 🧳 Rain cover for backpack

🧭 Trekking Essentials

  • 💧 Reusable water bottle or hydration bladder
  • 🔦 Headlamp with extra batteries
  • 🧴 Sunscreen (SPF 30–50)
  • 🕶️ UV protection sunglasses
  • 🧻 Wet wipes & toilet paper
  • 🍫 Energy bars / dry snacks

🩺 Health & Safety

  • 💊 Personal medications
  • 🩹 Basic first aid kit
  • 💊 Altitude sickness medicine (consult doctor)
  • 🧂 ORS / electrolytes

📱 Electronics

  • 📱 Mobile phone + power bank
  • 📸 Camera (optional)
  • 🔌 Universal adapter
  • 🔋 Extra batteries (cold reduces battery life)

🪪 Documents & Money

  • 🪪 Passport + photocopy
  • 🎫 Permits (provided by agency)
  • 💵 Cash (Nepali rupees for tea houses & personal use)

🧗 Optional but Useful

  • 🥢 Trekking poles (highly recommended for Thorong La)
  • 🛏️ Sleeping bag (for cold seasons)
  • 🧤 Hand warmers (winter trek)

Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, our representative will greet you and assist with your transfer to the hotel. After check-in, you can rest and recover from your journey.

Depending on your arrival time, you may explore nearby streets, local markets, or simply relax at the hotel. In the evening, there will be a short briefing about the upcoming Nar Phu Valley and Thorong La Pass trekking itinerary, including route overview and preparation details.

Enjoy your first night in Kathmandu, the vibrant capital city of Nepal.

After breakfast in Kathmandu, begin your long but scenic drive toward Koto, the gateway to the Nar Phu Valley region. The journey follows the Prithvi Highway and continues along the Marsyangdi River valley, offering beautiful views of terraced fields, rural settlements, and distant Himalayan peaks.

The route passes through popular towns like Besisahar and continues deeper into the Annapurna region. As you ascend higher, the landscapes become more rugged and mountainous, with winding roads and stunning river gorges.

Upon reaching Koto, a small settlement near Chame, check into the teahouse or lodge. Rest and prepare for the trekking section starting from the next day into the restricted Nar Phu Valley.

Overnight stay in basic mountain lodge.";}s:6:"item-2";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:29:"Day 3: Trek from Koto to Meta";s:11:"description";s:136:"Begin trekking into the restricted Nar Phu Valley region as you enter remote landscapes, deep gorges, and peaceful Himalayan wilderness.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:778:"

After breakfast in Koto, begin your trekking journey into the restricted Nar Phu Valley. The trail initially follows the narrow Marsyangdi River gorge, passing through dense pine forests, suspension bridges, and rocky paths carved into steep cliffs.

As you move deeper into the valley, the landscape becomes more remote and dramatic with fewer settlements and increasing wilderness. You will enter the conservation and restricted area checkpoint before continuing toward Meta.

Meta is a small seasonal settlement surrounded by high cliffs and alpine terrain. Upon arrival, check into a basic teahouse and rest while enjoying the peaceful mountain environment.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:4:"Koto";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:4:"Meta";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:27:"Approx. 14–16 km trekking";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:30:"Approximately 6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:196:"Restricted area permit is required for this region. After breakfast in Meta, continue your trek deeper into the Nar Phu Valley. The trail gradually ascends through barren landscapes, narrow canyons, and dramatic rock formations shaped by centuries of erosion.

As you move higher, vegetation becomes sparse and the scenery turns more alpine and rugged. You may pass occasional yak herder camps and experience the raw wilderness of the region with very few settlements along the route.

Arrive in Kyang, a small high-altitude settlement surrounded by dramatic cliffs and mountain views. Check into a teahouse and rest in the peaceful isolation of the Himalayas.

After breakfast in Kyang, begin your trek toward the highly remote Phu Village, one of the most isolated settlements in the Nar Phu Valley. The trail passes through dramatic canyon landscapes, narrow gorges, and high alpine terrain with stunning rock formations.

As you move deeper into the valley, the scenery becomes more rugged and mystical, with ancient Buddhist chortens, prayer flags, and mani walls guiding the way. The route is quiet and untouched, offering a true wilderness experience.

Arrive at Phu Village, a centuries-old Tibetan-influenced settlement located on a hillside overlooking the valley. Explore the traditional stone houses and ancient monasteries, and experience the preserved Himalayan culture.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:5:"Kyang";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:11:"Phu Village";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:27:"Approx. 10–12 km trekking";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:30:"Approximately 5–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:154:"This is a high-altitude remote trek with basic facilities. Today is an important acclimatization and exploration day in Phu Village. After breakfast, spend the day exploring this ancient Tibetan-influenced settlement, one of the most remote villages in Nepal.

Walk through narrow stone alleys, visit traditional houses, and observe the unique lifestyle of the local people who have preserved their culture for centuries. You may also hike to nearby viewpoints offering dramatic views of the surrounding valleys and mountains.

Visit local monasteries and chortens, and learn about the spiritual and cultural significance of the region. This slow-paced day helps your body adjust to the higher altitude while giving you deep cultural insight into the Nar Phu Valley.

Return to your teahouse in the evening and rest.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:11:"Phu Village";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:11:"Phu Village";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:58:"Short hikes around village (2–5 km optional exploration)";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:46:"Approximately 3–5 hours flexible exploration";s:14:"important_note";s:183:"Acclimatization is very important at this altitude. After breakfast in Phu Village, begin your descent toward Nar Phedi. The trail retraces part of the rugged Nar Phu Valley route, passing through rocky terrain, deep gorges, and ancient Buddhist chortens.

As you descend, the landscape gradually becomes less harsh, with slightly more vegetation and wider valley views. The journey offers a peaceful walking experience with stunning Himalayan backdrops and spiritual markers along the trail.

Arrive at Nar Phedi Monastery, a serene and isolated Buddhist monastery where trekkers often stay. Experience simple monastic life, peaceful surroundings, and a deeply spiritual atmosphere.

After a peaceful night at Nar Phedi Monastery, begin your trek toward Nar Village. The trail gradually ascends through dry alpine terrain, passing ancient chortens, prayer flags, and stone pathways that reflect the deep Buddhist heritage of the region.

As you gain altitude, the views open up to wide Himalayan landscapes and surrounding valleys. The route is culturally rich, with traditional Mani walls and occasional encounters with local villagers and yak herders.

Arrive at Nar Village, a beautiful high-altitude settlement known for its preserved Tibetan culture, traditional stone houses, and spiritual atmosphere. Spend the evening exploring the village and interacting with locals.

Take it slow due to altitude. After an early breakfast in Nar Village, begin your challenging trek toward Ngawal via the high mountain route. This section involves a significant ascent as you gradually leave the Nar Valley behind and enter the Annapurna region.

The trail passes through rugged alpine terrain, high passes, and remote landscapes with breathtaking views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks. Depending on the route and conditions, trekkers may experience sections of steep climb and rocky paths.

Arrive in Ngawal, a beautiful traditional village in the Manang region known for its stone houses, Buddhist culture, and panoramic mountain scenery. Enjoy a well-deserved rest in this scenic Himalayan settlement.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:11:"Nar Village";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:6:"Ngawal";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:71:"Approx. 15–18 km trekking (high altitude route via Kang La direction)";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:30:"Approximately 7–9 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:181:"This is a high-altitude and physically demanding day. Proper acclimatization, slow pace, and hydration are essential. Weather can change quickly, and sections may be steep or windy.";}s:6:"item-9";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:34:"Day 10: Trek from Ngawal to Manang";s:11:"description";s:114:"A scenic descent into the Manang valley with stunning views of Annapurna range and traditional Himalayan villages.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:685:"

After breakfast in Ngawal, begin your trek toward Manang. The trail descends gradually through beautiful landscapes, passing traditional stone villages, monasteries, and wide Himalayan valleys.

You will enjoy breathtaking views of Annapurna II, III, Gangapurna, and surrounding peaks throughout the journey. The route is part of the classic Annapurna Circuit, well-marked and culturally rich.

Arrive in Manang, one of the most important trekking hubs in the region. Explore the village, visit local monasteries, and prepare for higher altitude acclimatization ahead.

Manang is a key acclimatization point, so stay hydrated and avoid overexertion.";}s:7:"item-10";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:38:"Day 11: Trek from Manang to Yak Kharka";s:11:"description";s:107:"A gradual ascent from Manang to Yak Kharka as you enter higher alpine terrain with stunning mountain views.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:698:"

After breakfast in Manang, begin your gradual ascent toward Yak Kharka. The trail climbs steadily through alpine landscapes, crossing small settlements, yak grazing fields, and open valleys surrounded by towering Himalayan peaks.

The route offers breathtaking views of Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and Tilicho Peak as you gain altitude. You will notice thinner air and colder temperatures as you move higher into the mountains.

Arrive in Yak Kharka, a small high-altitude settlement used mainly by trekkers and yak herders. Rest and prepare for the next stage toward Thorong Phedi.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:6:"Manang";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:10:"Yak Kharka";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:26:"Approx. 9–11 km trekking";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:30:"Approximately 4–5 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:121:"Gradual altitude gain day. Walk slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid rushing. Weather can become cold and windy in Yak Kharka";}s:7:"item-11";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:45:"Day 12: Trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi";s:11:"description";s:108:"A steady ascent through alpine terrain as you approach Thorong Phedi, the base for crossing Thorong La Pass.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:667:"

After breakfast in Yak Kharka, begin your trek toward Thorong Phedi. The trail gradually ascends through rugged alpine landscapes, crossing suspension bridges, landslide-prone areas, and rocky paths.

As you move higher, the scenery becomes more barren and dramatic, with wide views of snow-capped peaks and deep valleys. The air becomes thinner, so a slow and steady pace is important.

Arrive at Thorong Phedi, the last major stop before crossing Thorong La Pass. Rest at a basic teahouse and prepare for the most challenging day of the trek ahead.

Walk slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid overexertion. Start very early in the morning (around 3–4 AM) from Thorong Phedi. The trail ascends steeply toward Thorong La Pass, the highest point of the entire trek at 5,416 meters. The climb is long and demanding due to high altitude and cold weather.

After reaching the summit of Thorong La Pass, enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Himalayas before beginning a long and steep descent toward Muktinath. The landscape gradually changes from snowy high mountains to dry Mustang terrain.

Arrive in Muktinath, a sacred pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Buddhists. Visit the famous Muktinath Temple and surrounding shrines before resting at your lodge.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Thorong Phedi";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:9:"Muktinath";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:27:"Approx. 15–17 km trekking";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:31:"Approximately 8–10 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:160:"Very challenging high-altitude day. Start early, walk slowly, and stay hydrated. Weather at Thorong La can change rapidly with strong winds and snow conditions.";}s:7:"item-13";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:39:"Day 14: Drive from Muktinath to Pokhara";s:11:"description";s:97:"A scenic long drive descending from the Mustang region to the beautiful lakeside city of Pokhara.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:690:"

After breakfast in Muktinath, begin your drive toward Pokhara. The journey descends from the dry, high-altitude Mustang region through dramatic landscapes, deep gorges, and riverside roads.

Passing through Jomsom and along the Kali Gandaki Valley, you will witness changing scenery from barren mountains to lush green hills and terraced fields. The drive offers beautiful views of Nilgiri, Dhaulagiri, and Annapurna ranges.

Arrive in Pokhara by evening and check into your hotel. Enjoy the peaceful lakeside atmosphere and relax after the long journey from the mountains.

Carry motion sickness medication if needed and be prepared for changing road conditions.";}s:7:"item-14";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:39:"Day 15: Drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:113:"A scenic drive back to Kathmandu from Pokhara, passing rivers, hills, and traditional villages along the highway.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:613:"

After breakfast in Pokhara, begin your drive back to Kathmandu along the Prithvi Highway. The route follows the Trishuli River, passing through green hills, terraced farmlands, and small roadside towns.

Enjoy scenic views of rural Nepal and mountain landscapes during the journey. You may stop along the way for lunch or short breaks.

Arrive in Kathmandu by late afternoon or evening and transfer to your hotel. The rest of the evening is free for relaxation or last-minute shopping in the city.

item.title: Upper Dolpo Trekking
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Upper Dolpo Trekking – A Remote Himalayan Adventure
The Upper Dolpo Trekking experience stands out as one of Nepal's most remote, rewarding, and deeply spiritual wilderness adventures. Tucked away in the far-western Himalayas, this forbidden land offers an extraordinary landscape defined by stark barren valleys, deep river gorges, and the legendary emerald-blue waters of Phoksundo Lake. Unlike the busier trails of Nepal, this ancient pathway provides absolute peace, untouched alpine beauty, and a rare opportunity to witness an isolated mountain culture that has remained unchanged for centuries. It is the ultimate journey for intrepid travelers seeking true solitude in a pristine Himalayan sanctuary.
Discover Hidden Valleys and Ancient Monasteries
This legendary trail leads adventurers through the high-altitude landscapes of Shey Phoksundo National Park. Along the way, you will witness spectacular scenery and cross challenging high mountain passes like Kang La and Saldang La. The route connects traditional, isolated villages where the local people practice the ancient, pre-Buddhist Bon religion. Exploring centuries-old monasteries like Shey Gompa adds an unforgettable spiritual depth to this rugged wilderness journey.
Why Choose this Isolated Wilderness Path?
This epic route offers an unparalleled escape for experienced hikers seeking true isolation and deep cultural immersion. Not only does it showcase dramatic trans-Himalayan scenery, but it also provides a rare glimpse into a lifestyle untouched by the modern world. Furthermore, the pristine environment serves as a sanctuary for rare wildlife, including the elusive snow leopard and blue sheep. Ultimately, it delivers an extraordinary adventure that very few travelers ever get to experience.
Preparing for Your Wilderness Expedition
Because this region is highly restricted and completely isolated, travelers must plan carefully before setting out. You will need a registered guide, a special restricted area permit, and fully self-sufficient camping equipment. The best time to visit is from May to October, as the area lies in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, making it an ideal summer trek.
The Upper Dolpo Trekking experience stands out as one of Nepal's most remote, rewarding, and deeply spiritual wilderness adventures. Located in the far-western Himalayas, this hidden region offers a mesmerizing landscape of barren valleys, deep gorges, and crystal-clear lakes. Unlike busier trails, this ancient pathway provides absolute peace, untouched natural beauty, and a chance to witness an isolated mountain culture that has remained unchanged for centuries. It is the ultimate choice for trekkers seeking a true, off-the-beaten-path journey.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
The Trail Conditions:

Straight, Uphill, Downhill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, somewhere flat man made stone steps, through the rhododendron, moss covered forests, suspensions metal bridges

Medication

  • Bandage for sprains
  • Plasters/Band-aids
  • Iodine or water filter (optional)
  • Moleskin/Second skin - for blisters
  • Antiseptic ointment for cuts
  • Anti-bacterial throat lozenges (with antiseptic)
  • Aspirin/paracetamol - general painkiller
  • Oral dehydration salts
  • Broad-spectrum antibiotic (norfloxacin or ciprofloxin)
  • Anti-diarrhea medication (antibiotic)
  • Diarrhea stopper (Imodium - optional)
  • Antibiotic for Giardia or similar microbe or bacteria
  • Diamox (altitude sickness - can be bought in Kathmandu)

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing / equipment for our trek to Upper Dolpo Trek

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket
  • Set lightweight thermals
  • North Face down Jacket (Preferably)
  • Small thin towel (sports towel best)
  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
  • Hat
  • Cotton or silk bag liner – optional
  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves
  • Rucksack
  • Pack tissues
  • Pair sunglasses
  • Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.
  • Camera and films
  • Head torch and spare batteries
  • Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) deg C during our trek)

Above things are required for Upper Dolpo trek. However if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.
Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, you will be warmly welcomed and transferred to your hotel. Enjoy a brief orientation about the trek and rest after your journey.
Sightseeing / Cultural Day In Kathmandu Valley

Explore the rich cultural heritage of Kathmandu Valley. Visit UNESCO World Heritage Sites including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, and Patan Durbar Square. Prepare for your upcoming trek in the evening.
Take a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, a vibrant city in western Nepal close to the Indian border. Overnight in Nepalgunj.
Fly from Nepalgunj to Jumla (2,370m), a remote and picturesque town in the highlands of western Nepal. Begin acclimatizing to the higher altitude.
Start trekking through lush forests and traditional villages to reach Gothi Chaur. Enjoy the beautiful landscape and gradual ascent.
Continue your trek through alpine meadows, passing by yak pastures and scattered settlements, eventually reaching Naphuknona.
Descend into the Bheri River Valley, following the scenic trail alongside the river. Take in the dramatic gorges and untouched wilderness.
Trek through traditional villages and diverse landscapes to reach Hurikot, a gateway to the Upper Dolpo region and Shey Phoksundo National Park.
Continue your journey deeper into the remote mountains, reaching the beautiful Garpung Khola valley where you’ll camp near the river.
We start the trek following the river upstream.
Begin the day by trekking upstream along the Garpung Khola. The trail winds through pristine valleys, offering breathtaking views and tranquil surroundings.

A big day crossing the Kagmara La (5100m). Taking a packed lunch, follow the Right Bank off the river for a short way until the path becomes slightly obscure below a steep climb. Reaching the top of this, the angle eases off slightly and the pass is no more than an hour and a half away. The pass is marked in the traditional Tibetan way with hundreds of prayer flags, and the view is quite stunning. The short climb to the summit of Kagmara RI (5370m) takes no more than half an hour, but the extra view is well worth it. The mountains of Tibet and Mount Everest in the distance form just part of this impressive panorama, which is dominated by the Dhaulagiri massif and the Annapurnas. The view to the south and west of the Kagmara Lekh and the Kanjiroba Himal is equally impressive. All in all a very special spot. There is no need to leave in a hurry, as the campsite is a mere hour below the pass on a flat grassy clearing by the river (3450m).

On our 1990 reconnaissance trip, Himalayan blue sheep and wild fox ware seen from the camp as well s numerous birds of pray. A big descent, over 1200 meters, leads through an idyllic valley to the village of Pungmo. Camp is made by the Choten the entrance to the village.

A rest day if you wish, but the spare day is to give everyone the chance to visit the important Gompa above Pungmo. There are in fact two Gompas as we have entered a region where both 'Bon' and 'traditional' Buddhism are practiced. Chotens become very confusing s one dictates an anti- clockwise passing whilst the other clockwise. However, the lams of both Gompas are willing to show you around for a small donation. To reach them, look out for a wooden bridge below the village. Cross this to the opposite bank of the river and follow the path up through the pine forest past a Choten. The path becomes quite exposed as it cuts across a cliff to reach the sanctuary

Today's destination is the village of Ringmo by the beautiful Phuksumdo Tal (lake). Keeping to the left side of the river, descend for one hour to a military camp (31d50m) at the junction of the Pungmo and Phuksumdo Rivers. Turns left immediately after the camp and follow a delightful path by the Phuksumdo River to a grassy clearing for lunch. The afternoon's walk up to Ringmo is very rewarding as huge rock walls guard the upper valley and it is not until some prayer flags are reached at 3800m that the lake can be seen. Equally impressive is the huge waterfall falling down from the Phuksumdo River. From the prayer flags, a pleasant half an hour's walk leads to the village of Ringmo and camp is made on the opposite side of the village (3700m). Crossing the bridge in the village and turn left to reach the lake.
A rest day in Ringmo camped by the beautiful clear waters of Ringmo Lake. The nearby monastery is worth a visit.

The final part of the trek sets out to explore the hidden valley of Tarap, one of the last bastions of Tibetan culture in Nepal. An easy day involving a couple of hours walks in the morning to a Yak grazing pasture by the Manduwa Khola. The path skirts along lodges hacked out of cliffs for the Yak caravans from Dolpo. The views down the Suli Gad and across to the Kagmara Lekh are particularly impressive. The campsite is in a lovely spot (3900m) below Kang Taiga (5916m).

Today is a very strenuous day crossing thee Basic Bhanjyang (Bagar La) (5200m). It is also one of the most fascination of the trek as we cross the watershed of the main Himalayan onto the dry Tibetan plateaus. Following the river to begin with, the path turns north up the first obvious side valley and climbs steeply to the pass, which marked by a choten and the usual prayer flags. The views to the east and north are one of complete contrast to those of the previous two weeks trekking. The mountain is orange and brown stretching out into Tibet to the north. The pass is often windy and the descent is party rapid to the river below and our camp (4650m). The road to shey and saldang is clearly etched out of the landscape by the tracks of thousands of Yaks that have made the journey south over the centuries the lifeline of Dolpo. At this point we are only three hours from the village of Shey, but access is not permitted.

The Tarap Valley is today's destination and despite the climb to the Numla La (5350m), the walk into this beautiful and wild Tibetan landscape is one of the highlights of the trek. A four to five hour climb leads to the pass and the view is indeed stunning. Dhaulagiri I am the prominent feature, with the rolling Tibetan hills and the Kanjiroba Himal to the west equally impressive. For an excellent 3600 panorama, climb the small peak to the left of the pass. The path descends gradually into the Tarap Valley. In two to three hours the Champa Gompa is passed on the left and camp is made a little further down the valley in the first village (4300m).

A long day. Due to the opens of the Tarap Valley, the sun hits the tent early, giving a spring feel to the morning. The mornings walk passes through the villages off Clumaga and Kakar, both extremely interesting with many Choten, again both Bun-Po (the ancient pre-Buddhistic religion) and Choba (orthodox Buddhist). There are two Gompas in Dho, Guru Bumba (Chob) and above the village Scipcha Gompa (Bon). Leaving Dho (a name given to the last village but actually meaning the upper collection of villages), the Tarap Khola is followed for two hours, at first on its left bank, to a bridge where lunch is taken. This is the last flat ground for three to four hours as the valley becomes narrow with deep goes crossed by innumerable small bridges. However, it is an extremely well made path, one of the finest gorge paths in the Himalayan, offering an entertaining afternoon's walk. A small campsite by a large campsite by a big cave.

The path through the gorge continues to impress, switching from the riverbank to way up the cliff side on some amazing constructions! After a long morning's walk (look out for Musk Deer), a large clearing by the river is reached. This is Lahini and marks the end of the gorge. The path Kanigaon (2700m) where we camp.

From the check post, head east for a few hundred yards to a well mad bridge which is crossed to the left bank of the Barbung Khola, into which the Trap Khola now flows. This river is followed for three hours to the village of Tarakot where we stop. Rest afternoon.
Another easy day, continuing along the Barbung Khola through a beautiful alpine valley to the Hindu village of Dunai. Four hours walking. Camp by the new 'Blue Sheep lodge'.

The final day's walk continues along the river to a tea shop by the side of the path (One and a half hours) which marks the start of the climb to the Juphal airstrip. The path climbs steadily, passing through the village of Juphal to the airstrip. Camp is made outside the RNAC office.
We take the flight to Nepalgunj, for an afternoon's rest before flying on to Kathmandu the following day. The views from the lake of the Annapurnas are famous throughout Nepal.

item.title: 6 days Tamang heritage trek
item.dc:creator: kabita

6 Days Tamang Heritage Trek Overview

The 6 Days Tamang Heritage Trek is a short and rewarding adventure in Nepal's beautiful Langtang region. This cultural trek takes you through traditional Tamang villages, scenic hills, and peaceful forests. Moreover, it offers a wonderful chance to experience authentic Himalayan culture without trekking to extreme altitudes. Therefore, it is an excellent choice for beginners, families, and travelers with limited time.

The journey begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi, the starting point of the trek. From there, you walk through charming villages such as Gatlang, Tatopani, Thuman, and Briddim. Along the way, you enjoy breathtaking mountain views, terraced farms, and lush rhododendron forests. In addition, the friendly Tamang people warmly welcome visitors and proudly share their traditions, culture, and daily lifestyle.

Experience Tamang Culture and Himalayan Beauty

One of the highlights of the trek is the opportunity to discover the rich heritage of the Tamang community. You can visit ancient monasteries, spin colorful prayer wheels, and explore villages influenced by Tibetan Buddhism. Furthermore, staying in local tea houses allows you to enjoy traditional meals and genuine hospitality.

Another memorable stop is Tatopani, where you can relax in natural hot springs after a rewarding day of hiking. Meanwhile, the surrounding landscapes provide stunning views of Langtang Lirung, Ganesh Himal, and other snow-covered peaks. Although the trek is relatively short, every day offers something unique and unforgettable.

The best seasons for the 6 Days Tamang Heritage Trek are spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). During these months, the weather is usually clear, and the mountain views are spectacular. However, the trek can also be enjoyed in winter by well-prepared travelers.

Overall, the 6 Days Tamang Heritage Trek combines natural beauty, local culture, and comfortable trekking into one unforgettable journey. Whether you are looking for cultural discovery, peaceful trails, or amazing Himalayan scenery, this trek promises a memorable experience in the heart of Nepal.

item.title: Langtang - Gosainkunda Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Langtang and Gosaikunda Trek

The Langtang Gosaikunda Trek is a rewarding Himalayan adventure that combines the natural beauty of Langtang Valley with the spiritual importance of the sacred Gosaikunda Lakes. This diverse journey takes you through peaceful forests, traditional Tamang villages, alpine landscapes, and dramatic mountain terrain. It is an excellent choice for trekkers who want to experience Nepal's scenery and culture beyond the more crowded Everest and Annapurna regions.

Explore Langtang Valley and Kyanjin Gompa

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi, the gateway to Langtang National Park. From there, the trail follows beautiful river valleys through dense forests filled with rhododendron, bamboo, and oak trees. Along the way, you will pass traditional Tamang settlements and experience the warm hospitality of local communities.

As the trail climbs higher, the landscape becomes increasingly spectacular. The journey leads to Kyanjin Gompa, an important cultural and spiritual center surrounded by impressive Himalayan peaks. From here, trekkers can enjoy panoramic views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Yala Peak, Gangchempo, and other snow-covered mountains.

Cross Lauribina Pass and Visit Gosaikunda

One of the most exciting sections of the journey is the crossing of Lauribina Pass at approximately 4,610 meters. The challenging ascent rewards trekkers with expansive mountain views and a remarkable high-altitude experience.

Beyond the pass lies Gosaikunda, a sacred alpine lake surrounded by rugged Himalayan landscapes. The lake holds great religious significance for Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims and creates a peaceful setting for trekkers. The combination of natural beauty and cultural importance makes this section one of the most memorable parts of the adventure.

Why Choose This Himalayan Adventure?

This trek is ideal for travelers looking for a combination of mountain scenery, cultural discovery, and challenging high-altitude trails. The route offers opportunities to explore traditional villages, interact with local communities, visit monasteries, and experience the changing landscapes of the Himalayas.

With comfortable teahouses, welcoming locals, and spectacular mountain views throughout the route, the Langtang Gosaikunda Trek provides an unforgettable experience for adventurous travelers. It is a perfect choice for those seeking a diverse Himalayan journey filled with nature, culture, and adventure.

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket
  • Set lightweight thermals
  • North Face down Jacket (Preferably)
  • Small thin towel (sports towel best)
  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
  • Hat
  • Cotton or silk bag liner – optional
  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves
  • Rucksack
  • Pack tissues
  • Pair sunglasses
  • Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.
  • Camera and films
  • Head torch and spare batteries
  • Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) deg C during our trek)

Above things are required for Langtang / Gosaikunda Trek. However if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.

item.title: Amadablam Base Camp Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek Overview

The Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek is one of Nepal's most scenic and rewarding trekking adventures. It takes you to the foot of the stunning Ama Dablam (6,812 m), one of the most beautiful mountains in the Himalayas. Although it is close to the Everest region, this trail is quieter than the Everest Base Camp Trek. Therefore, it is perfect for trekkers who want breathtaking mountain views and a peaceful experience.

The journey begins with a scenic flight to Lukla. From there, you follow traditional Sherpa trails through beautiful villages such as Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche, and Pangboche. Along the way, you cross suspension bridges, walk through rhododendron forests, and pass colorful prayer flags. Moreover, the route lies inside Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site rich in wildlife and natural beauty.

A Perfect Blend of Nature and Sherpa Culture

Besides spectacular scenery, the trek offers a unique cultural experience. You can visit ancient Buddhist monasteries, meet friendly Sherpa families, and learn about their traditions. In addition, comfortable tea houses provide warm hospitality and delicious local meals after each day's walk.

As you gain altitude, the views become even more impressive. You will enjoy panoramic sights of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Thamserku, Kangtega, and many other Himalayan peaks. Finally, reaching Ama Dablam Base Camp at 4,570 meters is the highlight of the trek. Standing beneath the towering mountain is an unforgettable experience.

The best seasons for the Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek are spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). During these months, the weather is usually stable, the skies are clear, and the mountain views are outstanding. However, good physical fitness is still important because the trail involves several days of walking at higher elevations.

Overall, the Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek is an excellent choice for travelers seeking incredible mountain scenery, rich Sherpa culture, and a less crowded Himalayan adventure. Whether you are an experienced trekker or an active beginner, this journey promises lasting memories and an authentic Everest region experience.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
The Trail Conditions

Straight, Up hill, Down hill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, muddy, some where dusty, man made stone steps, through the moss covered forests, Rocky glacier or If snows, snowy path crossing suspensions metal bridges and wooden bridges over the rivers

High Altitude Sickness:

Often times treks that ascend beyond 3500 m would require more days for acclimatization to ensure that trekkers do not suffer from high altitude sickness. The thinner air affects you in many ways and if you go high too fast there is a high chance to get affected.

Insurances of Guide and Porters

We do our Trekking insurance for the duration of 10 or 15 years from reputed insurance company in Kathmandu, Nepal which covers our insurance for the duration of our trek as well. On the other hand we (Hike Nepal) are a member of TAAN (Trekking Agent Association of Nepal) TAAN takes fully responsible for the staff of its members while we are on the trek. You are highly recommended to be insured for this trek from your country.

We, Nepalese eat a meal of Dhal Bhaat (rice with lentil soup, curry, and pickles) twice daily. The ingredients vary according to local and seasonal availability, but vegetarian options are the norm. Another cheap popular local dish is the ubiquitous instant noodle soup, enhanced by local vegetables, or meat or egg, depending on availability. Eating Nepali-style will provide you with truly local experience, guarantees fresh ingredients everywhere, and rules out disappointments.

Also, in all lodges tourists will be served their meals in the lodge dining room before the Nepali staff gets their meals in the kitchen or another place where guides and porters relax. And staff members' quarters are separate from the tourist rooms. This seemingly two-class system may be a difficult concept for some tourists, but it can also be seen as "time off" for the staff members. Nepalese eat mostly with their hands, a custom that is considered offensive by some tourists another reason why the staff members may actually prefer to eat separately.

Medication 

  • Bandage for sprains
  • Plasters/Band-aids
  • Iodine or water filter (optional)
  • Moleskin/Second skin - for blisters
  • Antiseptic ointment for cuts
  • Anti-bacterial throat lozenges (with antiseptic)
  • Aspirin/paracetamol - general painkiller
  • Oral rehydration salts
  • Broad-spectrum antibiotic (norfloxacin or ciprofloxacin)
  • Anti-diarrhea medication (antibiotic)
  • Diarrhea stopper (Imodium - optional)
  • Antibiotic for Giardia or similar microbe or bacteria
  • Diamox (altitude sickness - can be bought in Kathmandu)

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing/equipment for our trek to Everest Base Camp Trek

-Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent

-Pair lightweight trekking sandals

-Pairs thin walking socks

-Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants

-T-shirts

-Fleece Jacket

-Set lightweight thermals

-North Face down Jacket (Preferably)

-Small thin towel (sports towel best)
-Soap
-Shampoo
-Sunscreen
-Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
-Hat
-Cotton or silk bag liner - optional
-Neck warmer

-Pairs 'thinners' gloves

-Rucksack

-Pack tissues

-Pair sunglasses

-Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.

-Camera and films

-Head torch and spare batteries

-Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) DC during our trek )

The above things are required for Everest Base Camp. However, if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.

item.title: Everest Three Pass Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Everest Three Pass Trek – The Ultimate Himalayan Challenge Three Pass Trek is the ultimate trekking adventure in Nepal's Khumbu region. It is designed for experienced hikers who want to experience the complete variety of terrains in the Everest sanctuary. Because it loops through high mountain passes and glacier valleys, this challenging multi-day expedition remains an absolute favorite for elite travelers seeking deep solitude and raw alpine wilderness.
Conquer the Three Giant Mountain Passes
Your mountain journey begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla before following the trails into Sagarmatha National Park. Unlike standard base camp routes, this challenging circuit takes you over three massive high-altitude passes: Kongma La (5,535m), Cho La (5,420m), and Renjo La (5,360m). Along the way, staying in cozy local teahouses allows you to experience authentic Sherpa hospitality firsthand while resting after demanding trekking days.
Discover Pristine Glaciers and Sacred Lakes
Arriving at the high points of the Everest Three Pass Trek provides unparalleled close-up views of giant peaks, including Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Makalu. Additionally, the route navigates through the dramatic Ngozumpa Glacier and passes along the beautiful, emerald-blue Gokyo Lakes. The challenging alpine paths allow for a thorough exploration of the entire region, making it a highly rewarding expedition for passionate high-altitude hikers.
Why Choose This Legendary Wilderness Circuit?
Opting for the Everest Three Pass Trek offers the perfect mix of dramatic high-mountain landscapes, deep cultural discovery, and raw physical challenge. It serves as an ideal choice for hikers who want a complete Himalayan holiday away from the standard crowded trails. Ultimately, this unforgettable journey delivers incredible photography opportunities, profound isolation, and a deep appreciation for the world's highest mountains.

item.title: Annapurna Panorama Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Annapurna Panorama Trek Overview

Annapurna Panorama Trek is one of the most rewarding short trekking adventures in Nepal. It combines spectacular Himalayan scenery, traditional mountain villages, and rich local culture in the famous Annapurna region. Moreover, the trail is suitable for beginners, families, and experienced trekkers. Therefore, it is an excellent choice for anyone who wants an authentic Himalayan experience without reaching extreme altitudes.

The journey begins with a scenic drive from Pokhara before following well-maintained trails through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and charming Gurung and Magar villages. Along the way, you cross suspension bridges, enjoy peaceful surroundings, and stay in comfortable tea houses. In addition, friendly local people warmly welcome visitors and share their traditions, making the trek even more memorable.

Highlights of the Journey

The biggest highlight is the early morning hike to the famous Poon Hill viewpoint. From the top, you can watch a breathtaking sunrise over Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Dhaulagiri, Nilgiri, and Hiunchuli. Furthermore, the golden light on the snow-covered peaks creates unforgettable views. As a result, this viewpoint is one of the most photographed locations in Nepal.

Meanwhile, the trail continues through beautiful villages where you can experience local culture, taste traditional Nepali food, and learn about everyday mountain life. Likewise, the peaceful forests and colorful landscapes make every day enjoyable. Although the trek is relatively easy, it offers impressive scenery throughout the journey.

Best Time to Visit

Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the best seasons for the Annapurna Panorama Trek. During these months, the weather is usually clear, and the mountain views are outstanding. However, winter also offers peaceful trails and beautiful snow-covered landscapes for well-prepared trekkers.

Overall, this trek is perfect for travelers looking for breathtaking mountain views, authentic village life, and a memorable Himalayan adventure. Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or returning to explore more of the Annapurna region, Annapurna Panorama Trek promises an unforgettable experience.
