item.title: Ghandruk Trekking
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Ghandruk Trekking Overview

Ghandruk Trekking is one of the most popular short treks in Nepal. It takes you to the beautiful Gurung village of Ghandruk at 1,940 meters in the Annapurna region. Moreover, the trek offers breathtaking mountain views, rich local culture, and peaceful walking trails. Therefore, it is an excellent choice for beginners, families, and anyone with limited time.

The journey starts with a scenic drive from Pokhara to Nayapul or Kimche. From there, you follow easy trails through terraced fields, rhododendron forests, and traditional villages. Along the way, you cross suspension bridges and enjoy fresh mountain air. In addition, friendly tea houses provide comfortable accommodation and delicious local meals.

Furthermore, every day rewards you with spectacular views of Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna. As a result, the trek remains enjoyable from beginning to end.

Experience Gurung Culture

One of the highlights of Ghandruk Trekking is visiting the traditional Gurung village. Here, you can explore stone-paved streets, traditional houses, and ancient monasteries. Moreover, you can visit the Gurung Museum and learn about local history and customs.

Meanwhile, local families warmly welcome visitors into their community. Consequently, you experience authentic Himalayan hospitality throughout the trek. Likewise, the peaceful surroundings create a relaxing atmosphere after each day of walking.

Scenic Mountain Views

Besides its rich culture, Ghandruk Trekking is famous for its outstanding scenery. During spring, colorful rhododendron forests bloom across the hillsides. Similarly, autumn brings crystal-clear skies and excellent mountain visibility. However, winter also offers beautiful snow-covered landscapes and quieter trails.

In addition, photographers enjoy countless opportunities to capture sunrise and sunset over the Annapurna range. Therefore, every season has its own unique charm.

Best Time for Ghandruk Trekking

Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the best seasons for Ghandruk Trekking. During these months, the weather is usually stable and comfortable. Furthermore, mountain views are at their best. However, proper trekking gear is important in every season.

Finally, Ghandruk Trekking combines stunning Himalayan scenery, authentic Gurung culture, comfortable tea houses, and peaceful trails into one unforgettable adventure. Overall, it is one of the finest short treks in Nepal and an excellent choice for travelers of all experience levels.

item.title: Ghorepani Ghandruk trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek Overview

The Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek is one of the most popular short treks in Nepal. It offers spectacular mountain views, charming Gurung and Magar villages, and beautiful rhododendron forests. Moreover, the trek is suitable for beginners, families, and experienced trekkers. Therefore, it is an excellent choice for anyone who wants to explore the Annapurna region in a short time.

The journey begins with a scenic drive from Pokhara to Nayapul or Ulleri. From there, the trail passes through peaceful forests, stone staircases, rivers, and traditional mountain villages. Along the way, you enjoy warm local hospitality and comfortable tea houses. In addition, every day offers breathtaking views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks.

Sunrise at Poon Hill and Local Culture

One of the biggest highlights of the Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek is the early morning hike to Poon Hill (3,210 m). From the viewpoint, you can watch a spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges. Furthermore, you enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Hiunchuli, Nilgiri, and many other snow-covered peaks. As a result, Poon Hill is one of Nepal's most famous viewpoints.

After visiting Poon Hill, the trail continues to the beautiful village of Ghandruk. Meanwhile, you can explore traditional stone houses, ancient monasteries, and the local Gurung Museum. Moreover, you have the opportunity to learn about Gurung culture, customs, and daily life while enjoying genuine Himalayan hospitality.

Best Time for the Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek

Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the best seasons for the Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek. During spring, colorful rhododendron forests bloom across the hills. Likewise, autumn offers clear skies and excellent mountain views. However, this trek is also enjoyable during winter because the trails remain accessible.

Overall, the Ghorepani Ghandruk Trek combines stunning Himalayan scenery, rich local culture, peaceful forests, and unforgettable sunrise views. Whether you are trekking in Nepal for the first time or returning for another adventure, this journey offers an unforgettable experience in the Annapurna region.

item.title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek - 12 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Annapurna Base Camp Trek – 12 Days Itinerary
The Annapurna Base Camp Trek is one of Nepal's most legendary and popular classic walking adventures. This stunning route brings you deep into the spectacular Annapurna Sanctuary, offering an immersive journey surrounded by giant Himalayan peaks. Because of its incredible variety of terrains, this classic multi-day expedition remains an absolute favorite for travelers worldwide who dream of standing at the foot of massive mountains.
What to Expect on the Annapurna Base Camp Trek
Your expedition begins with a scenic drive from Pokhara to the trailhead, quickly leading into beautiful rhododendron forests and traditional Gurung villages. As you ascend toward the base camp, the lush green hills slowly transform into a rugged alpine landscape. Along the way, staying in cozy local teahouses allows you to experience warm Nepalese hospitality firsthand while enjoying spectacular daily mountain views.
Reaching the Spectacular Annapurna Sanctuary
Arriving at the final destination provides an unparalleled 360-degree panorama of majestic peaks, including Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machapuchare (Fishtail), and Hiunchuli. Watching the morning sun rise over these ice-capped walls is an unforgettable highlight of the adventure. Additionally, the itinerary allows for safe acclimatization, making the high-altitude route accessible and enjoyable for average hikers.
Why Choose This Iconic 12-Day Journey?
The Annapurna Base Camp Trek offers the perfect mix of dramatic high-mountain landscapes, deep cultural immersion, and accessible trails. Not only do you walk through diverse ecological zones, but you also challenge yourself in a safe, guided setting. Ultimately, this unforgettable Himalayan holiday delivers incredible memories, stunning photography opportunities, and a deep appreciation for mountain life.

item.title: Everest Ponarama trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Everest Panorama Trek – The Perfect Himalayan Experience

The Everest Panorama Trek is the perfect choice for travelers who want to experience the beauty of the Everest region without trekking to Everest Base Camp. Unlike longer high-altitude expeditions, this journey combines breathtaking mountain scenery, authentic Sherpa culture, and comfortable trekking days. As a result, it is ideal for families, beginners, and anyone with limited time who still dreams of seeing Mount Everest.

Explore Sherpa Villages and Scenic Trails

The Everest Panorama Trek begins with a spectacular mountain flight from Kathmandu to Lukla before following scenic trails through Sagarmatha National Park. Along the way, you cross suspension bridges, walk through rhododendron and pine forests, and visit traditional Sherpa villages such as Phakding and Namche Bazaar. Furthermore, friendly local hospitality and centuries-old monasteries provide a fascinating cultural experience. In addition, every day offers incredible views of snow-covered Himalayan peaks.

Enjoy Incredible Everest Mountain Views

One of the highlights of the Everest Panorama Trek is the hike to the famous Everest View Hotel, one of the world's highest hotels. From here, trekkers enjoy unforgettable panoramic views of Mount Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Thamserku, and many other Himalayan giants. Meanwhile, the gradual ascent allows proper acclimatization, making the trek safer and more enjoyable. Consequently, you can appreciate the spectacular scenery while reducing the risk of altitude sickness.

Why Choose the Everest Panorama Trek?

The Everest Panorama Trek offers the perfect balance of adventure, culture, and natural beauty. Not only does it showcase some of the world's most famous mountains, but it also introduces you to the unique traditions of the Sherpa people. Additionally, the shorter itinerary makes it suitable for travelers with limited holiday time. Ultimately, the Everest Panorama Trek delivers an unforgettable Himalayan experience filled with stunning landscapes, rich culture, and lifelong memories.

The trail is relatively gentle and allows your body to gradually adjust to the altitude before reaching the village of Phakding.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Lukla (2840m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"Phakding (2610m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:35:"35 minute flight + 3–4 hours trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"Approx. 8 km trek";s:14:"important_note";s:232:"Flights to Lukla depend on weather conditions and may be delayed. After entering Sagarmatha National Park, the trail gradually climbs through forests of pine and rhododendron. The final ascent to Namche Bazaar is steep but rewarding, offering your first views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks. Namche Bazaar is the vibrant Sherpa capital of the Everest region.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Phakding (2610m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:21:"Namche Bazaar (3440m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:16:"6–7 hours trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:13:"Approx. 11 km";s:14:"important_note";s:194:"The final climb to Namche Bazaar is challenging. Drink plenty of water and watch for early signs of altitude sickness such as headache or fatigue.";}s:6:"item-3";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:62:"Day 4: Hike to Khumjung (3780m) via Hotel Everest View (3880m)";s:11:"description";s:389:"This day is planned for acclimatization while enjoying spectacular mountain views. Gradual climbs and descents lead back to Lukla, where the trekking journey concludes. In the evening, many trekkers celebrate the successful completion of their adventure with their guides and porters.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Monjo (2835m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:13:"Lukla (2840m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:13:"Approx. 13 km";s:14:"important_note";s:192:"Confirm your flight schedule for the next morning and pack your bags early. Keep essential items and documents in your hand luggage.";}s:6:"item-8";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:28:"Day 9: Depart from Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:327:"After breakfast, our team will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport for your international departure flight. This marks the end of your unforgettable trekking journey in Nepal. As you leave, you carry memories of spectacular mountain landscapes, Sherpa culture, and one of the world’s most famous trekking regions.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Kathmandu Hotel";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:31:"Tribhuvan International Airport";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:21:"30–45 minutes drive";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"Airport transfer";s:14:"important_note";s:177:"Please arrive at the airport at least three hours before your international flight. item.title: 6-Day Annapurna Base Camp Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Annapurna Base Camp Trek

The 6-Day Annapurna Base Camp Trek is an ideal Himalayan adventure for travelers who want to experience the beauty of Nepal in a limited amount of time. This short journey combines spectacular mountain scenery, traditional villages, peaceful forests, and unforgettable trekking experiences. Despite its compact itinerary, the route takes you deep into the Annapurna Sanctuary and close to some of the region’s most impressive peaks.

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Pokhara to Jhinu Danda, where the walking journey starts. From there, the trail passes through charming Gurung and Magar villages, lush rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and rushing mountain streams. Along the way, welcoming teahouses provide comfortable accommodation, traditional meals, and an opportunity to experience local hospitality.

Scenic Trails and Local Culture

As the trail gains elevation, the landscape gradually changes from green valleys and forests to dramatic alpine terrain. The surrounding mountains become increasingly impressive, creating beautiful views throughout the journey. The peaceful villages and traditional lifestyles along the route also provide a genuine glimpse into life in the Himalayan foothills.

The trail eventually enters the Annapurna Sanctuary, a spectacular natural amphitheater surrounded by towering peaks. Fresh mountain air, quiet trails, and panoramic scenery make this section particularly rewarding.

Reach Annapurna Base Camp

The ultimate destination is Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 meters. From the base camp, trekkers can enjoy magnificent views of Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna.

Early morning is one of the most memorable times to be there, as the first sunlight illuminates the surrounding snow-covered peaks. Standing beneath these enormous mountains creates an unforgettable Himalayan experience.

Why Choose This Trek?

This short Himalayan adventure is suitable for travelers with a reasonable level of fitness who want to explore the mountains without spending several weeks on the trail. Established paths, teahouse accommodation, beautiful scenery, and cultural encounters make the journey both convenient and rewarding.

For travelers looking for a short Annapurna trekking experience, this route offers an excellent combination of mountain views, local culture, and adventure within just six days.

• Scenic drive from Pokhara to Jhinu, followed by a beautiful trek into the Annapurna region

  • Reach Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 meters) surrounded by stunning Himalayan peaks

  • Enjoy close views of Annapurna I, Machapuchhre (Fishtail), Hiunchuli, and Annapurna South

  • Experience traditional Gurung and Magar villages, including the famous Chhomrong village

  • Walk through lush forests filled with bamboo, waterfalls, and rhododendron trees

  • Explore the peaceful and breathtaking Annapurna Sanctuary glacial valley

  • Witness unforgettable sunrise and sunset views over snow-covered mountains

  • Stay in traditional mountain teahouses and experience local hospitality

  • Opportunity to see wildlife such as langur monkeys, Himalayan thar, and colorful birds

  • Short and rewarding trek suitable for trekkers with limited time but big Himalayan dreams

  • Experience a complete journey from green hills to high alpine mountain landscapes in just six days

• Authorized English-speaking/local Expert Trekking Guide x1 during trek
  • Hotel pickup and drop-off
  • Road permits, all necessary paperwork, ACAP, and Trekkers' Information Management System fee(s)
  • All applicable government tax
  • Accommodation x4 nights during the trek
  • All meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) during the trek
  • Private Transportation by 4 wheel drive jeep from Pokhara to Samrung and Jhinu Hot Spring to Pokhara as
    per the itinerary.
  • All expenses for the guide/porter; meals, accommodation, salary, equipment, insurance, and
    transportation.

• Soft and hard drinks
  • Travel and rescue insurance
  • International flights; Nepalese visa fee
  • Tips for guide(s), porter(s) and driver(s)
  • Personal expenses (phone calls, laundry, bar bills, battery recharge, extra porters, bottle or boiled water,
    shower, etc.)
  • Extra night accommodation in Pokhara because of early arrival, late departure, or early return from the
    trip due to any reason other than the scheduled itinerary
Pokhara – Samrung – Sinuwa (2,200m / 7,218ft) (3 hrs Jeep, 4 hrs trek)

Start your journey early from Lakeside, Pokhara, taking a scenic jeep ride to Samrung via Nayapul (approx. 3 hours). Enjoy breathtaking views of the Seti River, Modi River, rolling green hills, and traditional villages along the way. From Samrung, begin your trek toward Sinuwa, a peaceful village surrounded by lush forests and stunning mountain vistas. The trek takes around 4 hours, with gentle ascents through terraced fields and charming settlements. Experience the warmth of local hospitality as you settle in for the night in a cozy teahouse in Sinuwa.

Today’s journey takes you deeper into the Himalayas as you trek from Sinuwa to Deurali. The trail winds through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests, offering glimpses of snow-capped peaks along the way. As you ascend, the air gets cooler, and the landscapes become more rugged and dramatic. After 7 hours of trekking, arrive at Deurali, a serene village nestled beneath towering cliffs. Relax and recharge for the next day's exciting adventure to Annapurna Base Camp. You’ll be staying in a cozy teahouse in Deurali for the night.
Deurali – Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m / 13,550ft) (6 hrs trek)

Embark on the most thrilling day of the trek as you make your way from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC). The trail ascends gradually, leading you past glacial moraines and high-altitude landscapes. After 5 hours of trekking, you’ll reach the legendary Annapurna Base Camp, surrounded by towering peaks and pristine glaciers. Marvel at the panoramic views of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and Hiunchuli. Spend the night at Annapurna Base Camp itself, soaking in the beauty of the Himalayas under a starry sky.
Annapurna Base Camp – Lower Sinuwa (2,200m / 7,218ft) (8 hrs trek

Wake up early to witness a spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna Massif before beginning your descent. Retrace your steps back through Deurali and Bamboo, passing through diverse landscapes of alpine meadows and dense forests. The trek to Lower Sinuwa takes around 8 hours, offering plenty of time to reflect on your incredible journey. Enjoy a well-earned rest in a cozy teahouse, surrounded by the tranquil beauty of the region
Lower Sinuwa – Jhinu Dada Hot Springs – Pokhara (4 hrs trek, 3 hrs drive)

On the final day, descend from Lower Sinuwa to Jhinu Dada (4 hours of trekking). Treat yourself to a relaxing dip in the natural hot springs, soothing your tired muscles and celebrating your trekking achievement. Afterward, take a 3-hour jeep ride back to Lakeside, Pokhara, enjoying the scenic drive through picturesque villages and lush hills. Arrive in Pokhara with unforgettable memories, a deep appreciation for the Annapurna region, and a sense of accomplishment from your adventure. On the way, reflect on the incredible experiences, stunning landscapes, and the sense of achievement you've gained throughout the journey

item.title: Annapurna Circuit Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Annapurna Circuit Trek Overview

The Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of Nepal’s most diverse Himalayan adventures, taking travelers through lush forests, peaceful mountain villages, alpine valleys, and dramatic high-altitude landscapes. The route offers an incredible combination of natural beauty, local culture, and exciting mountain experiences.

From the lower valleys to the high Himalayan passes, the scenery changes throughout the journey. Trekkers can enjoy terraced fields, rhododendron forests, traditional settlements, rocky landscapes, and spectacular views of snow-covered peaks. The gradual change in altitude also allows time to experience different environments and communities along the way.

Highlights of the Annapurna Region

The trail passes through communities influenced by Gurung, Manang, and Thakali cultures. Travelers can experience traditional village life, local food, mountain hospitality, and historic religious sites. These cultural encounters add depth to the adventure and provide a closer look at life in the Himalayas.

The route also offers impressive views of Annapurna II, Annapurna III, Gangapurna, Tilicho Peak, Chulu Peaks, and Pisang Peak. Each section of the journey provides a different perspective of the surrounding mountains.

Crossing Thorong La Pass

One of the most memorable parts of the journey is crossing Thorong La Pass at 5,416 meters. The climb requires proper preparation and acclimatization, particularly around Manang. Reaching the pass is a rewarding achievement, with panoramic Himalayan views making the effort worthwhile.

After crossing the pass, the trail descends toward Muktinath and continues through the dramatic Kali Gandaki region. The changing terrain makes the route exciting from beginning to end.

Why Choose This Himalayan Adventure?

This trek is an excellent choice for travelers looking for a combination of mountain scenery, cultural discovery, and outdoor adventure. Comfortable teahouses, welcoming local communities, and experienced trekking support make the experience more enjoyable.

Whether you are an experienced trekker or planning your first major Himalayan journey, the Annapurna Circuit offers an unforgettable way to explore Nepal’s spectacular mountain landscapes.

• Cross Thorong La Pass (5,416m), one of the highest trekking passes in the world

• Experience dramatic landscape changes from green hills to high alpine desert

• Enjoy breathtaking views of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Tilicho Peak

• Explore beautiful mountain villages like Chame, Pisang, and Manang

• Visit the sacred temple of Muktinath, important for both Hindus and Buddhists

• Walk through the Kali Gandaki Gorge, the deepest gorge in the world

• Discover unique culture influenced by Tibetan and Himalayan traditions

• Visit Manang village, one of the most scenic and important acclimatization stops

• Relax in natural hot springs at Tatopani

• Experience peaceful monasteries, prayer flags, and traditional mountain lifestyle

• Walk through diverse forests of pine, oak, and rhododendron

• Suitable for trekkers seeking a complete and diverse Himalayan adventure

• Airport pick-up and drop-off by private vehicle

• Standard hotel accommodation in Kathmandu with breakfast (as per itinerary)

• Tourist bus or private vehicle transportation (Kathmandu to trek starting point and trek ending point to Kathmandu/Pokhara as per itinerary)

• Domestic flights if required by itinerary (if applicable, optional upgrade)

• Accommodation in comfortable teahouses during the trek

• Three meals a day during the trek (Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner)

• Experienced, licensed, and English-speaking trekking guide

• Necessary number of porters (1 porter for 2 trekkers), including their salary, insurance, food, and accommodation

• Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)

• Trekkers’ Information Management System (TIMS) card

• All government taxes and official service charges

• First aid kit carried by the guide

• Assistance for emergency rescue arrangement (rescue cost covered by your travel insurance)

• International airfare to and from Nepal

• Nepal entry visa fees and visa extension costs

• Travel insurance (must include high-altitude trekking and emergency evacuation coverage)

• Lunch and dinner in Kathmandu and Pokhara

• Personal trekking equipment and gear (such as boots, jackets, gloves, etc.)

• Personal expenses such as hot shower, Wi-Fi, charging, telephone, laundry, and drinks

• All kinds of beverages including tea, coffee, soft drinks, bottled water, and alcoholic drinks during the trek

• Porter service beyond the standard package allowance

• Tips for guide and porter (expected and appreciated)

• Extra accommodation and meals due to flight delay, early return, or personal reasons

• Costs arising from natural disasters, weather conditions, strikes, or other unforeseen circumstances

• Any expenses not mentioned in the “Package Include” section
Pokhara/Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani(1800m/5,905 ft) (8/9 hrs drive)
You'll be driven from Pokhara/Kathmandu to Besisahar on a bus and then you'll be continuing your journey toward Dharapani on a shared Jeep enjoying the scenic journey.
Dharapani to Chame (2,670m/8,760 ft)(10 hrs drive) (6 hrs trek)

You'll then be trekking up in the mountains from Dharapani until reaching Chame enjoying the beauty of the himalayan range. This is just the beginning of the trek. You’ll be staying overnight at teahouse at Chame.
Chame to Upper Pisang (3,300m/10,826 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Chame to Upper Pisang, a picturesque village with stunning mountain views. You'll explore and immerse yourself in the local culture
Upper Pisang to Ngawal (3,700m/12,140 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll continue the trek to Ngawal, a beautiful village nestled in a hillside. The breathtaking views of Annapurna II, Annapurna III, and Gangapurna mountains and valleys will mesmerize you.
Ngawal to Manang(3540m/11,614 ft)(Acclimatization Day)(2 hrs trek)

You'll trek to Manang after exploring the cave nearby Ngawal and take a day to rest and acclimatize to the higher altitude in Manang. You will explore the village and enjoy the panoramic mountain views.
Manang to Yak Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. You'll prepare for the challenging pass-crossing the next day. Overnight stay in Thorong Phedi..
Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi (4,450m/14,600 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. You'll prepare for the challenging pass-crossing the next day. Overnight stay in Thorong Phedi.
Thorong Phedi to Muktinath (3,800m/12,467 ft) via Thorong La Pass (5,416m/17,769 ft)(12 hrs trek)

You'll start early in the morning for the challenging but rewarding ascent to Thorong La Pass. You'll experience the thrill of crossing the high mountain pass and enjoy panoramic views. You'll descend to Muktinath temple, a sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and explore the scenic village. Overnight stay in Muktinath..
Muktinath to Jomsom (2,720m/8,923 ft)(5 hrs trek)

You'll descend further to Jomsom, a windy town in the Mustang region. You'll witness the dramatic change in landscapes as you enter the arid and desert-like terrain and explore the town. Overnight stay in Jomsom.

You'll take a bus from Jomsom to Pokhara, enjoying views of the mountains. You'll relax and unwind in Pokhara, reflecting on the incredible journey you've completed. Congratulation! You've accomplished your dream adventure.

Clothing

• Moisture-wicking base layer (top and bottom)
• Warm fleece or insulated jacket
• Down jacket (for cold and high altitude)
• Waterproof and windproof outer jacket
• Trekking pants (2–3 pairs)
• Thermal innerwear
• Warm hat or beanie
• Sun hat or cap
• Warm gloves and inner gloves
• Wool or trekking socks (3–5 pairs)
• Comfortable underwear

Footwear

• Good quality waterproof trekking boots
• Lightweight shoes or sandals (for teahouse use)
• Gaiters (optional, useful for snow and dust)

Bags

• Daypack (20–30 liters)
• Duffel bag (carried by porter)
• Rain cover for backpack
• Dry bags or plastic bags (to keep items dry)

Sleeping Gear

• Sleeping bag (rated for cold temperatures)
• Sleeping bag liner (optional for extra warmth)

Trekking Equipment

• Trekking poles
• Sunglasses with UV protection
• Headlamp or flashlight with extra batteries
• Water bottles or hydration bladder
• Water purification tablets or filter

Personal Items

• Sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher)
• Lip balm with SPF
• Personal toiletries
• Quick-dry towel
• Hand sanitizer
• Wet wipes and tissue paper

Medical and First Aid

• Personal medications
• Basic first aid kit
• Blister treatment
• Pain relief tablets
• Altitude sickness prevention medicine (consult doctor)

Documents and Miscellaneous

• Passport and permits
• Travel insurance copy
• Cash (local currency)

item.title: 6-Day Langtang valley Treks
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover a Short Himalayan Adventure

The 6-Day Langtang Valley Trek is a rewarding journey through one of Nepal’s most beautiful mountain regions. Located north of Kathmandu, this route combines dramatic Himalayan scenery, peaceful forests, traditional villages, and welcoming teahouses. It is an excellent choice for travelers who want an authentic mountain experience within a limited timeframe.

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi, the gateway to the valley. From there, the trail follows the Langtang River through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests. Along the way, trekkers cross suspension bridges, pass waterfalls, and walk through traditional Tamang settlements surrounded by impressive mountain landscapes.

Stunning Mountain Views

A major highlight is reaching Kyanjin Gompa, a peaceful settlement surrounded by spectacular Himalayan peaks. From here, trekkers can hike toward Kyanjin Ri at 4,773 meters for panoramic views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Gangchempo, Yala Peak, Langshisa Ri, and other snow-covered mountains.

The early morning scenery is particularly impressive, with sunlight illuminating the surrounding peaks. The viewpoint also provides excellent opportunities for photography and quiet moments in the mountains.

Experience Tamang Culture

The journey offers more than beautiful landscapes. Travelers can experience the traditions and hospitality of local Tamang communities while staying in family-run teahouses and enjoying traditional Nepalese meals. The route passes through villages that reflect the resilience of local communities and their strong connection to the Himalayan environment.

A Perfect Short Trek in Nepal

With manageable walking days and well-established trails, this adventure is suitable for both beginners and experienced hikers with a reasonable level of fitness. The gradual change in altitude also allows trekkers to enjoy the scenery and cultural experiences along the way.

For travelers seeking spectacular mountain views, peaceful trails, local culture, and an authentic Himalayan experience, this Langtang Valley trek offers an unforgettable six-day adventure.

• Weather Conditions: Be prepared for rapidly changing weather. Dress in layers, as the temperature can vary significantly between day and night. Also put waterproof gear for unexpected rain.
  • Road Conditions: The roads can be rough and dusty, so ensure your Scorpio Jeep is in good condition.
  • Difficulty Levels: Our trips include challenging ascents and descents. Ensure you're in good physical condition.
  • Altitude Awareness: Gradual acclimatization is crucial. Follow our guides’ advice to avoid altitude sickness.
  • Proper Gear: Wear sturdy, comfortable boots or shoes and bring essentials like a hat, sunscreen, and a first-aid kit. Tips for the Trip:
  • Local Culture: Respect local customs and communities. Your journey will take you through diverse cultural regions.

We will begin our journey with a morning drive right after breakfast that will lead you to Syabrubesi. The bus journey follows a winding route, navigating both uphill and downhill roads, passing through various rural towns and farming villages. Along the way, you will encounter Trisuli Bazaar, a larger town situated in the sub-tropical zone in Nuwakot district. As the road ascends further, transitioning into a cooler region, the landscape changes from rice paddies to terraced fields of maize and millet. With these changes in weather and environment come shifts in culture and people as well. Eventually, you will arrive at Dhunche (1,965 m.), which serves as the primary town of both the Langtang area and Rasuwa district. Here lies Langtang National Park headquarters where your trekking permits are thoroughly checked by park wardens from the Royal Nepalese Army who are responsible for overseeing this protected area. Continuing your journey downhill for approximately 1-2 hours brings you to Syabrubesi village where we will stay for the night.
Syabrubesi - Bamboo - Lama Hotel (6 hrs trek)

The journey from Syabrubeshi is quite enjoyable, with a few uphill sections. However, the majority of the hike takes place on a relatively flat trail that passes through terraced farm fields and villages. Eventually, the trail descends and merges with another path that originates from upper Syabru at the Riverside Lodge. From there, you continue along a path that leads into a refreshing forest within the gorge, following alongside the rushing Trisuli River. The trek mainly consists of climbing uphill in the pleasant shade of rhododendron and oak forests. After approximately six hours of hiking, you reach a small clearing where Lama Hotel is situated. You will spend overnight at Teahouse/Lodge accommodations
Lama Hotel - Langtang Village (6 hrs trek)

Starting from Lama Hotel, a morning hike of 2-3 hours will take you to Ghoda btable. Ghodatabela is situated in the midst of a forest filled with pine, hemlock, and rhododendron trees. As you continue on this trail, you will begin to notice the effects of increasing altitude. In Nepali language, Ghoda tabela means "horse stable." In the past, people from Langtang and even as far as Kathmandu used to trade with Tibet by bringing Tibetan ponies to this town. Ghoda tabela was an ideal place for cattle and horses to graze. Upon reaching Ghoda tabela, there is a lodge and a park warden's barrack where your permit will be checked once again. From here onward, the trek continues for a few more hours along the trail leading to Langtang and its picturesque valley. For about an hour after leaving Ghoda tabela behind, you walk through refreshing shade provided by alpine woods while following a small stream. As you ascend uphill for another hour or so before reaching Langtang village itself via gentle winding trails that have occasional ups and downs.

Starting from Mundu, the morning stroll takes you along a flat path for a brief period before gradually ascending through thorny blueberry and alpine bushes. Along the way, you will come across a Mani prayer wall that should be circumvented in a clockwise direction, adhering to local customs and beliefs. As you continue eastward, the valley opens up and reveals a grassy meadow offering breathtaking views of numerous snowcovered peaks in the distance. The journey becomes more enjoyable but may feel more challenging due to the gain in altitude as you approach Kyanjin Gompa for your overnight stay. Situated amidst picturesque surroundings, Kyanjin Gompa is adorned with towering peaks visible from all directions. Among them is Langtang Lirung, reaching an impressive height of over 7,000 meters with its icefall not too far from the village. Perched on top of a ridge created by glacial debris consisting of rocks and boulders lies Kyanjin Gompa monastery—a small sanctuary within an area that also includes more than 20 lodges and even a cheese factory. This stretch of the trek takes about 3 hours. You will have your lunch ready upon reaching Kyanjin Gompa. If the weather is permissible, you will then be guided towards Kyanjin Ri which takes about 3 hours roundtrip. Upon returning spend your night at Teahouse/Lodge accommodations.
Kyanjin Gomba - Langtang Village - Thangshyap (6 hrs trek)

As per the itinerary plan you will start your return journey after a pleasant night at Kyanjin Gompa. If the weather on the previous day is not feasible, you will be taking a morning hike to the top of Kyanjin ri on this day. After returning from the hike, you will be served with breakfast before your beginning your return journey. The trail we take is the same on our way up. We traverse descending through small hamlets located along. Further ahead from Langtang Village, we reach Thangshyap for our night stay
Thangshyap - Lama Hotel - Rimche - Bamboo - Syabrubesi (6 hrs trek)

We retrace our footsteps alongside Langtang Khola towards Syabrubesi. Today’s stretch is all descent that is steep and through dense forest. We traverse through Bamboo and Pairo villages before reaching the Langtang hydropower project. From here we walk on a dirt road towards Syabrubesi marking the end of our trekking journey. Overnight at Syabrubesi hotel.

On the final day, our vehicle will start off from Syabrubesi for your drive towards Kathmandu. We will take the high mountains road of Rasuwa and descend to Nuwakot. From Nuwakot, its a smooth sailing highway ride towards Kathmandu. It takes anywhere from 6-7 hours to reach Kathmandu. We will drop you off at your hotel in the evening. Arrive at your hotel with unforgettable memories, a deep appreciation for the Langtang region, and a sense of accomplishment from your adventure. On the way, reflect on the incredible experiences, stunning landscapes, and the sense of achievement you've gained throughout the journey

item.title: Pikey Peak Trek – 8 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Pikey Peak Trek

The Pikey Peak Trek is a scenic short adventure in Nepal’s lower Everest region, offering spectacular Himalayan views, peaceful trails, and authentic Sherpa culture. Away from the busier routes, this journey provides a wonderful opportunity to experience the natural beauty of the Himalayas in a quieter setting.

The adventure takes you through traditional mountain villages, lush rhododendron forests, alpine meadows, and peaceful hillside trails. Along the way, trekkers can experience the warm hospitality of local communities while discovering the customs and traditions of the Sherpa people. The changing landscapes make every day of the journey unique.

Spectacular Himalayan Sunrise Views

One of the main highlights is the early morning ascent to Pikey Peak at 4,065 meters. From the summit, trekkers can enjoy panoramic views of Mount Everest, Makalu, Kanchenjunga, Gaurishankar, Numbur, Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and many other Himalayan peaks.

The sunrise over the snow-covered mountains creates a memorable experience, especially for photographers and nature lovers. The viewpoint offers an impressive perspective of the Himalayan range without requiring a lengthy expedition.

Experience Sherpa Culture

The route also provides opportunities to experience traditional mountain life. Trekkers pass through welcoming Sherpa settlements and learn about local customs, Buddhist traditions, and everyday life in the region. Ancient monasteries, including Thupten Chholing Monastery near Junbesi, add cultural and spiritual value to the journey.

Comfortable teahouses along the trail provide accommodation, local meals, and warm hospitality after each day of walking.

A Rewarding Short Himalayan Adventure

This journey is suitable for both beginners and experienced hikers with a reasonable level of fitness. The moderate trails and manageable itinerary make it ideal for travelers who have limited time but still want to enjoy a genuine Himalayan experience.

With peaceful trails, beautiful forests, traditional villages, rich culture, and panoramic mountain scenery, the Pikey Peak Trek is a rewarding way to explore Nepal’s Everest region in just eight days.

Today is a peaceful exploration day in Junbesi, one of the most beautiful Sherpa villages in the lower Everest region. After breakfast, you can explore the traditional village, local houses, farmland, monasteries, and surrounding viewpoints. You may also visit Thupten Choling Monastery, an important Buddhist monastery located above Junbesi. The walk to the monastery offers beautiful countryside views, quiet trails, and a deeper experience of Sherpa culture and Buddhist lifestyle. After the visit, you will return to Junbesi for an overnight stay.

After breakfast, you will drive back from Junbesi to Kathmandu. The journey passes through Salleri, Phaplu, local villages, rivers, hills, and scenic countryside roads. After several days in the peaceful Pikey Peak region, the drive back to Kathmandu gives you time to enjoy the changing landscapes of rural Nepal. After arriving in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel. The evening is free for rest, shopping, or enjoying your final night in the city.

Your 8-day Pikey Peak Trek comes to an end today. Depending on your international flight schedule, you may have some free time for breakfast, packing, or last-minute shopping. Our representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport for your final departure. item.title: Mardi Himal Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Hidden Gem of the Annapurna Region

The Mardi Himal Trek is one of the best short trekking adventures in Nepal. Located in the famous Annapurna region, this peaceful trail offers stunning mountain views, beautiful forests, and authentic village life. Opened to trekkers in 2012, the route is still less crowded than the popular Annapurna Base Camp Trek. It is an excellent choice for travelers who want a quieter Himalayan experience without missing spectacular scenery.

The journey begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara, followed by a short drive to Kande. From there, the trail climbs through lush rhododendron forests, peaceful oak woods, and charming Gurung and Magar villages. As you gain altitude, the landscape changes into open alpine meadows and narrow ridges with breathtaking views in every direction.

Spectacular Himalayan Views

One of the biggest highlights of the Mardi Himal Trek is the incredible mountain scenery. Throughout the trek, you will enjoy close-up views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Mardi Himal, and several other snow-covered peaks. The hike to Mardi Himal Base Camp, at approximately 4,500 meters, rewards you with one of the finest panoramic viewpoints in the Annapurna region.

Perfect for Beginners and Experienced Trekkers

The Mardi Himal Trek is suitable for both beginners and experienced hikers. The trail is well marked and does not require technical climbing skills. Although you will reach a high altitude, the itinerary allows enough time for proper acclimatization. Comfortable teahouses along the route provide warm meals, cozy accommodation, and genuine Nepali hospitality.

A Short Trek with Lasting Memories

Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or returning for another adventure, the Mardi Himal Trek offers an unforgettable Himalayan experience. It combines breathtaking mountain landscapes, rich local culture, peaceful trails, and rewarding viewpoints in just a few days. If you are looking for an adventure that is both accessible and unforgettable, the Mardi Himal Trek is an excellent choice.

item.title: Gokyo Lake Cholapass+ EBC Trekking
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Why Choose the Gokyo Lake Cho La Pass Trek?

The Gokyo Lake Cho La Pass Trek is an unforgettable Himalayan adventure combining turquoise mountain lakes, dramatic passes, Sherpa culture, and Everest Base Camp. The route offers a rewarding alternative to the classic Everest trail, with diverse landscapes and spectacular views throughout the journey.

Stunning Himalayan Landscapes

The journey takes you through the heart of the Everest region, with impressive views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu. The trail passes through peaceful valleys, alpine meadows, suspension bridges, and rugged mountain terrain. Each section brings a new perspective of the Himalayas.

Explore the Gokyo Lakes

One of the major highlights is the beautiful Gokyo Lakes, surrounded by towering peaks and glaciers. Trekkers can also climb Gokyo Ri for panoramic views across the Everest region. The peaceful lakes and dramatic scenery make this section especially memorable.

Experience Sherpa Culture

The route passes through traditional Sherpa settlements, including Namche Bazaar and Khumjung. Along the way, travelers can visit monasteries, prayer wheels, and other cultural sites while learning more about the region's mountain communities and traditions.

Cross the Challenging Cho La Pass

Crossing Cho La Pass adds an exciting challenge to the adventure. The high-altitude pass connects the Gokyo Valley with the Everest Base Camp route and requires good fitness and proper acclimatization. In return, trekkers are rewarded with spectacular glacier and mountain views.

Reach Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar

The journey continues toward Everest Base Camp, one of Nepal's most iconic trekking destinations. After reaching the base camp, the climb to Kala Patthar provides exceptional views of Everest and surrounding peaks, particularly around sunrise and sunset.

This combination of high-altitude landscapes, local culture, turquoise lakes, and iconic Himalayan viewpoints makes the journey a memorable experience for adventurous trekkers.

Don’⁠t point with a f‍inger – especially don’t point with feet​ (about anything).‍
Don‌’t to​u‍ch pe‍ople on the he⁠a​d – always considered sa‍cred.
⁠ Don’t bargain aggressively – pri⁠ces⁠ ar⁠e already f⁠air in the mountains.
Don't​ show Public Displ⁠ay⁠ of Aff⁠ection – people frown on this in​ rural areas.
Don't lit‍t​er or throw f‌o‌od i‌n fire​ pits (fire is sacred).

⁠Wel⁠come to Kat​hmandu! You will be met at the ai‍r⁠port by a Sunris‍e Adv⁠entur‍e Tr​ek re⁠p⁠resentative, who will then take you to your hotel. We will provide you wit‍h‍ a br​iefing and additional informa‍t‌ion‍ about t‌he tr​ip prog⁠ram in⁠ the eveni​ng.⁠
Fly to Lu⁠kla and trek to P‌hakd⁠i​ng (2620m)

Lukl‍a‍ i‌s recognized a​s the She​rpa​ village. W⁠e will continue on our trek and secure​ our loa‍d‍s. After about forty minutes of phenom⁠enal mountain fl‌ying experie‌nces,‍ there will b‌e memories t​o last a lifetim​e. Af‌ter reaching Lukla, w‌e will tr‍avel through Dudh Koshi, better kn‌ow​n as the​ Milk River. Enjo‌ying breathtak​ing views of Moun‍t Kusum Kanga​ru, and many o‌the​r peaks‍, as we ascend and de‌scend the trails sur​roun‌ded by green‌ f​o‌res​ts. A‌fter ho‍ur​s of hikin‌g, we wil‍l cross thr‌ough monasteries, small Sherpa‌ v​illages, a‌nd arrive in Phakding. Meals such as, bre‍akfast, lunch, and dinner‌, a​re includ‌ed and‍ spent at a local trekking​ lodge.

T‍he Khu‌mbu regio⁠n's principal administrative⁠ and commercial hub is Namche Baz‍aar‌. You‍ c‌an se⁠e Hi​malayans working in a variety of jobs. The b‌reathtaking b⁠lue⁠ pi​ne, fir, jun​i​per, and rhododendron for⁠e⁠s‍ts, along with the first glimpse of Eve⁠rest, hel‌p you mana​ge your‍ excit​ement​ fo‌r the exh⁠ilar​at⁠i‍ng journey. We p‍ass numerous village⁠s‍, inc‍l⁠uding T‌ok Tok, Banker, Monjo, Josalle, Th​amse​rku, Kangteg​a, and‍ K‌onde, as we​ enter S‍agar‍matha‌ National Park‌.‍ Here, we get to e‍xa​mine the Sherpa people‌'s way of life,​ which is based on vari⁠ous trad‍i​tional‍ customs an​d val‍ues​. Included in the meals were breakfast, lunch, and di‌nner, foll‌o⁠w‍ed b​y an overnight stay‌ at a trekking l​odge.

We ad‍j⁠us​t to the new environment and altitude in Nam‍che Bazaar. We spend t‍he day takin⁠g i⁠n th‌e mounta‍in views and Khumbu⁠ Peak's sunrise and s‌unset. We h‌ike a s‌hort distance to the Sherpa Mu​seum, where we can​ see the d‌istinctive custo‍ms and cu‍ltures of the⁠ Sherp⁠a people.‍ I⁠n a⁠dditi⁠on,‍ y‍ou will either be sh‌own a‍round Khumjung vil​lage‍ or Tham‌e Monastery. We live in Khumjung​ Village, a s‍izab‍le Sherpa community w​here we can observe their distinctive cultura‌l v‌alues and wa‌y of life‍. W‍e take in the expansive mountain views as w‌e acclimate t‍o the lighter air and get read‍y for the‍ next day​'s excursion! In​cluded​ in the‌ m‌e​als are breakf​ast, lunch⁠, and din‌ner, followed by an ove‍rnigh‍t sta​y at a​ tre​kking l‍odge.

We begin our journ​ey to Dole this morn‌in‍g af‌te​r ea‌ting breakfast. Fir​s​t, with a view of​ the snow-capped Shana​sa mountains​, we eventually make our way around Na‍mche Bazaar, clim⁠b​ Mongl‌a Hill, des​cend to Pho‌rtse Than​g‍a, a⁠nd t‍h‍en wal⁠k to Dole. There are t​eah⁠ouses in the small⁠ village of Dole in this area. We travel past br​eathtaking vistas of mounta​ins s‍u​ch as Eve‌rest, Kantega, Th⁠amserku‌, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Amada⁠blam. We arrive at M‌ong a​nd beg‍in‌ our descent to the Dudhkoshi bank. We cl​imb the hill once mor‍e, pas‍s through a tiny villag‌e​, and arriv‍e at Do‍le. Included in th‍e meals are breakfast, lu⁠nch, and dinner, followed by‍ an o‌v‌ernight sta⁠y at a trekking lodg​e.

We leave Dole and climb ov​er the pic​turesqu​e ridge. Along the river​, we wil‌l trav‍erse sand spurs⁠ and‌ w​a⁠lk h‍igh ab⁠ove the valley.‍ We have the opportuni‌ty​ t‌o observe the life⁠s​tyles of the locals with varyin​g cu‍ltur⁠al values as we‌ pa‌ss through the‌ villages of Lhabharm​a and Luza. We stroll pas‌t the Dudhkoshi valley afte​r t​aking in the breatht‍aking scener⁠y. Before movi⁠ng on to our next destinati‍o‌n, we‌ will‍ also stop by the H‍imalay‌a Rescue O​peration, which wa‍s⁠ founded to provide basic med⁠i⁠c​al​ care,⁠ and res‍t. Included in the meals are breakfast, lunch, and din⁠ner, foll⁠owed by an overnight stay at a tre‌kking lodge.‌

We hike to Gokyo to​d‍ay⁠, which‌ is encircled by b‍reathtaki​ng mountain views‍, while f​o‌llowing the Lama foo​tprints. Af​ter trav‌ersing a path dotted with boulders at the edge of th‌e third la​ke,‍ we reach Goky⁠o after c⁠ross‌ing the second lake, Long‌ponga (469​0m). Ascending th⁠e‌ ri​dge pr​ovides breathtaking v‌iews of the Cho-Oyu, Kantega, C‍holat‌se, and Pan​gk⁠a mountains‍. While traveli‌ng, we stop in P⁠angka, th⁠e site o‍f the 1‌995 ava​l​an‍che disas​ter th‌at claimed the lives of‍ ov⁠er 40 peop‌le. We now‌ desc⁠end to the river and​ a⁠scend steeply to the Ngozumpa moraine. W⁠e pass b‍oth the upper and l‌ower Gokyo L‍akes‌ b‌ef‍ore arriving at⁠ G​o​ky​o aft​er a few⁠ ho​urs of walking. I‍nclu​de‍d in the meals are brea‍kfast, lunc‌h, and dinner, followed by an overnight stay at a trekking lodge.
Day​ hike to Gokyo Ri and tr⁠ek to Thagnak (4678m⁠)

Gok‍yo Ri ha‍s an altitude of 5483m. And we will⁠ hike i⁠t up‍ steeply in the morning. It is a satisfying place‍ because you can‌ see the spectacular vie​ws of the Gokyo Valley​, the Kh​u‌mbu Him‍alayas, Everest, L‍hotse‌, N‍uptse, Makalu, Cho-Oyu⁠ and Gychun⁠g K​ang. Sunrise and sunset vi‌ews of the Everes‌t peaks also j​ustify tre‍kking to G‌okyo. As‍ we hike dow‍n towards Gokyo Val​ley‍, we will al‌so peek at the vie​ws of K‍usum Kagaru, Kantega, T​hamse‌rku⁠, and others. We travel to Thangnak after spending a few hours st⁠rolling through the verdant fo​rests that e⁠nc‍ircle the glaciers. Included in the meals are breakfast, lunch​, and di​nne​r, follo‍wed by‍ an‌ overn‍ig​ht stay at a trekking lodge.
Trek to Dzonglha via Cho La P‌a‌ss (5420m)

Since we must a‌s‍c​end the steep path to the region's highest point and traver‌se some ext‍rem‍ely icy tra‌cks, today i​s tr‌u​ly the day when na‌tur‍e puts​ our strength to the​ te‍st.⁠ To ge​t to Cho La Pass‌, we⁠ will first clim‌b‍ a steep path t‌h‍at leads to a trail w‌ith sharp d‍rops, and then we will climb once more. This time, w⁠e are accomp‍anied by views of the‍ moun‌tains an⁠d Bu⁠ddhi⁠st p‌raye‌r flags. We have a close-up view⁠ of the m‌agnificent peaks⁠ Cholatse and Tabuch​e because⁠ we are adjacent to them. With st‌unning vie⁠ws of the vall‍ey a​nd⁠ villages from the summ‍it,⁠ we des​cend​ gent‍ly to Dzongla after c⁠rossing the Cho La Pass​. Inclu‌ded in the meals are break‍fa⁠st, l‍unc⁠h, and dinner, follow⁠ed by an overnigh‌t‍ sta‌y at a trekking lodge.

As⁠ you app‌roach the end of th⁠e moraine of the Khumb‌u Gla‌cier, the h‌ike‍ towards Ev​e​rest Base Camp cont⁠inues across alpine meadows and summer yak pastures.‌ After this⁠, t⁠he trek to the village⁠ of Gora‍k Shep is s‍teep and arduous. Next, you w‍ill⁠ go to Lobuche t⁠o ta⁠ke in Nuptse distant and the stunning sunset. As we walk through the glacial v⁠is‌tas, we had w​onderf‍ul vi‌ews‍ of the mount⁠ains including Nupts​e, Lhotse, Amadabl‍am, and many other towering pea​ks.​ Meals⁠ will include breakfast, lunch, and dinner, followed by‌ an overnight at a tr​ekking l​odge.

W‍e hike to‍ Gorak Shep f‍rom Lobuche​. This 5-kil‍ometer hi‍ke gives us a gre⁠at opport⁠unity to see the Cha​ngri glaci‍er and oth‍er mo​untain​s, p‌rimarily Pumori. One of the greatest ti‍mes to trek⁠ to Ever‍est‍ Cho La Pass is du⁠ring the‌ Go‍rakshep trek. We exper‌ience many u‍ps and downs while trekking t‌hro‌ugh the verdant forests.​ We arrive at th‌e base camp after c‌limbing over th⁠e g​lacial route‌. Here, we take pleasure in the magnificent glacial surroundings and the stunning moun‌tain v⁠iews‍. In‍clude‍d i‌n the meals a‍re breakfast,​ lunch, and dinn‍e⁠r⁠, followed by an ove‌rnight stay a​t a‌ trekking lo‍dg‌e.
M⁠orning h‌ike to either Eve​rest Base Camp (5365m)or Kala Patth​ar (5550m) a‍nd trek to Pheri‌che (3950m)

Today,​ we⁠ will be hiking to kala‌patthar, whic‍h as the‍ name suggests, is the b‍est place t​o "view" E​ver⁠es‍t. And, If E⁠BC is the base of Everest, it is also where all climber⁠s‍ are present at tim​es, and we get to take nice photos in fro​n⁠t of Everest duri‌ng the climbing season. But th⁠en,‍ we w⁠ill view lots o‌f peaks including Nupt​se, Lhotse, Amadablam, Taboche, Cholatse, Pumor‌i, Everest, a‍nd others from ka​lapat‌thar. Then we‌ wi‌l​l hike from G‌o‌rak Shep to Per‌i​che. Th‌e hike t​o Periche will ta‍ke us⁠ d⁠o‌wn thr⁠ough rhodode‌ndron forests and‌ down terrain. The meal‌s included are breakfa⁠st, lunch, and dinner, and we​ wil‍l s‌tay in a‌ trekking lo‍dge.

W‌e hike d‌ownhill from Peric​he to Tengboc‍he, where we visit an old mon​ast​ery before⁠ returning to N​amc‍he Bazaar. This monastery was j‌ust‍ rebuilt. We get t​o‍ s‍ee t‌he expa​nsive vistas of the mo‌untains Thams‌erk‌u, Kangtega, Khumbi La, and⁠ Kong‌do R​i as we hike just beneath t⁠he breathtaking Himalayas. We inve‌stigate​ the local way of life as we travel thro‌ugh the tiny village of​ Pangboche. A‌fter a while‍ o⁠f walking, th​e trail leads u‌s to Tengboche Nmache, the oldest monastery. In​cluded in the meals a​re brea​k‍fast, lu⁠nch, and di​nner, f⁠ollowed by a​n overnight stay‌ at a trekking lodge.

We‍ will be t​rekking back to Lukla today to catch our f‌light to Kathma‍ndu, which will be our final trek. We‍'‌l​l⁠ explore Lukla during the day. We pass the lovely vil‌lages of the K​humbu region‌ as‌ we stro‌l‍l a⁠bove the hill. We follow‍ t‍he Dudhkos⁠hi​ Rive t​rail e‌dge, cros‍sing suspension bridges before arriving at Lukla. Included in the⁠ meals a​re breakfast, lunch, and dinner, followed by an overnight stay at a trekking lodge‌.

We fly back t‌o Kathm​andu in the morning, where we can‌ once more take in the breatht​aking valleys and landscape⁠s r‌ep⁠lete with breathtaking mountain v​ista‍s. Yo⁠u‍ can part‍ic‍ipate in t⁠he‍ compan​y's‍ e‌vening meal an‍d c​ul‌tural pro‍gr⁠am in the evening.

On the final d​ay, yo​u can eit‌her relax and head home safel⁠y or follow a​lo​ng w⁠ith us at Sunr⁠ise Adven‌ture Treks and​ Tour for⁠ another day of ad‌ve‍nture. Als​o,​ in accord⁠an‍ce with your flight‍ itin‍erar‍y, we‌ will take you to the⁠ a⁠irport abo‌ut three hours e⁠arly to make sure you​ get your next flight.

Airport pickup and drop-off, as well as all‍ g​r⁠ound tran​sportation while trave​ling.‍

item.title: Annapurna Circuit Trek via Tilicho Lake
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Hidden high in the heart of the Himalayas, Tilicho Lake and the Annapurna Circuit Trek together create one of the most breathtaking adventures in the world. This journey is not just a trek; it is a life-changing experience that combines dramatic mountain landscapes, ancient cultures, remote villages, and one of the highest lakes on Earth.

Tilicho Lake – The World Above the Clouds

Situated at an altitude of 4,919 meters, Tilicho Lake is often celebrated as one of the highest lakes in the world. Surrounded by towering peaks of the Annapurna range, the turquoise waters shimmer against a backdrop of snow-covered giants and rugged cliffs. The trail to Tilicho is both challenging and rewarding, offering raw Himalayan beauty at every step.

Trekkers pass through remote settlements, glacial valleys, and landslide-prone trails carved into steep mountainsides. The journey demands determination, but the moment you stand before the pristine lake, framed by Tilicho Peak and the Annapurna massif, every step feels worthwhile. The silence, broken only by mountain winds, creates a sense of peace that is rare and unforgettable.

Annapurna Circuit – Nepal’s Classic Trek

The Annapurna Circuit is one of Nepal’s most iconic trekking routes. It circles the Annapurna Massif, offering an incredible variety of landscapes — from lush subtropical forests and terraced rice fields to alpine meadows and high-altitude deserts.

The trek traditionally begins in the lower Marsyangdi Valley and gradually ascends through diverse cultural regions inhabited by Gurung, Thakali, and Manangi communities. Along the way, trekkers experience centuries-old monasteries, prayer flags fluttering in the wind, and warm Himalayan hospitality.

One of the major highlights of the circuit is crossing the Thorong La Pass (5,416 meters), one of the highest trekking passes in the world. Reaching the top at sunrise, surrounded by panoramic Himalayan views, is a powerful and emotional achievement for many adventurers.

A Perfect Combination of Adventure and Culture

Adding Tilicho Lake to the Annapurna Circuit extends the adventure and offers a deeper exploration of the region. It introduces more dramatic landscapes and a sense of remoteness that feels untouched by time. The blend of physical challenge, spiritual atmosphere, and cultural richness makes this trek truly unique.

From rhododendron forests to barren high-altitude landscapes, from warm teahouses to icy mountain winds, every day brings a new perspective. The Annapurna Circuit with Tilicho Lake is not just about reaching a destination — it’s about embracing the journey, connecting with nature, and discovering strength within yourself.

For trekkers seeking one of the most diverse and rewarding Himalayan experiences, this combination stands as a dream adventure waiting to be explored.

• Visit Tilicho Lake at 4,919 meters, surrounded by dramatic Himalayan peaks.

  • Witness the stunning turquoise water reflecting the snow-covered mountains.

  • Experience a peaceful and less-crowded high-altitude destination.

  • Conquer one of the highest trekking passes in the world.

  • Enjoy breathtaking sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.

  • Feel the true achievement of high-altitude adventure.

  • Walk through lush green forests and terraced farmland.

  • Trek across alpine meadows and glacial valleys.

  • Explore the dramatic desert-like terrain of Manang and Mustang.

  • Experience the warm hospitality of Gurung, Thakali, and Manangi communities.

  • Visit ancient monasteries, mani walls, and prayer flags along the trail.

  • Discover Tibetan-influenced culture in high Himalayan settlements.

  • Enjoy close-up views of Annapurna, Tilicho Peak, Gangapurna, and Dhaulagiri.

  • Capture unforgettable panoramas throughout the journey.

  • A perfect blend of adventure and endurance.

  • Ideal for trekkers seeking both natural beauty and physical accomplishment.

  • A rewarding extension to the classic Annapurna Circuit route.

• Hotel pickup and drop by private vehicle.
  • Authorized English-speaking government licensed Guide
  • All necessary paperworks, trekking permits (TIMS ), ACAP and all government and local taxes.
  • Tea-house accommodation x10 nights during the trek
  • All meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) during the trek
  • All expenses for staffs: including their salary, insurance, equipment, food, transportation and accommodation.
  • All applicable government tax
  • Private Transportation as per the itinerary as per the number of pax (Kathmandu –Besisahar - Chame, Muktinath –
    Tatopani Hot spring - Pokhara)

• International airfare to and from Nepal.

  • Nepal entry visa fees (obtainable upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu).

  • Travel and rescue insurance (mandatory and must cover high-altitude trekking up to 5,500 meters).

  • Personal trekking equipment (except sleeping bag and down jacket provided by the company).

  • Lunch and dinner in Kathmandu and Pokhara

  • Extra accommodation in Kathmandu due to early arrival, late departure, or early return from the trek.

  • Personal expenses such as snacks, soft drinks, bottled water, hot showers, Wi-Fi, battery charging, laundry, and bar bills.

  • Tips for guide, porter, and driver (tipping is customary in Nepal).

  • Costs arising from natural disasters, weather conditions, flight delays, political disturbances, or any unforeseen circumstances beyond our control.

  • Any other expenses not specifically mentioned in the “Package Includes” section.
Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani (1800m/5,905 ft) - Chame (2,670m/8,760 ft) (10 hrs drive)
You will be taken by a bus from Kathmandu to Besisahar and then continue your journey to Dharapani and finally to Chame in a private Jeep, enjoying the scenic journey.
Chame to Upper Pisang (3,300m/10,826 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Chame, you'll walk to Upper Pisang, a picturesque village with stunning mountain views. You will discover and immerse yourself in the local culture.
Upper Pisang to Ngawal (3,700m/12,140 ft) (6 hrs hike)
You will continue the hike to Ngawal, a beautiful village located on a hillside. The breathtaking views of Annapurna II, Annapurna III, and Gangapurna mountains and valleys will mesmerize you.
After exploring the cave near Ngawal, you will walk to Manang and take a day to relax and get used to the high altitude in Manang. You will explore the village and enjoy panoramic mountain views.
Manang - Tilicho Base Camp (4,150m/13,615 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Manang, you will hike to Tilicho Base Camp. You will soar through the alpine landscapes and experience the tranquility of the high Himalayas.
Tilicho Base Camp to Shri Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft) (6 hrs hike)

From the Base Camp, you will walk to Lake Tilicho (5050m/16,568 ft) and enjoy the natural beauty of the tranquil lake surrounded by mountains. You'll rise and fall through the Alpine landscapes and experience the high Himalayas.
Shri Kharka - Yak Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft) (6 hrs walk)
You will walk from Shri Kharka to Yak Kharka and experience the natural beauty of the Manang and Annapurna Himalayas.
Yak Kharka - Thorong Phedi (4,450m/14,600 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Yak Kharka, you will walk to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. The next day, you will be prepared for the difficult passage of passage.
Thorong Phedi to Muktinath (3,800m/12,467 ft) via Thorong La Pass (5,416m/17,769 ft) (12 hrs walk)

You'll set off early in the morning for the challenging but rewarding climb to Thorong La Pass. You will experience the thrill of crossing the high mountain pass and enjoy the panoramic views. You will descend to the Muktinath temple, a sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and explore the scenic village. Overnight stay will be in Muktinath.

You'll descend towards Jomsom, a windswept town in the Mustang district. You'll witness the dramatic change in landscapes as you venture into the arid and desert-like terrain and explore the town and head towards Tatopani Hotspring where you’ll take a dip into Natural Hotspring to rejuvenate yourself. Overnight stay will be in Tatopani.

You will be driven from Tatopani to Pokhara and enjoy the mountain views. You will relax and unwind thinking about the incredible journey you have completed in Pokhara. Congratulations! You've completed your dream adventure.

Upper Body

  • Moisture-wicking base layer (thermal tops)

  • Trekking shirts (quick-dry)

  • Fleece or insulated jacket

  • Down jacket (provided if included in package)

  • Waterproof and windproof outer jacket (Gore-Tex or similar)

Lower Body

  • Thermal base layer (bottom)

  • Trekking pants (2 pairs recommended)

  • Waterproof/windproof trekking pants

  • Comfortable casual pants (for evenings)

Innerwear

  • Undergarments

  • Sports bras (for women)

  • Warm socks (3–4 pairs)

  • Lightweight trekking socks (2–3 pairs)

 Footwear

  • Sturdy, waterproof trekking boots (well broken-in)

  • Lightweight sandals or camp shoes

  • Gaiters (recommended for snow conditions)

 Head & Hand Gear

  • Warm wool or fleece hat

  • Sun hat or cap

  • Neck gaiter or buff

  • Sunglasses with UV protection

  • Warm gloves (inner + outer waterproof gloves)

 Trekking Equipment

  • Backpack (30–40L for daily use)

  • Duffel bag (carried by porter)

  • Sleeping bag (provided if included in package)

  • Trekking poles

  • Headlamp with extra batteries

  • Water bottles or hydration bladder

  • Water purification tablets or filter

 Toiletries & Personal Care

  • Toothbrush & toothpaste

  • Small towel

  • Sunscreen (SPF 30+)

  • Lip balm with SPF

  • Hand sanitizer

  • Wet wipes

  • Basic first-aid kit

  • Personal medications

 Accessories

  • Power bank

  • Camera or smartphone

  • Charging cables

  • Travel adapter (Type C/D/M for Nepal)

  • Snacks and energy bars

 Important Documents

  • Valid passport

  • Nepal visa

  • Travel insurance (covering high altitude up to 5,500m)

  • Passport-sized photos (for permits)

  • Copies of important documents

Optional but Recommended

  • Microspikes (early spring/late autumn snow)

  • Lightweight book or journal

  • Earplugs

  • Dry bags or zip-lock bags

item.title: Everest Base Camp
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Why choose Everest Base Camp trek?

The Everest Base Camp Trek is widely regarded as one of the finest trekking experiences in the world. This classic 15-day journey leads you deep into the Khumbu region to the base of Mount Everest (8,848.86 meters), the highest peak on the planet. Along the way, trekkers encounter a powerful mix of dramatic mountain scenery, traditional Sherpa culture, and ever-changing landscapes. It is a journey that offers not only natural beauty, but also a strong sense of purpose and achievement.

The adventure begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla, a mountain airstrip set among steep hills and towering peaks. From here, the trail follows the Dudh Koshi River through a series of traditional villages connected by suspension bridges and forested paths. Early sections of the trek pass through green valleys filled with pine and rhododendron, while higher elevations reveal more rugged terrain and expansive mountain views.

Namche Bazaar is one of the most significant stops along the route. This vibrant mountain town serves as the main gateway to the Everest region and provides an important acclimatization break. Trekkers can enjoy clear views of Everest, Ama Dablam, and nearby peaks while exploring local markets, bakeries, and cultural sites. The journey continues to Tengboche, where the region’s most important monastery stands against a backdrop of towering mountains, offering both cultural insight and unforgettable scenery.

Beyond Tengboche, the trail climbs steadily through Dingboche and Lobuche, where the environment becomes more remote and alpine in character. These higher settlements play a key role in helping trekkers adjust safely to the altitude. The final approach leads to Gorakshep and then to Everest Base Camp (5,364 meters), the historic starting point for Everest expeditions. Standing here, surrounded by glaciers and immense peaks, is a moment that leaves a lasting impression.

A further highlight is the ascent of Kala Patthar (5,545 meters), a viewpoint known for its exceptional panorama of Everest. The early morning climb rewards trekkers with clear, close views of the mountain and a sunrise that illuminates the entire range. For many, this becomes one of the most memorable parts of the journey.

Throughout the trek, accommodation is provided in locally operated teahouses, where trekkers experience genuine hospitality and daily life in the mountains. The route also passes through Sagarmatha National Park, a protected area recognized for its natural and cultural importance. Its forests, wildlife, and mountain landscapes add depth and variety to the experience.

Although the Everest Base Camp Trek requires good physical condition and preparation, it does not involve technical climbing. With proper pacing and acclimatization, it is achievable for many trekkers. More than just a physical challenge, it is a journey that offers perspective, connection with nature, and a deep sense of accomplishment.

For those who have dreamed of walking in the shadow of Everest, this trek represents an extraordinary opportunity. It is not simply about reaching base camp, but about the experience of the journey itself and the memories created along the way.

flight to lukla & trek to Padking( 4h /2610m/8695ft)

Today early morning we fly to Lukla .is about Minute flight. once we are landed in Lukla we meet our porter and we walk downhill to chaurikharka and further descend to thadokoshi.you may see some mountain from this point. we continue our trek uphill to ghat & a ridge marked with painted mani stone. after one more hour of ascending we will finally reach Phadking.overnight at tea house.

Upon arrival, we meet our porter and begin our trek, descending to Chaurikharka and further to Thadokoshi, where you may enjoy views of the surrounding mountains. We then ascend uphill to Ghat, passing a ridge marked with painted mani stones, and after roughly an hour of trekking, reach Phakding, where we stay overnight in a cozy tea house, resting for the next stage of our journey.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Kathmandu(1350M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:17:"Phakding (2610 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:3:"7KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:34:"3–4 hours trek, 35-minute flight";s:14:"important_note";s:247:"Flights to Lukla are weather dependent and may be delayed or rescheduled. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol.";}s:6:"item-2";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:48:"Day 3:Phakding to Namche Bazar(7h/3450m/11290ft)";s:11:"description";s:1948:"After breakfast, we begin our scenic trek following the beautiful Dudh Koshi River, enjoying the refreshing mountain air as the trail winds through pine and rhododendron forests. The sound of the rushing river accompanies us as we cross several thrilling suspension bridges decorated with colorful prayer flags and pass through small traditional Sherpa villages with stone houses, prayer wheels, and mani walls. Soon we reach Monjo, the entrance to Sagarmatha National Park, where our permits are checked before we officially enter this UNESCO World Heritage Site. The path continues with gentle ups and downs through forested terrain until we arrive at Jorsalle, the last village before Namche Bazaar, where we can take a short rest or enjoy tea while preparing for the climb ahead. From Jorsalle, the trail follows the river to the dramatic high suspension bridge at the confluence of the Dudh Koshi and Bhote Koshi rivers; standing on this bridge is an unforgettable experience, and on a clear day we may catch our first breathtaking glimpse of Mount Everest, along with surrounding Himalayan giants, a magical moment that fills us with excitement. After crossing the bridge, the trail begins a long and steady uphill ascent through dense pine forest, requiring a slow and steady pace as we gain significant altitude; along the way, the views gradually open up, revealing spectacular mountain scenery behind us. After approximately 5–6 hours of trekking, we finally reach Namche Bazaar (3,440 m), the largest Sherpa settlement and vibrant commercial hub of the Khumbu region, beautifully set in a natural amphitheater surrounded by towering peaks. Namche offers a surprising range of facilities including good restaurants, bakeries, trekking gear shops, internet cafés, ATMs, and money exchange services. In the evening, we relax and explore the lively market area before enjoying a warm meal and an overnight stay at a comfortable tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Phakding(2610M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Namche Bazar(3440M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:4:"11KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"6H";s:14:"important_note";s:225:"Today involves significant altitude gain. Proper hydration is very important.";}s:6:"item-3";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:42:"Day 4:Acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar";s:11:"description";s:463:"Today, although we remain in Namche Bazaar due to the high altitude, it is not a full rest day. After breakfast, we trek to a nearby viewpoint to enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding mountains, including Mount Everest. We then hike up to Syangboche, home to the highest airport in the region, and visit the Everest View Hotel for some stunning vistas. After a hearty breakfast, we embark on a rewarding short hike toward Nagarjun Hill, where we are treated to awe-inspiring panoramic views of some of the most iconic Himalayan peaks, including Ama Dablam, Makalu, Lhotse, Tawache, Cholatse, and numerous other majestic peaks that punctuate the skyline. The crisp mountain air, sweeping vistas, and serene landscapes make this hike an unforgettable experience, offering countless photo opportunities and moments of reflection. After soaking in these magnificent Himalayan panoramas, we gently descend back to Dingboche, where we enjoy a leisurely lunch and rest, letting our bodies recover and prepare for the adventures ahead. Overnight stay is at the same charming tea house, surrounded by the serene beauty of the mountains.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:5:"3.5KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"3H";s:14:"important_note";s:162:"This rest day is critical for successful trek completion. From here, the trail climbs steadily uphill for some time before leveling out as we follow the glacial valley toward Lobuche. Surrounded by towering mountains and vast alpine landscapes, we finally reach Lobuche (4,910 m), a small settlement with a few tea houses serving trekkers and climbers on the Everest Base Camp route. The trail gradually & Rockey all the way, once we reach in Gorakshep we chick into the hotel and have some rest, we continue up the edge of the Khumbu glacier until we finally reach base camp. if you are lucky & timing is right you may see expedition team. after spending some time to enjoying, we back way down to gorakshep.over night at tea house. The trail climbs steeply over rocky and sandy slopes, and the thin mountain air makes the ascent slow and steady. As we gain height, breathtaking panoramic views gradually unfold, including close-up views of Mount Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, and the stunning Pumori. Reaching the summit of Kala Patthar is a truly unforgettable moment, offering the best panoramic view of Everest and the surrounding Himalayan giants, especially during sunrise or early morning light when the peaks glow beautifully.
After spending some time taking photographs and enjoying the spectacular scenery, we descend carefully back to Gorakshep for a short rest and breakfast. We then continue trekking down the valley, retracing our steps along the Khumbu Glacier toward Lobuche and further downhill to Thukla. From here, the trail gradually descends to the wide and peaceful valley of Pheriche. Compared to the previous high-altitude days, the descent feels easier as oxygen levels increase and breathing becomes more comfortable. Finally, we reach Pheriche (4,240 m), a beautiful settlement surrounded by mountains, where we enjoy a well-deserved rest and overnight stay at a tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Gorakshep(5160M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:15:"Pheriche(4250M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:4:"10KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"6H";s:14:"important_note";s:126:"The morning hike is cold and physically demanding. The trail follows a familiar path through beautiful rhododendron and juniper forests with scenic mountain views along the way. We gradually descend to Phunki Tenga, a small riverside settlement where we stop for lunch and a short rest. After lunch, we begin the steady uphill climb through forested trails toward Tengboche, home to the famous Tengboche Monastery, the largest monastery in the Everest region. From Tengboche, the trail continues with gentle ups and downs before descending further toward the Dudh Koshi valley. Finally, we follow the gradual trail back to Namche Bazaar, where we enjoy a relaxing evening and overnight stay at a comfortable tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Pheriche(4250M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:13:"Namche(3440M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:4:"16KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"9H";s:14:"important_note";s:118:"Even though you are descending, stay careful on downhill trails to avoid knee injury. The path leads us down along the Dudh Koshi River, crossing several suspension bridges decorated with colorful prayer flags and enjoying the last views of the surrounding mountains. Today marks our final night in the Everest region, and as we walk, we reflect on the unforgettable journey through the Himalayas. After several hours of gradual descent and short uphill sections, we arrive in Lukla. In the afternoon, we relax and celebrate the completion of our trek with a hot shower and some free time to explore the small mountain town. In the evening, we gather with our trekking guide and porter to enjoy a few drinks, share stories, and celebrate our successful adventure together. Overnight stay at a comfortable tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Namche(3440M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:12:"Lukla(2860M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:4:"17KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"7H";s:14:"important_note";s:99:"Trail may be crowded.
