Do not walk too fast to avoid slips and falls.";}s:7:"item-12";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:59:"Day 13: Morning flight Lukla to Kathmandu(30m flight/1300m)";s:11:"description";s:642:"On the final morning in the mountains, you can enjoy the last beautiful views of the snow-capped Himalayan peaks surrounding Lukla before boarding your scenic flight back to Kathmandu. The short mountain flight offers one more breathtaking aerial view of the Himalayas, bringing your unforgettable Everest adventure to a close. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you to your hotel. In the afternoon, you will have free time to relax or explore the vibrant city at your own pace — perhaps strolling through the bustling streets of Thamel for shopping, cafés, and souvenirs. Overnight stay at the hotel in Kathmandu.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:12:"Lukla(2860M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"kathmandu(1350M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:25:"Flight – approx. 138 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:39:"30 Minutes flight & 30 Minuts drive";s:14:"important_note";s:437:"Flights from Lukla are highly dependent on weather conditions and are often scheduled early in the morning when visibility is clear. Delays and cancellations are common, so please remain flexible and patient. Keep your essential items, valuables, and important documents in your hand carry. After arriving in Kathmandu, you will return to a lower altitude, and your body may feel more relaxed. Use this time to rest and recover properly.";}s:7:"item-13";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:27:"Day 14: Kathmandu free day ";s:11:"description";s:565:"Today is a free and relaxing day in Kathmandu after completing your Everest Base Camp trek. You may choose to rest at your hotel or explore the cultural and historical attractions of the city. Popular places to visit include Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple. You can also enjoy shopping in Thamel for souvenirs, handicrafts, and trekking gear. This day allows you to recover comfortably and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Kathmandu before your final departure. Overnight stay at hotel in Kathmandu.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Kathmandu (1,350m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Kathmandu (1,350m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:39:"Optional sightseeing (as per your plan)";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"Free and flexible";s:14:"important_note";s:397:"This is a rest and buffer day, which is very important in case of Lukla flight delays due to weather. Please do not book your international flight on this day. You may use this time to rest your body after the trek, explore the city, or shop for souvenirs. If you rented trekking equipment, please return it on time. Stay hydrated and allow your body to fully recover after the high-altitude trek.";}s:7:"item-14";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:47:"Day 15: Transfer to airport for final departure";s:11:"description";s:573:"Today marks the end of your unforgettable Everest Base Camp Trek. As you leave Nepal, you will carry with you incredible memories of the Himalayan landscapes, Sherpa culture, and your successful journey to Everest Base Camp. We hope this adventure has been a truly rewarding and memorable experience. EverPeak Adventures thanks you for trekking with us and hopes to welcome you again for another Himalayan journey in the future. Safe travels.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Kathmandu (1,350m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:31:"Tribhuvan International Airport";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:12:"Approx. 6 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:21:"20–30 minutes drive";s:14:"important_note";s:452:"Please be ready at your hotel according to the transfer schedule provided by our team. It is recommended to reach the airport at least 3 hours before your international flight time. Make sure you have packed all your belongings, including important documents, passport, and flight tickets. Before leaving, double-check your room to avoid leaving anything behind. Our representative will assist you with the airport transfer and final departure process.";}}

Proper equipment and trekking gear are essential for a safe and comfortable Everest Base Camp Trek. Since the trek passes through different altitudes and weather conditions, having the right clothing and gear helps you stay warm, dry, and protected throughout the journey.

Clothing should be layered to adjust easily to changing temperatures. A moisture-wicking base layer, warm fleece or down jacket, and a waterproof outer jacket are highly recommended. Comfortable trekking pants, thermal innerwear, gloves, warm hat, and wool socks are also important, especially at higher elevations where temperatures drop significantly.

Good quality trekking boots are one of the most important items. They should be well-fitted, waterproof, and already broken in before the trek to avoid blisters. A lightweight daypack is needed to carry daily essentials such as water, snacks, camera, and extra clothing.

Other essential items include sunglasses with UV protection, sunscreen, lip balm, reusable water bottle, trekking poles, and a sleeping bag suitable for cold temperatures. Personal items such as basic toiletries, medications, and a headlamp are also necessary.

Choosing the right gear ensures comfort, safety, and confidence, allowing you to fully enjoy the Everest Base Camp trekking experience.

item.title: Manaslu Circuit Trek
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Why Choose the Manaslu Circuit Trek?

The Manaslu Circuit Trek is one of Nepal’s most rewarding off-the-beaten-path adventures. Set around Mount Manaslu (8,163 m), the world’s eighth-highest mountain, this route combines spectacular Himalayan scenery, traditional villages, and fascinating cultural experiences. Compared with the busier Everest and Annapurna trails, the region offers a quieter and more authentic experience for travelers looking to explore Nepal’s remote mountain landscapes.

Explore the Remote Manaslu Region

The journey begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola before following the Budhi Gandaki River through lush forests, terraced farmland, suspension bridges, and peaceful settlements. As the trail gains elevation, the landscape gradually changes from green valleys to alpine terrain. Along the way, trekkers encounter welcoming communities, traditional homes, Buddhist monasteries, and ancient cultural traditions.

Discover Himalayan Landscapes and Mountain Views

One of the highlights is the remarkable variety of scenery throughout the route. The trail passes through dramatic river valleys, dense forests, alpine meadows, and rugged mountain terrain. As you move higher, impressive views of Mount Manaslu, Himal Chuli, Ganesh Himal, and other snow-covered peaks create unforgettable moments. The changing landscapes also provide excellent opportunities for photography and nature exploration.

Cross the Larke La Pass

The most challenging section is the ascent to Larke La Pass (5,160 m). Reaching the summit requires good preparation and proper acclimatization, but the effort is rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views across the surrounding Himalayas. After crossing the pass, the trail descends toward the Marsyangdi Valley, where the scenery changes once again.

Culture, Nature, and Adventure

Beyond the mountain views, this Himalayan journey offers meaningful encounters with local communities and their way of life. Trekkers can experience Buddhist traditions, visit historic monasteries, and learn about the customs that have shaped the region for generations. The combination of remote landscapes, cultural richness, and physical challenge makes this route an excellent choice for adventurous travelers.

With its peaceful trails, diverse scenery, and authentic mountain experiences, the Manaslu Circuit Trek provides a memorable alternative to Nepal’s more crowded trekking routes.

The‌ Manaslu region is home to a mix of Gurung, Nubri, and Tibetan-influenced communities‍, each with their own traditi‌ons, dialects, and way‍ o‍f life. Ma‍ny villages,‍ especially at higher altitudes like Samagaon and Samdo, follow strong Budd‌h‌is‌t practic‌e‍s. You‌’l‌l find prayer flags, maniwa‌lls (stone carvings with Buddhist prayers),‌ and monasteries througho‌ut the trek. Life here is simp‌le and‌ revolves around farming, herding yaks, and religious rituals.

As a visitor, showing respect‍ to loca‍l culture is very important. Always walk to the le‌ft side o‌f maniwalls and stupas as a sign of respect, and spin prayer⁠ whe‍el‌s clockwise. Greet locals with a smile and a simple‍ “‌Na‍maste‍” or the Tibetan‍ greeting “Tashi Delek.” Modest dress is app‌reciated in‍ villages cover shoulder‍s and avoid very short clothing, even though trek‍king gear is acce‌ptable.

What we can do

Walk left of s‌tupa‌s (clockwise).

Greet locals with Namaste or‍ Tashi Delek.

D‍ress modestly in villages.

Carry your trash and keep the trail clean.

Hike slo‌wly and acclimati‍ze pr‍operly.

Support local tea houses and‍ buy from villagers.

‌Ask before taking photos.

What we can't do

Don’t touch a‍ny‌one’s head or point your feet at shrines.

Don’t enter monasteries withou‍t per‌mission.

Don’t harm animals or w‍ildlif‌e.

After several hours of trekking through forests and narrow trails, we reach Lokpa, a quiet village that marks the entrance to the Tsum Valley.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Jagat (1,340 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:14:"Deng (1,860 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:15:"18–20 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"6–7 hours trek ";s:14:"important_note";s:137:"Today’s trail is mixed with stone steps, narrow paths, and forest sections. Comfortable trekking shoes and steady pacing are important.";}s:6:"item-4";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:50:"Day 5: Trek from Deng to Namrung (2630m / 8629 ft)";s:11:"description";s:556:"Today’s trek takes you deeper into the Manaslu region, where the scenery becomes more dramatic and the cultural atmosphere more Tibetan. The trail passes through small villages, forests, mani walls, and prayer wheels. You will cross the Budhi Gandaki River several times and climb gradually through beautiful landscapes. As you gain altitude, you may begin to see impressive mountain views and traditional stone houses. Namrung is a beautiful village with mountain views and a peaceful environment, making it a great place to rest after the day’s walk.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:14:"Deng (1,860 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:17:"Namrung (2,630 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:15:"18–19 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:152:"Altitude starts to increase from this day, so walk slowly and avoid rushing. Drink enough water and inform your guide if you feel headache or dizziness.";}s:6:"item-5";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:50:"Day 6: Trek from Namrung to Lho (3180m / 10433 ft)";s:11:"description";s:484:"The walk from Namrung to Lho is one of the most scenic sections of the lower Manaslu region. The trail passes through beautiful villages such as Lihi and Sho, where you can see traditional houses, barley fields, mani walls, and prayer flags. As you move higher, the views of Manaslu and nearby peaks become more impressive. Lho is a stunning village known for its monastery and breathtaking mountain views. After reaching Lho, you can rest or visit the local monastery in the evening.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:17:"Namrung (2,630 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:13:"Lho (3,180 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 10–12 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"4–5 hours trek ";s:14:"important_note";s:147:"This is a shorter trekking day, which helps with gradual acclimatization. Take time to enjoy the mountain views and avoid unnecessary fast walking.";}s:6:"item-6";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:51:"Day 7: Trek from Lho to Samagaun (3530m / 11581 ft)";s:11:"description";s:514:"Today’s trail offers spectacular views of Mt. Manaslu and the surrounding Himalayan peaks. You will pass through Shyala, a beautiful village surrounded by mountains and open landscapes. The route is relatively shorter but visually very rewarding. As you approach Samagaun, the valley becomes wider, and the village appears with traditional houses, monasteries, and mountain backdrops. Samagaun is one of the most important villages on the Manaslu Circuit and a key place for acclimatization before moving higher.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Lho (3,180 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Samagaun (3,530 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:14:"8–10 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"4–5 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:123:"Even though the walking time is shorter, the altitude is now above 3,500 meters. You can spend the day exploring the village, visiting the monastery, or taking an optional hike to Manaslu Base Camp or Pungyen Gompa, depending on your fitness and weather conditions. The purpose of this day is to help your body adjust to the altitude before continuing towards Samdo and Larkya La Pass. Samagaun offers beautiful mountain views, peaceful cultural surroundings, and a chance to learn more about the local lifestyle of the Manaslu region.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Samagaun (3,530 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Samagaun (3,530 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:29:"Optional hike around Samagaun";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:25:"4–7 hours optional hike";s:14:"important_note";s:131:"Acclimatization is very important for safety. The trail is shorter but gradually gains altitude as it follows open landscapes, yak grazing areas, and beautiful mountain scenery. The route feels more remote and peaceful as you move closer to the Tibetan border region. Samdo is a traditional village with strong Tibetan cultural influence and impressive views of surrounding peaks. After reaching Samdo, you can rest and explore the village slowly.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Samagaun (3,530 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:15:"Samdo (3,875 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:13:"8–9 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"3–4 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:130:"This is a short trekking day, but the altitude is high. The trail gradually climbs through dry and rugged high-altitude landscapes. The environment becomes colder and more remote as you move closer to the base of Larkya La Pass. This is a short but important day because you need enough rest before the long and challenging pass-crossing day. After reaching Dharamsala, you will have an early dinner and prepare your gear for the next morning.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Samdo (3,875 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:35:"Dharamsala / Larkya Phedi (4,460 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:13:"7–8 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"4–5 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:141:"Accommodation at Dharamsala is basic, and it can be very cold. From the pass, you can enjoy breathtaking views of Himlung Himal, Cheo Himal, Kang Guru, Annapurna II, and other Himalayan peaks. After spending some time at the top, the trail descends steeply towards Bimthang. The long descent can be tiring, but the mountain views and sense of achievement make this day unforgettable.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:35:"Dharamsala / Larkya Phedi (4,460 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Bimthang (3,590 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 22–24 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"8–10 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:159:"Start early, wear warm layers, and carry enough water and snacks. This section is peaceful and scenic, with excellent views of the surrounding hills and mountains. The route passes through rivers, hills, villages, and scenic countryside. After many days in the mountains, returning to Kathmandu feels comfortable and refreshing. item.title: Langtang valley Yala peak
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Why Choose the Langtang Valley Yala Peak Trek?

The Langtang Valley Yala Trek combines scenic Himalayan trekking with an exciting peak-climbing experience in Nepal. The journey takes you through lush forests, traditional Tamang villages, peaceful mountain valleys, and impressive high-altitude landscapes.

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to the trailhead before following the Langtang Valley toward Kyanjin Gompa. Along the way, trekkers pass through rhododendron forests, suspension bridges, rivers, and welcoming mountain communities. The changing scenery provides a wonderful mix of nature, culture, and Himalayan views.

After reaching Kyanjin Gompa, you have time to acclimatize and explore the surrounding area. The route then leads toward Yala Peak, which stands at approximately 5,520 meters. The climb offers an exciting challenge and rewarding views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Ganesh Himal, and other snow-covered peaks.

Beyond the climb, the journey provides opportunities to experience local culture and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of the Langtang region. Experienced guides, comfortable teahouse accommodation, and gradual acclimatization make the adventure suitable for trekkers with a good level of fitness.

Overall, this journey is an excellent choice for travelers who want to combine a Himalayan trek with a manageable peak-climbing experience. It offers beautiful scenery, cultural encounters, and memorable mountain views without the crowds found on some of Nepal’s more popular routes.

• Trek through the beautiful Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's most scenic Himalayan regions.
  • Summit Yala Peak (5,500m), a perfect introductory trekking peak.
  • Enjoy breathtaking views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Shishapangma, and surrounding Himalayan peaks.
  • Visit the traditional Tamang villages and experience local mountain culture.
  • Explore the historic settlement of Kyanjin Gompa.
  • Hike to Kyanjin Ri for spectacular sunrise and panoramic mountain views.
  • Walk through lush forests of rhododendron, pine, and bamboo.
  • Encounter diverse wildlife within Langtang National Park.
  • Experience comfortable teahouse accommodation throughout the trek.
  • Ideal combination of cultural trekking and non-technical peak climbing adventure.

item.title: Upper Mustang Trek – 16 Days (Drive Option) with 2 Nights in Lo Manthang
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Upper Mustang Trek Overview

The 16-day Upper Mustang Trek begins with your arrival in Kathmandu, where our team welcomes you at the airport and transfers you to your hotel. After a trek briefing and preparation, you drive to Pokhara along the scenic Prithvi Highway. The following day, the journey continues through the Kali Gandaki Valley via Tatopani and Marpha before reaching Jomsom, the gateway to the Mustang region.

From Jomsom, the trek starts towards Kagbeni, an ancient village that marks the entrance to the restricted area of Upper Mustang. The trail then passes through traditional settlements such as Chele, Syangboche, Ghami, and Tsarang. Along the way, you walk through dramatic desert landscapes, colorful cliffs, deep valleys, and remote Tibetan-influenced villages. Ancient monasteries, prayer walls, and centuries-old traditions add cultural depth to the journey.

The trek eventually reaches Lo Manthang, the historic walled capital of the former Kingdom of Mustang. You spend two nights here to explore its rich cultural and historical attractions. Visits include ancient monasteries, traditional houses, the royal palace, and nearby Chhoser, which is famous for its mysterious cave complexes carved into the cliffs. This extra time allows for a deeper understanding of the region's Tibetan Buddhist heritage and unique way of life.

After exploring Lo Manthang, the return journey follows a scenic route through Drakmar, Ghiling, and Kagbeni. From Kagbeni, you drive back through Jomsom, Marpha, and Tatopani before reaching Pokhara. The final drive returns you to Kathmandu, completing an unforgettable adventure.

Why choose this trek?

Combining spectacular Himalayan scenery, ancient culture, and remote desert landscapes, this trek offers one of Nepal's most rewarding and distinctive trekking experiences.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Explore the remote Upper Mustang region, a restricted Himalayan area rich in Tibetan culture and traditional villages.

  • Visit Lo Manthang, the walled capital, and enjoy 2 nights in this historic town.

  • Witness stunning Himalayan desert landscapes, cliffs, and canyons.

  • Trek through villages like Kagbeni, Chele, Syangboche, Ghami, Tsarang, and Drakmar.

  • Experience ancient monasteries, mani walls, and prayer flags, reflecting Mustang’s spiritual heritage.

  • Remote trekking with minimal tourist crowds, offering an authentic Himalayan adventure.

  • Opportunities for photography, cultural exploration, and unique landscapes rarely seen by outsiders.

• Airport transfers in Kathmandu (arrival and departure)

  • Accommodation in Kathmandu hotels and teahouses during the trek

  • Full-board meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) during the trek

  • Experienced English-speaking trekking guide and porters

  • Trekking permits and restricted area permits for Upper Mustang

  • National park entry fees where applicable

  • First aid kit and emergency support throughout the trek

  • Transportation from Pokhara to Jomsom and return drives as per itinerary

• International airfare to and from Nepal

  • Travel insurance including emergency evacuation

  • Personal trekking equipment and gear

  • Extra meals, drinks, and snacks outside the trekking plan

• Trekking Boots & Socks: Sturdy, well-broken-in boots and moisture-wicking socks for long trails.

  • Warm Clothing: Layered clothing including down jacket, fleece, thermal wear, and windproof outer layers.

  • Rain Gear: Waterproof jacket and pants to protect against sudden weather changes.

  • Trekking Poles: Helpful for stability on uneven or rocky terrain.

  • Headwear & Gloves: Hat, gloves, and sunglasses to protect from sun, wind, and cold.

  • Backpack: Comfortable daypack with water bottles, snacks, and personal items.

  • Sleeping Bag: Suitable for sub-zero temperatures at high altitude teahouses.

  • Personal Items: Toiletries, sunscreen, lip balm, trekking permits, and first aid essentials.

  • Optional Gear: Camera, binoculars, and personal trekking electronics.

item.title: Chum Valley Trek | Remote Manaslu Cultural Trek Nepal
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Chum Valley Trek Overview

The Chum Valley Trek is a rewarding 16-day journey into one of Nepal’s most remote Himalayan regions. Located in the Manaslu area, this peaceful valley is known for its Tibetan-influenced culture, ancient monasteries, traditional villages, and spectacular mountain scenery. Away from busy trekking routes, the journey offers an authentic experience surrounded by pristine landscapes and welcoming communities.

The adventure begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola. From there, the trail follows the Budhi Gandaki River through forests, terraced fields, suspension bridges, and traditional settlements. Along the way, trekkers pass through Jagat, Lokpa, Chumling, Chhokang Paro, and Nile while experiencing the region’s unique culture and warm hospitality.

Explore the Sacred Chum Valley

One of the major highlights is a visit to Mu Gompa, an important spiritual center in the region. Trekkers can explore ancient Buddhist sites, prayer walls, and traditional settlements while learning about the customs preserved by local communities. The route also provides beautiful views of Ganesh Himal, Himalchuli, and surrounding snow-covered peaks.

Experience Remote Himalayan Landscapes

The trail features deep valleys, alpine meadows, forests, rivers, and rugged mountain terrain. As the elevation increases, gradual acclimatization allows trekkers to adjust comfortably while enjoying changing landscapes. The highest point of the journey reaches approximately 5,160 meters above sea level.

Why Choose the Chum Valley Trek?

This adventure is ideal for travelers looking for a combination of cultural discovery, peaceful trails, and impressive Himalayan scenery. From ancient monasteries and remote villages to dramatic mountain landscapes, every section offers a memorable experience. The Chum Valley Trek provides an excellent opportunity to explore a hidden Himalayan destination while connecting with local traditions and nature.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Hotels in Kathmandu and teahouses during the trek

• Explore the remote and sacred Tsum Valley, often called the “Hidden Valley of Happiness”
  • Visit ancient Buddhist monasteries like Mu Gompa and Rachen Gompa
  • Experience authentic Tibetan-influenced culture and traditional village life
  • Scenic drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola through rivers, hills, and valleys
  • Trek through untouched landscapes of the Manaslu Conservation Area
  • Walk along beautiful Budhi Gandaki River with suspension bridges and deep gorges
  • Spot diverse Himalayan flora, fauna, and peaceful alpine scenery
  • Reach high viewpoints with dramatic views of Manaslu and surrounding peaks

• All airport pick-up and drop-off in Kathmandu
  • 3 nights hotel accommodation in Kathmandu with breakfast
  • Full board meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) during the trek
  • Licensed English-speaking trekking guide
  • Required permits (Manaslu Conservation Area Permit & Tsum Valley Permit)
  • Private jeep transport (Kathmandu – Machha Khola – Kathmandu)
  • Teahouse/lodge accommodation during the trek
  • First aid kit and necessary trekking support equipment

• International airfare to/from Nepal
  • Nepal visa fees and travel insurance
  • Personal expenses (snacks, drinks, phone, laundry)
  • Hot showers, WiFi, and charging fees in teahouses
  • Tips for guide, porter, and driver
  • Porter service (available on request at extra cost)
  • Extra accommodation or meals due to early return/late departure
  • Emergency evacuation or rescue costs (if required)
  • City sightseeing entrance fee

Clothing
• Lightweight trekking pants and shorts
• Moisture-wicking t-shirts (short and long sleeves)
• Insulating fleece or down jacket
• Waterproof and windproof jacket
• Thermal base layers (top and bottom)
• Warm trekking gloves and liner gloves
• Hat or cap for sun protection
• Warm hat/beanie for high altitudes
• Neck gaiter or buff
• Trekking socks (wool or synthetic)
• Gaiters (optional, for snow or mud)

Footwear
• Sturdy trekking boots (well broken-in, waterproof)
• Lightweight camp shoes or sandals for evenings

Backpack & Accessories
• Daypack (20–30L) for daily essentials
• Waterproof backpack cover or dry bags
• Duffel bag for porters (optional, can be provided)

Sleeping & Camping Gear
• Sleeping bag (rated -10°C to -15°C for high altitudes)
• Sleeping bag liner (optional for extra warmth)
• Trekking poles

Health & Safety
• Personal first aid kit (plasters, painkillers, blister pads)
• Sunscreen (SPF 50+) and lip balm
• Sunglasses with UV protection
• Water bottles or hydration bladder
• Water purification tablets or filter
• Headlamp with spare batteries
• Personal medications

Miscellaneous
• Camera or smartphone with extra memory cards
• Power bank or solar charger
• Notebook or trekking journal (optional)
• Snacks/energy bars
• Toilet paper and wet wipes
• Hand sanitizer

item.title: Manaslu and Chum Valley 19 days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Discover the Manaslu and Chum Valley Trek

The Manaslu Chum Valley Trek is a remarkable 19-day journey through Nepal’s remote Himalayan landscapes. The adventure combines spectacular mountain scenery, peaceful villages, ancient Buddhist monasteries, and authentic local culture. Away from the busier Everest and Annapurna routes, this trail offers a quieter and more immersive experience for travelers seeking natural beauty and cultural discovery.

Explore the Sacred Chum Valley

Located near the Tibetan border, Chum Valley is known for its unique traditions and spiritual heritage. The trail passes through traditional villages, ancient monasteries, prayer walls, and sacred sites. Trekkers can experience the daily lifestyle of local communities while enjoying the peaceful surroundings and warm hospitality.

Experience Diverse Himalayan Landscapes

The journey moves through terraced hillsides, lush forests, rushing rivers, and remote mountain settlements. As you gain altitude, the landscape changes into alpine meadows and rugged Himalayan terrain. Along the way, you can enjoy impressive views of Mount Manaslu (8,163 m), Ganesh Himal, Himlung Himal, and other snow-covered peaks.

Cross the Larkya La Pass

A major highlight of this adventure is crossing Larkya La Pass at 5,106 meters. The challenging ascent rewards trekkers with breathtaking views of glaciers, towering peaks, and deep Himalayan valleys. Reaching the pass creates a memorable sense of achievement before the trail gradually descends through scenic mountain settlements.

Why Choose the Manaslu Chum Valley Trek?

This 19-day Himalayan adventure is ideal for travelers who want a combination of challenging trails, cultural experiences, and spectacular scenery. From the sacred landscapes of Chum Valley to the dramatic crossing of Larkya La Pass, every section offers something unique. With remote villages, centuries-old traditions, and unforgettable mountain views, the Manaslu Chum Valley Trek provides an authentic experience away from Nepal’s crowded trekking routes.

llenging trails, cultural discovery, and breathtaking Himalayan views, the Manaslu and Chum Valley Trek is an excellent choice for travelers seeking a quieter and more authentic Himalayan experience.

item.title: Makalu Base Camp Trek – 18 Days Himalayan Adventure
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Explore the Remote Makalu Region

The Makalu Base Camp Trek is an 18-day Himalayan adventure through one of Nepal’s most remote and spectacular trekking regions. Far from the busy trails of Everest and Annapurna, this journey offers dramatic mountain scenery, traditional villages, rich cultural heritage, and an exceptional wilderness experience. The route leads toward the base of Mount Makalu (8,485 m), the fifth-highest mountain in the world. The adventure begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar, followed by a drive to Num. From here, the trail winds through traditional Rai and Sherpa villages, where you can experience local customs, welcoming communities, and the unique lifestyle of people living in the eastern Himalayas.

Diverse Landscapes and Natural Beauty

One of the most remarkable features of this journey is its incredible natural diversity. The trail passes through Makalu Barun National Park, an area renowned for its rich biodiversity and pristine mountain environment. As you gain altitude, the landscape gradually changes from lush subtropical forests filled with rhododendrons and bamboo to alpine meadows, rocky valleys, glaciers, and rugged high-altitude terrain. The changing scenery makes every stage of the adventure unique. You will cross suspension bridges, walk beside cascading rivers, and follow remote mountain trails surrounded by impressive Himalayan landscapes. The peaceful environment also provides excellent opportunities for photography and wildlife observation.

Spectacular Himalayan Mountain Views

Throughout the route, trekkers can enjoy magnificent views of Makalu, Chamlang, Baruntse, Mera Peak, and numerous other snow-covered mountains. As the trail approaches higher elevations, the surrounding peaks become increasingly dramatic. Reaching Makalu Base Camp (4,870 m) is the major highlight of the expedition. Standing beneath the towering south face of Mount Makalu creates an unforgettable sense of achievement. The remote setting, powerful mountain scenery, and peaceful surroundings make the destination particularly rewarding for experienced trekkers.

An Off-the-Beaten-Path Himalayan Adventure

This journey is ideal for experienced trekkers who want to explore a quieter and less-developed region of Nepal. Compared with more popular trekking routes, the trail offers greater solitude and a stronger connection with nature and local communities. The combination of challenging trails, diverse landscapes, traditional villages, rich biodiversity, and spectacular mountain views makes this 18-day adventure an excellent choice for travelers seeking something beyond the usual Himalayan routes. From the lower forests to the high alpine wilderness, every section reveals a different side of eastern Nepal and creates lasting memories of an extraordinary mountain expedition.

Makalu Base Camp Trek – 18 Days Himalayan Adventure in Nepal %%page%% %%sep%% %%sitename%%
Makalu Base Camp Trek takes you through remote Himalayan villages, pristine wilderness, and breathtaking mountain scenery in eastern Nepal.
Makalu Base Camp Trek 18-day is a Himalayan adventure through remote villages, diverse landscapes, Makalu Barun National Park, and stunning mountain scenery.

item.title: Lower Dolpo & Phoksundo Lake Trek–16 Days
item.dc:creator: kabita
item.content:encoded:
Explore the Remote Dolpo Region

The Lower Dolpo & Phoksundo Lake Trek is a spectacular 16-day wilderness adventure through one of Nepal’s most remote and culturally fascinating regions. The journey takes you through untouched valleys, rugged mountain landscapes, traditional villages, and areas strongly influenced by Tibetan culture. Far from Nepal’s busier trekking routes, the region offers a peaceful experience surrounded by dramatic scenery and pristine nature. The adventure begins in Kathmandu with a flight to Nepalgunj, followed by a flight to Juphal, the gateway to the Dolpo region. From here, the trail passes through traditional settlements, terraced fields, deep river valleys, and rugged mountain terrain. Along the way, you will encounter local communities whose customs and lifestyles have been preserved for generations.

Journey Through the Himalayan Wilderness

The route passes through places such as Dunai, Tarakot, Laini, and Nawarpani before reaching higher and more remote landscapes. As the trail climbs, green valleys gradually give way to dramatic cliffs, rocky slopes, and high mountain scenery. A major highlight is Dho Tarap, one of Nepal’s highest permanent settlements. This remote Himalayan village provides an excellent opportunity to experience local culture while acclimatizing to the increasing altitude. Surrounded by impressive mountains and traditional homes, the settlement offers a fascinating glimpse into life in the Dolpo region. The trail then crosses remote valleys and challenging mountain passes before continuing toward Numa La Base Camp and Pelung Tang. The changing landscapes, colorful rock formations, deep valleys, and panoramic Himalayan views make this section particularly rewarding for adventurous trekkers.

Discover the Beauty of Phoksundo Lake

The spectacular Phoksundo Lake is the crown jewel of the journey. Famous for its brilliant turquoise waters, the lake is surrounded by dramatic cliffs, forests, and cascading waterfalls, creating one of Nepal’s most remarkable natural landscapes. Reaching the lake provides a memorable opportunity to appreciate the peaceful beauty of the region and explore its surrounding trails. The area is also known for its unique cultural heritage, traditional villages, and connection to the ancient Bon and Tibetan Buddhist traditions.

An Unforgettable Himalayan Adventure

This journey is ideal for experienced trekkers seeking solitude, cultural immersion, and extraordinary natural scenery. The combination of remote mountain trails, traditional communities, high-altitude landscapes, and the magnificent Phoksundo Lake creates an unforgettable Himalayan experience. With its untouched wilderness and distinctive cultural character, the Dolpo region offers a rewarding alternative to Nepal’s more crowded trekking destinations. From remote villages and rugged passes to the turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake, every stage of the adventure reveals a different side of Nepal’s spectacular western Himalayas.

• Explore the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang, the former kingdom of Mustang.

  • Visit Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and the royal palace.

  • Discover the sky caves of Chhoser, carved into cliffs centuries ago.

  • Experience the unique desert landscapes and barren cliffs of Upper Mustang.

  • Interact with the local Tibetan-influenced culture and traditions.

  • Walk through remote villages like Kagbeni, Chele, Syangboche, Ghami, and Tsarang.

  • Witness breathtaking high-altitude desert scenery and panoramic Himalayan views.

  • Enjoy two nights of cultural immersion in Lo Manthang.

item.title: Gokyo Valley Trek – 14 Days
item.dc:creator: flyup-7
item.content:encoded:
Explore the Gokyo Valley

The Gokyo Valley Trek is a spectacular 14-day journey through Nepal’s Everest region, combining peaceful mountain landscapes, traditional Sherpa villages, turquoise alpine lakes, and breathtaking Himalayan views. It offers a quieter alternative to the busier Everest Base Camp route while providing an unforgettable high-altitude experience. The adventure begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. From there, the trail follows the Dudh Koshi River through lush forests, suspension bridges, and charming mountain settlements before reaching Namche Bazaar. This vibrant Sherpa town is an important acclimatization stop and provides an opportunity to experience local culture while enjoying views of the surrounding peaks. After Namche, the route leaves the main Everest trail and heads toward Dole and Machhermo. As you climb higher, the landscape gradually changes from green forests to alpine valleys surrounded by impressive Himalayan peaks. The trail eventually reaches Gokyo, a beautiful lakeside settlement surrounded by mountains and glaciers.

Gokyo Ri and Himalayan Panoramas

One of the major highlights is the early morning ascent of Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). From the summit, trekkers can enjoy panoramic views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and the enormous Ngozumpa Glacier. The sunrise over the Himalayan peaks creates a memorable experience and offers excellent opportunities for photography. The Gokyo Lakes are another remarkable attraction along the route. Their clear turquoise waters, surrounded by rugged mountains and glaciers, create one of the most beautiful landscapes in the Everest region. The journey also provides opportunities to experience authentic Sherpa traditions and observe the unique lifestyle of communities living in the high Himalayas.

A Peaceful Himalayan Adventure

Carefully planned acclimatization helps you adjust gradually to the increasing altitude. The combination of scenic trails, mountain villages, alpine landscapes, and spectacular viewpoints makes this journey ideal for travelers looking for adventure, natural beauty, and cultural experiences. After exploring the Gokyo region, the trail descends toward Lukla. A scenic flight then returns you to Kathmandu, where you can relax, explore the city, or prepare for your onward journey. With its stunning scenery, peaceful trails, and unforgettable mountain views, this 14-day Himalayan adventure is an excellent way to experience the beauty of Nepal’s Everest region.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Hotel in Kathmandu & Teahouses During Trek

• Scenic mountain flight between Kathmandu and Lukla
  • Explore the vibrant Sherpa town of Namche Bazaar
  • Acclimatization hike with stunning Himalayan views
  • Trek through peaceful and less-crowded Gokyo Valley
  • Visit the magnificent Gokyo Lakes
  • Sunrise hike to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m)
  • Panoramic views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu
  • Experience authentic Sherpa culture and hospitality
  • Walk alongside the massive Ngozumpa Glacier
  • Comfortable airport-to-airport service in Nepal

• Airport pick-up and drop-off services in Kathmandu.
  • All ground transportation as per the itinerary.
  • Two nights hotel accommodation in Kathmandu on a twin-sharing basis with breakfast.
  • Domestic flight ticket from Kathmandu to Lukla and Lukla to Kathmandu.
  • Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit.
  • Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit.
  • Experienced, government-licensed English-speaking trekking guide.
  • Porter service (one porter for every two trekkers).
  • All guide and porter expenses, including meals, accommodation, salary, insurance, and transportation.
  • Teahouse accommodation during the trek on a twin-sharing basis.
  • Three meals a day (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) during the trek.
  • First aid medical kit carried by the guide.
  • All applicable government taxes and service charges.

• International airfare to and from Nepal.
  • Nepal entry visa fees.
  • Travel and rescue insurance.
  • Personal trekking equipment and gear.
  • Lunch and dinner in Kathmandu.
  • Additional hotel nights in Kathmandu due to early arrival, late departure, or flight delays.
  • Personal expenses such as laundry, telephone calls, internet, hot showers, charging devices, and drinks.
  • Bottled water, soft drinks, alcoholic beverages, and snacks.
  • Tips for guides, porters, and support staff.
  • Emergency evacuation and rescue expenses.
  • Costs arising from flight delays, cancellations, natural disasters, political disturbances, or unforeseen circumstances beyond our control.
  • Any services not specifically mentioned in the "Package Includes" section.

🎒 Backpack & Bags

  • Duffel bag (60–80L)
  • Daypack (25–35L)
  • Rain cover

👕 Clothing

  • Trekking T-shirts (2–3)
  • Trekking pants (2 pairs)
  • Thermal base layers
  • Fleece jacket
  • Down jacket
  • Waterproof jacket & pants
  • Warm hat and sun hat
  • Gloves

👞 Footwear

  • Waterproof trekking boots
  • Camp shoes/sandals
  • Trekking socks (4–5 pairs)
  • Warm wool socks

🥾 Trekking Equipment

  • Sleeping bag (-10°C to -15°C)
  • Trekking poles
  • Headlamp
  • Water bottles or hydration bladder
  • Sunglasses
  • Power bank

🧴 Personal Items

  • Sunscreen
  • Lip balm
  • Personal medications
  • Basic first-aid kit
  • Toiletries
  • Wet wipes and hand sanitizer

❄️ Note: Temperatures at Gokyo and Gokyo Ri can drop below freezing, so warm layers and a good sleeping bag are highly recommended.

Welcome to Nepal. After arriving at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, our representative will receive you and transfer you to your hotel. After check-in, you can rest from your journey or explore nearby streets, markets, and cafés. Kathmandu is a lively city with a mix of cultural heritage, temples, and modern travel facilities. In the evening, you will meet your trekking guide for a short briefing about the Gokyo Valley Trek, including route details, equipment checks, permits, and final preparation.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:41:"Tribhuvan International Airport (1,350 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:22:" 30–45 minutes drive";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:21:"Airport transfer only";s:14:"important_note";s:193:"Please keep your passport, travel insurance, trekking permits, and flight documents ready. Early in the morning, you will take a scenic mountain flight to Lukla, the gateway to the Everest region. The flight offers beautiful views of hills, valleys, and Himalayan peaks. After landing at Lukla, you will meet the porter team and begin your trek towards Phakding. The trail descends gently through small Sherpa villages, forests, prayer wheels, and suspension bridges. This first trekking day is short and comfortable, allowing your body to adjust slowly to the mountain environment.

Today’s trek follows the Dudh Koshi River through pine forests, villages, and several suspension bridges. You will pass places like Monjo and Jorsalle before entering Sagarmatha National Park. After crossing the famous high suspension bridge, the trail climbs steeply towards Namche Bazaar. On a clear day, you may get your first glimpse of Mt. Everest during the climb. Namche Bazaar is the main trading hub of the Everest region, with shops, bakeries, lodges, and beautiful mountain views.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Phakding (2,610 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 10–12 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:170:"Today includes a long uphill section before Namche Bazaar. Walk slowly, drink enough water, and avoid rushing because altitude gain becomes more noticeable from this day.";}s:6:"item-3";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:43:"Day 4: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:477:"

Today is an important acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. You can take a short hike to the Everest View Hotel or nearby viewpoints for excellent views of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other Himalayan peaks. The hike helps your body adjust to the altitude before moving higher. After returning to Namche, you can explore the local market, Sherpa culture museum, cafés, and traditional streets. This rest day is very useful for both safety and enjoyment.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:29:"Optional acclimatization hike";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:25:"3–5 hours optional hike";s:14:"important_note";s:132:"Acclimatization does not mean sleeping all day. A short hike and return to the same sleeping altitude helps your body adjust better.";}s:6:"item-4";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:57:"Day 5: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Dole (4038m / 13248 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:488:"

After breakfast, the trail begins with beautiful mountain views and gradually separates from the main Everest Base Camp route. You will walk towards the quieter Gokyo Valley route through rhododendron forests, small settlements, and open hillsides. The trail passes near Mong La and Phortse Tenga before climbing towards Dole. As you move higher, the landscape becomes more peaceful and remote. Dole is a small mountain village surrounded by hills and beautiful Himalayan scenery.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:14:"Dole (4,038 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 11–13 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:" 5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:158:"The altitude crosses 4,000 meters today, so it is important to walk slowly. Keep yourself warm and avoid unnecessary physical effort after reaching the lodge.";}s:6:"item-5";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:53:"Day 6: Trek from Dole to Machhermo (4470m / 14665 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:488:"

Today’s trek is shorter but the altitude continues to increase. The trail climbs gradually through open valleys, yak grazing areas, and small settlements such as Luza and Lhafarma. You will enjoy wide mountain landscapes and peaceful surroundings throughout the day. Machhermo is a beautiful village located below rocky hills and snow-capped peaks. After reaching Machhermo, you can rest, walk around the village slowly, and prepare your body for the higher altitude near Gokyo.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:14:"Dole (4,038 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Machhermo (4,470 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:22:" Approx. 7–9 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"4–5 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:171:"This is a high-altitude trekking day. Today you will trek towards the beautiful Gokyo Valley, one of the most scenic destinations in the Everest region. The trail gradually climbs through high alpine landscapes with views of Cho Oyu and surrounding peaks. On the way, you will pass the first and second Gokyo Lakes before reaching the main Gokyo village beside the stunning third lake, Dudh Pokhari. The blue lake, mountain reflections, and peaceful setting make Gokyo one of the most beautiful places in the Himalayas.

Early in the morning, you will hike to Gokyo Ri, one of the best viewpoints in the Everest region. From the top, you can enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and the massive Ngozumpa Glacier. The sunrise view from Gokyo Ri is truly unforgettable. After enjoying the views, you will descend back to Gokyo for breakfast and rest. Later, you can explore nearby Gokyo Lakes and enjoy the peaceful beauty of the valley.

After enjoying the beauty of Gokyo Valley, you will begin your return journey towards Dole. The trail descends gradually through the same high-altitude landscapes, passing lakes, yak pastures, and small mountain settlements. As you lose elevation, breathing becomes easier and the temperature feels more comfortable. The return walk offers a different perspective of the valley and surrounding peaks. You will reach Dole by afternoon and rest at a local teahouse.

Today you will continue descending towards Namche Bazaar. The trail passes through forests, small villages, and scenic viewpoints. You will again pass Phortse Tenga and Mong La before joining the main route back to Namche. The walk offers beautiful views of Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other peaks. After reaching Namche Bazaar, you can enjoy better lodge facilities, hot drinks, bakeries, and a relaxed evening in the lively Sherpa town.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:14:"Dole (4,038 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 11–13 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:132:"The trail has both downhill and uphill sections, so do not underestimate the day. This is the final trekking day of the Gokyo Valley Trek. The trail descends steeply from Namche Bazaar towards the Dudh Koshi River and continues through familiar villages, forests, and suspension bridges. You will pass Monjo, Phakding, and other small settlements before climbing gradually back to Lukla. After reaching Lukla, you can celebrate the successful completion of your trek with your guide and porter team. It is a special evening to remember your journey through the Everest and Gokyo region.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:23:"Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:" Lukla (2,860 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:23:"Approx. 18–20 km trek";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:157:"This is a long walking day, so start early and walk carefully, especially on downhill sections. Confirm the next morning’s flight schedule with your guide.";}s:7:"item-11";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:53:"Day 12: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu (1350m / 4412 ft)";s:11:"description";s:0:"";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:471:"

Early in the morning, you will take a scenic flight from Lukla back to Kathmandu. The flight offers one final view of the Himalayan landscape before returning to the capital city. After arriving in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you to your hotel. The rest of the day is free for rest, hot shower, laundry, or a short walk around nearby markets. After several days in the mountains, this day gives you time to relax and enjoy the comfort of the city.

";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:" Lukla (2,860 m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:19:"Kathmandu (1,350 m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:51:"30–35 minutes flight and 30–45 minutes transfer";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:26:" Flight and hotel transfer";s:14:"important_note";s:146:"Lukla flights can be delayed or cancelled due to weather. Today is a free day in Kathmandu after returning from the trek. You can use this day for rest, shopping, souvenir buying, massage, or exploring cultural places around the city. If you are interested, you can visit popular heritage sites such as Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, Swayambhunath, or Kathmandu Durbar Square. This day also works as a useful buffer day in case the Lukla flight gets delayed due to weather. In the evening, you can enjoy a farewell dinner or spend your final night peacefully in Kathmandu.

item.title: Upper Mustang Jeep Tour – 12 Days Standard Itinerary
item.dc:creator: flyup-7
item.content:encoded:
The Upper Mustang Jeep Tour is one of Nepal's most unique overland adventures. It takes travelers deep into the hidden Himalayan kingdom of Mustang. Once an independent Tibetan kingdom, Upper Mustang has preserved its culture and traditions for centuries. Today, it is known for its ancient monasteries, cave settlements, medieval villages, and dramatic desert landscapes.

This 12-day journey begins in Kathmandu and continues to Pokhara. From there, travelers enter the Kali Gandaki Valley by private 4WD jeep. The route passes through Kagbeni, Chhusang, Samar, Ghami, Tsarang, and Lo Manthang. Along the way, visitors enjoy breathtaking Himalayan scenery and authentic Tibetan-influenced culture. The tour offers a unique opportunity to explore one of Nepal's most remote regions. Travelers can visit traditional villages, historic monasteries, and sacred Buddhist sites. Additionally, the route features spectacular cliffs, deep canyons, and colorful rock formations. These landscapes create a truly unforgettable travel experience.

Lo Manthang is the cultural heart of Upper Mustang. This historic walled city served as the capital of the former Kingdom of Mustang. Visitors can walk through narrow streets, explore ancient palaces, and observe local traditions. Furthermore, the city provides excellent insight into the region's rich history and heritage. The itinerary also includes an excursion to the famous Chhoser Cave area. These ancient caves were carved into cliffs centuries ago and remain one of Mustang's most fascinating attractions. Upper Mustang is deeply connected to Tibetan Buddhism. Throughout the journey, travelers encounter prayer flags, chortens, monasteries, and sacred sites. Moreover, local communities continue to practice traditions that have been preserved for generations.

Why Choose the Upper Mustang Jeep Tour?

The Upper Mustang Jeep Tour is ideal for travelers who prefer comfort while exploring remote destinations. Unlike trekking, a jeep tour allows visitors to cover greater distances in less time. Finally, the return journey includes a visit to the sacred Muktinath Temple, making this adventure both culturally enriching and spiritually rewarding.

item.title: Langtang Valley Comfort Trek – 9 Days
item.dc:creator: Everpeak
item.content:encoded:
Why Choose the Langtang Valley Comfort Trek?

The Langtang Valley Comfort Trek is a carefully designed 9-day Himalayan adventure combining breathtaking mountain scenery, authentic Tamang culture, and comfortable lodge accommodation. It offers an excellent balance of adventure and relaxation, making it ideal for travelers who want to explore the Himalayas without sacrificing comfort. Your journey begins with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi, the gateway to the Langtang region. From here, the trail passes through lush rhododendron and bamboo forests, crosses suspension bridges, and follows peaceful mountain rivers. Along the way, you will encounter traditional Tamang villages and experience the warm hospitality and unique culture of local communities.

Discover the Beauty of Langtang Valley

As you continue higher, the landscape gradually changes from dense forests to beautiful alpine meadows and dramatic Himalayan terrain. The trail provides spectacular views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Langshisa Ri, and other surrounding peaks. One of the major highlights is reaching Kyanjin Gompa, a peaceful mountain settlement surrounded by impressive peaks. You can explore the historic monastery, enjoy the mountain scenery, and experience the unique atmosphere of this remote Himalayan village. An early morning hike toward Kyanjin Ri provides panoramic views and unforgettable sunrise scenery.

A Comfortable Himalayan Adventure

This 9-day journey is perfect for travelers seeking a comfortable way to experience the natural and cultural beauty of Nepal. Comfortable lodges, delicious local meals, and carefully planned walking distances make each day more enjoyable while allowing sufficient time to appreciate the surrounding environment. The route is also less crowded than some of Nepal’s more popular trekking areas, offering a peaceful experience through forests, villages, and high mountain landscapes. Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or returning for another Himalayan adventure, this Langtang trek offers a memorable combination of nature, culture, comfort, and mountain scenery. For travelers interested in exploring other regions of Nepal, you can also visit our Gokyo Valley Trek or explore our other Himalayan trekking packages for additional adventure options.

You will pass through several local towns and may experience rough road sections, especially near the Pahiro area, which is known for landslide-prone terrain. Despite the challenging road conditions, the journey is highly scenic and gives your first real glimpse of rural Himalayan life. By late afternoon, you reach the Pahiro/Syabrubesi area for an overnight stay.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:27:"Hotel in Kathmandu (1,400m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:31:"Pahiro (Approx. 1,200–1,400m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:18:"Approx. 80–90 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"5–6 hours drive";s:14:"important_note";s:81:"Road conditions can be rough and affected by landslides, so travel time may vary.";}s:6:"item-2";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:45:"Day 3: Pahiro to Ghodatabela (3,000m approx.)";s:11:"description";s:641:"Today marks your first trekking day in the Langtang Valley. After breakfast, you begin your hike from Pahiro, following a scenic trail that gradually ascends through dense forests, suspension bridges, and riverside paths. The sound of flowing rivers and waterfalls accompanies you as you move deeper into the Langtang region.
Along the way, you may spot wildlife, yak caravans, and small resting points used by trekkers. The trail becomes more peaceful and surrounded by alpine forest as you approach Ghodatabela. This area is known for its wide open valley views and fresh mountain air, making it a perfect place to end the day’s trek.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:37:"Pahiro (Approx. 1,200–1,400 meters)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:28:"Ghodatabela (Approx. 3,000m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:18:"Approx. 10–12 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"6–7 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:85:"Steady ascent with moderate difficulty. Stay hydrated and walk at a comfortable pace.";}s:6:"item-3";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:44:"Day 4: Ghodatabela to Kyanjin Gompa (3,870m)";s:11:"description";s:661:"After breakfast, you continue your trek deeper into the Langtang Valley, gradually leaving the forest zone behind and entering wide alpine landscapes. The trail opens up with spectacular views of snow-covered peaks, yak pastures, and traditional Tamang settlements along the way.
As you ascend steadily, you will pass through small villages like Langtang area remnants and open valley sections shaped by the 2015 earthquake, now beautifully rebuilt. The scenery becomes more dramatic as Langtang Lirung and surrounding peaks dominate the horizon. By afternoon, you reach Kyanjin Gompa, the spiritual heart of the valley, surrounded by mountains and glaciers.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:34:"Ghodatabela (Approx. 3,030 meters)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:22:"Kyanjin Gompa (3,870m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:16:"Approx. 6–8 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"3–4 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:69:"Altitude gain is noticeable; take it slow for proper acclimatization.";}s:6:"item-4";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:66:"Day 5: Acclimatization & Exploration at Kyanjin Gompa (3,870m)";s:11:"description";s:633:"Today is a rest and exploration day in the beautiful Kyanjin Valley. Early in the morning, you can hike up to Kyanjin Ri, one of the best viewpoints in the Langtang region, offering panoramic views of Langtang Lirung, glaciers, icefalls, and surrounding Himalayan peaks. The climb is steep but highly rewarding with unforgettable scenery.
After returning, you can explore Kyanjin Gompa village, visit the ancient monastery, and optionally tour the local cheese factory to experience traditional yak cheese production. The rest of the day is free to relax, enjoy the mountain atmosphere, and acclimatize properly before descending.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:28:"Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 meters)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:13:"Kyanjin Gompa";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:38:"Approx. 5–10 km (hike to Kyanjin Ri)";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:36:"4–6 hours (hike & exploration)";s:14:"important_note";s:94:"Important acclimatization day. Do not rush the hike; maintain a steady pace and stay hydrated.";}s:6:"item-5";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:62:"Day 6: Trek from Kyanjin Gompa to Ghodatabela (3,000m approx.)";s:11:"description";s:656:"After breakfast, you begin your descent from Kyanjin Gompa, retracing your steps back through the beautiful Langtang Valley. The trail offers a completely different perspective of the landscapes you climbed earlier, with wide alpine valleys, yak pastures, and distant snow peaks gradually giving way to forested sections.
The downhill walk is long but comfortable, passing through scenic viewpoints, small settlements, and river crossings. As you lose altitude, the air becomes warmer and the vegetation gradually turns dense again. By late afternoon, you arrive at Ghodatabela, where you will rest for the night surrounded by peaceful mountain scenery.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Kyanjin Gompa";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:28:"Ghodatabela (Approx. 3,000m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:18:"Approx. 10–12 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:91:"Long descent day. The trail is peaceful and less crowded, offering a relaxing walking experience compared to the higher alpine sections. Along the way, you will pass suspension bridges, waterfalls, and local Tamang villages that reflect the culture of the Langtang region.
By afternoon, you reach Sherpa Gaun, a quiet and beautiful village known for its authentic mountain lifestyle and warm hospitality. It is a perfect place to rest and experience local culture after several days of trekking in higher altitudes.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:11:"Ghodatabela";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:28:"Sherpa Gaun (2,500–2,600m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:17:"Approx. 8–10 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:16:"5–6 hours trek";s:14:"important_note";s:91:"Mostly downhill and forest trail. The drive follows the same scenic mountain highway, passing through rivers, green hills, waterfalls, and rural settlements. Along the way, you can enjoy the final views of the Langtang region before descending fully into the Kathmandu Valley.
This is a long but comfortable drive that gives you time to relax and reflect on the completed trek. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel where you can rest, shop, or explore the city one last time.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:35:"Sherpa Gaun / Syabrubesi road point";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:18:"Hotel in Kathmandu";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:20:"Approx. 120–130 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:17:"7–8 hours drive";s:14:"important_note";s:77:"Long scenic drive. This marks the end of your 9 Days Langtang Valley Comfort Trek, filled with beautiful mountain landscapes, cultural villages, and unforgettable Himalayan experiences. Safe travels and hope to see you again for another adventure in Nepal.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:18:"Hotel in Kathmandu";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:31:"Tribhuvan International Airport";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:17:"Approx. 5–10 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:21:"30–35 minutes drive";s:14:"important_note";s:76:"Departure day. Langtang Valley Comfort Trek is a 9-day Himalayan adventure with stunning mountain views, Tamang culture, comfortable lodges, and Kyanjin Gompa.

item.title: Everest Luxury Trek with Heli Return
item.dc:creator: Everpeak
item.content:encoded:
Experience the Ultimate Everest Luxury Trek

The Everest Luxury Trek with Helicopter Return is the perfect choice for travelers who want to experience the Everest region in comfort. It combines scenic trekking, luxury mountain lodges, and a breathtaking helicopter flight back to Kathmandu. As a result, you can enjoy the beauty of the Himalayas without retracing the same trail.

A Scenic Journey Through the Everest Region

Your adventure begins with a spectacular flight to Lukla. From there, you trek through the heart of Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Along the way, you pass traditional Sherpa villages, ancient monasteries, colorful prayer flags, and suspension bridges. In addition, every day offers magnificent views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and many other Himalayan peaks.

Luxury Accommodation and Better Comfort

Unlike the standard Everest Base Camp Trek, this luxury trek includes the best available accommodation along the route. Whenever possible, you stay in comfortable mountain lodges with private rooms and modern facilities. Moreover, you enjoy warm hospitality, delicious meals, and personalized service throughout the journey. The itinerary also includes proper acclimatization days, making your trek safer and more enjoyable.

Helicopter Return from Everest

One of the highlights of this adventure is the scenic helicopter flight back from Gorak Shep after visiting Kala Patthar. Instead of trekking back to Lukla, you fly over glaciers, deep valleys, and snow-covered Himalayan peaks. Consequently, you save several days of walking while enjoying spectacular aerial views of the Everest region. This unforgettable flight adds a unique and luxurious finish to your adventure.

Why Choose the Everest Luxury Trek with Helicopter Return?

Whether you are celebrating a special occasion, planning a honeymoon, or simply seeking a premium Himalayan adventure, this trek is an excellent choice. It offers the perfect balance of adventure, comfort, culture, and breathtaking scenery. Furthermore, our experienced guides, carefully selected accommodations, and professional service ensure a smooth and memorable experience from start to finish.

  • Trek through the legendary Sherpa villages of Lukla, Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche, Dingboche, and Lobuche
  • Visit the famous Tengboche Monastery, the spiritual heart of the Khumbu region

Clothing

Footwear

First Aid & Medication

We pass through a picturesque village with fields of buckwheat, potatoes, and vegetables, then continue toward Imja Village and Lobuche Khola before ascending to Dingboche. Upon arrival, we enjoy spectacular views of Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and many other surrounding peaks. Overnight stay is at a tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:15:"Tengboche3880M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:6:"10.5KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"5H";s:14:"important_note";s:171:"You are now entering high altitude zone. Walk slowly and maintain your breathing rhythm. Do not ignore symptoms of altitude sickness. Inform your guide if you feel unwell.";}s:6:"item-6";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:39:"Day 7: Acclimatization day in Dingboche";s:11:"description";s:861:"Today is a crucial acclimatization day to help our bodies adjust to the high altitude. After a hearty breakfast, we embark on a rewarding short hike toward Nagarjun Hill, where we are treated to awe-inspiring panoramic views of some of the most iconic Himalayan peaks, including Ama Dablam, Makalu, Lhotse, Tawache, Cholatse, and numerous other majestic peaks that punctuate the skyline. The crisp mountain air, sweeping vistas, and serene landscapes make this hike an unforgettable experience, offering countless photo opportunities and moments of reflection. After soaking in these magnificent Himalayan panoramas, we gently descend back to Dingboche, where we enjoy a leisurely lunch and rest, letting our bodies recover and prepare for the adventures ahead. Overnight stay is at the same charming tea house, surrounded by the serene beauty of the mountains.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:5:"3.5KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"3H";s:14:"important_note";s:162:"This rest day is critical for successful trek completion. Do not remain completely inactive, but avoid heavy effort. Follow your guide’s instructions carefully.";}s:6:"item-7";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:45:"Day 8: Dingboche to Lobuche(5h/4900m/16000ft)";s:11:"description";s:742:"After breakfast, we continue our trek along the rocky lateral moraine of the Khumbu Glacier, walking on a rugged trail with dramatic views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks. Along the way, we pass the memorial site at Thukla, where stone monuments stand in honor of climbers who lost their lives while attempting nearby summits — a quiet and emotional place that invites reflection. From here, the trail climbs steadily uphill for some time before leveling out as we follow the glacial valley toward Lobuche. Surrounded by towering mountains and vast alpine landscapes, we finally reach Lobuche (4,910 m), a small settlement with a few tea houses serving trekkers and climbers on the Everest Base Camp route. Overnight stay at a tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Dingboche(4410M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:14:"Lobuche(4940M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:3:"9KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"5H";s:14:"important_note";s:150:"Temperature drops significantly at this altitude. Wear proper warm clothing. Keep your body warm and stay hydrated. Avoid unnecessary physical stress.";}s:6:"item-8";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:82:"Day 9:Lobuche to Everest base camp(5360m/17450ft)Back to Gorak shep(5180m/16960ft)";s:11:"description";s:587:"Finally the most Awaiting day of hour whole trip as we climb to Everest Base Camp is Today. This is a big & difficult day walk along the Khumbu glacier up to base camp. Early morning breakfast then we start our journey towards Gorakshep. The trail gradually & Rockey all the way, once we reach in Gorakshep we chick into the hotel and have some rest, we continue up the edge of the Khumbu glacier until we finally reach base camp. if you are lucky & timing is right you may see expedition team. after spending some time to enjoying, we back way down to gorakshep.over night at tea house.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:14:"Lobuche(4940M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:16:"Gorakshep(5160M)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:7:" 14.5KM";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:2:"7H";s:14:"important_note";s:162:"This is a long and difficult day. Walk slowly and conserve energy. Stay with your group and follow your guide. Weather conditions can be harsh, so dress properly.";}s:6:"item-9";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:99:"Day 10: Morning Hike to Kala Patthar, Descent to Gorak Shep & Shared Helicopter Flight to Lukla";s:11:"description";s:1285:"Today, we hike to Kala Patthar, the highest point of the Everest Base Camp Trek. We start early in the morning to enjoy a spectacular sunrise over the majestic Himalayan peaks. From Kala Patthar, you can admire breathtaking views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Pumori, and the surrounding mountains. After enjoying the panoramic views, we descend to Gorak Shep for breakfast. From there, we take a shared helicopter flight to Lukla. Please note that the helicopter flight is shared, not a private charter. If you prefer a private helicopter flight, please contact us for the additional cost.
Due to aviation limitations at high altitudes above 4,500 meters, helicopters can land at Gorak Shep but can take off with a maximum of three passengers at a time. If there are more than three passengers, the helicopter will first take three passengers from Gorak Shep and drop them at a designated location below 4,500 meters, usually Pheriche. The helicopter will then return to Gorak Shep to pick up the remaining passengers. After collecting the first group from the designated location, it will continue to Lukla with everyone together. The helicopter flight from Gorak Shep to Lukla takes approximately 15–20 minutes, depending on weather conditions and the number of passengers.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:16:"Gorakshep(5160M)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:13:"Lukla (2800m)";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:6:"4.4 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:33:"4-5 hrs trek & 20 mins flight";s:14:"important_note";s:391:"The shared helicopter service is subject to weather conditions, passenger availability, and Civil Aviation Authority regulations. During peak trekking seasons, short waiting times or shuttle transfers may be required due to helicopter weight restrictions at high altitude. We recommend keeping your travel schedule flexible, as mountain weather can occasionally cause delays or rescheduling.";}s:7:"item-10";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:88:"Day 11: Flight from Lukla to Kathmandu or Manthali (Ramechhap) and Transfer to Kathmandu";s:11:"description";s:1655:"Lukla to Manthali Flight (March, April, May, September, October & November)
During the peak trekking seasons, flights from Lukla usually operate to Manthali (Ramechhap) Airport. The flight takes approximately 20 minutes, followed by a 5–6 hour drive to Kathmandu. Driving time may vary depending on road and traffic conditions. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel by a shared tourist vehicle.
Lukla to Kathmandu Flight (January, February, June, July, August & December)
During the remaining months, flights generally operate directly from Lukla to Kathmandu and take approximately 35 minutes. After landing in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel by a shared tourist vehicle. Please note that flight schedules and destinations are determined by the airlines and aviation authorities and may change depending on weather conditions and seasonal air traffic.
🚁 Helicopter Upgrade (Optional)
For added comfort and convenience, you can upgrade to a direct shared helicopter flight from Lukla to Kathmandu for an additional USD 450 per person (based on a minimum of 5 passengers sharing). This is the best option to avoid the long drive from Manthali to Kathmandu during the peak trekking seasons (March, April, May, September, October, and November).
If you have extra time in Nepal, we also offer exciting tours to Pokhara, Chitwan National Park, Kathmandu Valley, and many other destinations. We also organize outbound tours to Tibet, India, and Bhutan. In the evening, enjoy a farewell dinner at a traditional Nepali restaurant to celebrate the successful completion of your Everest adventure.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:13:"Lukla (2800m)";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:10:" Kathmandu";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:0:"";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:0:"";s:14:"important_note";s:384:"Flight operations between Lukla, Kathmandu, and Manthali are highly dependent on weather conditions, air traffic, and airline schedules. Delays, cancellations, or route changes are common in the Everest region, especially during peak trekking seasons. We recommend keeping at least one extra buffer day in your itinerary before your international departure to avoid any inconvenience.";}s:7:"item-11";a:8:{s:12:"heading-trek";s:70:"Day 12: Transfer to the International Airport for Your Final Departure";s:11:"description";s:415:"Your unforgettable Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return comes to an end today. After breakfast, one of our airport representatives will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport for your onward flight.
We sincerely thank you for choosing Ever Peak Adventures and hope you leave Nepal with unforgettable memories. We look forward to welcoming you back for another Himalayan adventure in the future.";s:23:"day_wise_gallery_images";s:0:"";s:24:"days_wise_starting_point";s:9:"Kathmandu";s:21:"day_wise_ending_point";s:32:" Tribhuvan International Airport";s:17:"day_wise_distance";s:6:"7-8 km";s:12:"daywise_hour";s:13:"30 min drive ";s:14:"important_note";s:302:"We recommend packing light, as domestic flights and helicopters have strict baggage weight limits. Please carry your essential items in a small daypack and keep your total luggage within the recommended limit. Our team will provide detailed baggage guidelines during the pre-trip briefing in Kathmandu.";}}
